recipes.title: Crispy Lemon Butter Chicken
ingredients: Bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs — 6 medium / 800 g
Ground black pepper — 1 g / ½ tsp
Unsalted butter — 45 g / 3 tbsp, cubed and kept cold
Chicken stock — 120 ml / 8 tbsp / 0.42 UK cup / ½ US cup
Finely grated lemon zest — 2 g / 1 tsp
Plain flour — a little, for dusting the chicken (from the video)
To serve (from the video): mashed potato; broccoli florets cooked with 2 tbsp water, butter, salt and pepper
steps: 1. Season the chicken thighs with salt and pepper, then pat a little flour over both sides (the flour helps crisp the skin).
2. Mash or finely chop the garlic, chop the parsley, zest the lemon and squeeze about 2 tbsp juice.

3. Heat the olive oil and a little butter in a frying pan over a steady, medium heat. Add the chicken skin side down and cook for about 10 minutes, turning now and then, until golden and cooked through. Cook in batches if the pan is crowded.
4. Turn the thighs skin side down again for a final couple of minutes of colour, then rest them in a bowl to catch the juices.
5. Pour off most of the fat, leaving about a tablespoon. Fry the garlic gently without letting it burn.
6. Add the chicken stock and simmer for about 3 minutes until reduced by about half. Stir in the lemon juice, the resting juices and the lemon zest.
7. Take the pan off the heat and stir in the cold butter a couple of cubes at a time, then the parsley, to make a runny lemon butter sauce.
8. Return the pan to a very low flame, put the chicken back in skin side up and warm for a couple of minutes. Don't spoon sauce over the skin until serving so it stays crisp.
9. Meanwhile microwave the broccoli florets with 2 tbsp water for about 3 minutes, drain, then toss with butter, salt and pepper.
10. Serve the chicken with mash and the broccoli, spooning the pan sauce over at the table.

recipes.title: Sausage and Potato Casserole with Herb Dumplings
ingredients: Thick pork sausages – (not counted aloud) [description: 8, 600–700 g]
Potatoes – cubed [description: 400 g]; optional to add in pan or tray
Celery – a couple of sticks from the fridge, diced (said in video; not on description list)
Tomato purée – a good heaped tablespoon [description: 1 tbsp]
Plain flour – a good couple of tablespoons [description: 3 tbsp]
Worcestershire sauce – about a tablespoon [description: 1 tbsp]
Beef stock – from gravy granules [description: 800 ml low-salt]
Black pepper – as you like [description: ½ tsp]; salt sparingly [to taste]
Cold butter – rubbed to breadcrumbs [description: 75 g grated]
Dried thyme – a little [description: ½ tsp]
Cold milk – enough to make a dough [description: ~120 ml gradually]
steps: Brown sausages: Oil in a tray; roast the sausages in the oven, turning, until coloured (about 20–25 minutes; finish timing overlaps veg prep).

Start the veg: Soften onion, carrot, and celery in a little oil about 6–7 minutes. Add garlic ~30 seconds. Stir in heaped tablespoon tomato purée (~1 minute), then Worcestershire, pepper, a tad of salt, and a couple of tablespoons flour; cook out. Add beef stock/gravy granules and a pinch of thyme; simmer gently while sausages finish. Potatoes can go in the pan or straight into the casserole.
Combine: Drain excess sausage fat. Put sausages and gravy-veg into a casserole. Cover with a pleated foil lid (or a real lid). Bake about 25 minutes.
Dumplings: Mix self-raising flour, salt, parsley, thyme; rub in butter; add milk to a soft dough. Shape dumplings.

Bake with dumplings: Nestle dumplings on top; re-cover with a tented foil lid; bake about 20 minutes. Remove foil and bake another 15–20 minutes until dumplings are crusty outside and fluffy inside. Serve.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qgvGrulo8bQ

recipes.title: Who Said French Cooking Was Hard? French Tacos
ingredients: 600 g chicken breast (1 lb 5 oz), cut into small strips
½ tsp ground black pepper (1 g)
200 ml double cream or heavy cream — ¾ US cup + 1 tbsp + 1 tsp; ⅔ UK cup + 2 tsp
100 g mature Cheddar, finely grated — a scant 1 US cup; ¾ UK cup
¼ tsp ground black pepper (0.5 g)
GLUE: 1-2  tbsp flour 1 tbsp water mix
steps: 1. Cook the frozen chips in the air fryer at about 215–220°C for about 20 minutes, until lightly coloured but still soft.
2. Slice the chicken breast into thin strips and toss in a bowl with the salt, pepper, oregano, paprika (smoked or sweet), cumin and garlic powder.
3. Make the burger sauce: mix the mayonnaise, ketchup and yellow mustard and set aside.
4. Heat the oil in a pan and fry the chicken in two batches until coloured and just cooked. Don't overcook the strips.
5. For the cheese sauce, warm the cream gently without boiling, add the black pepper, then melt in the grated Cheddar until pourable but thick. Take off the heat.
6. Mix 1–2 tbsp flour with 1 tbsp water to make a paste 'glue' (optional).
7. Lay out each wrap, spread burger sauce in the middle, then add chips, hot chicken and some cheese sauce, keeping the filling central.
8. Brush the flour glue on the edges, fold the sides in and the top and bottom over to make a sealed parcel.
9. Toast the parcels seam side down on a hot plate, griddle or dry frying pan until golden and marked, then turn and toast the other side.
10. Serve with extra cheese sauce. Tip: if the cheese sauce won't thicken, stir in 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with water.

recipes.title: One Pack of Mince, a Whole Pan of Dinner
ingredients: 2 medium onions, cut into chunky wedges
300 g (10½ oz) carrots, cut into thick chunks
1 kg (2 lb 3 oz) potatoes, peeled and cut into 2.5 cm (1-inch) chunks
2 tbsp chopped fresh parsley, to finish
To serve (from the video): a small cabbage, sliced, microwaved with 2 tbsp water, then butter, salt and pepper
steps: 1. Cut the carrots into rustic chunks, the onions into wedges and the potatoes into roughly 2 cm cubes.
2. Heat the oil in a large pan and add the beef mince (it can go in frozen). Season with salt and pepper and cook until the water has cooked out and the mince has a little colour.
3. Add the onion wedges and carrot chunks and cook for 6–8 minutes, turning occasionally, to start softening.
4. Add the garlic and cook for about 1 minute, then stir in the tomato purée and cook for a minute.
5. Stir in the flour (about 3 level tablespoons) and cook for about a minute.
6. Add the Worcestershire sauce, then the beef stock, scraping up the bits on the bottom of the pan. Add the bay leaf and thyme.

7. Add the potatoes, bring to a simmer, cover and cook for about 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potatoes and carrots are tender. Add a splash of water if the gravy gets too thick or starts to stick.
8. Meanwhile microwave the sliced cabbage with 2 tbsp water for 4 minutes, stir, then 4 minutes more. Stir in butter, salt and pepper, cover and let it steam for a minute.
9. Remove the bay leaf, check the seasoning, scatter over the parsley and serve with the buttered cabbage.

recipes.title: Spaghetti & Meatball Soup — Yes, I Broke It!
ingredients: 30 g dried breadcrumbs — ⅓ US cup / a generous ¼ UK cup
2 tbsp tomato purée — 30 g; concentrated tomato paste in the US
2 × 400 g tins chopped tomatoes — 800 g total
750 ml beef or chicken stock — 3⅛ US cups / 2⅔ UK cups
100 g dried spaghetti, broken into short lengths
Salt and black pepper, to taste
Fresh basil and grated Parmesan, to serve, optional
steps: 1. Dice the onion, coarsely grate the carrot and grate or mince the garlic, keeping 2 cloves for the meatballs and the rest for the soup.
2. Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for a moment, then mix with the beef mince, beaten egg, 2 grated garlic cloves, oregano, salt and pepper.
3. Roll into small meatballs (about 26–28) and set them on a tray.
4. Heat the olive oil in a large pan and fry the meatballs in batches just until coloured all over. They don't need to be cooked through. Set aside and pour off most of the oil.
5. Fry the onion, then the carrot, until lightly coloured. Add the remaining garlic for about 30 seconds.
6. Stir in the tomato purée and cook briefly, then the sugar if using.

7. Add the tomatoes (chop whole ones in the pan), oregano, a little salt and black pepper, then the stock. Simmer gently, stirring now and then. Add water or more stock if it gets too thick, as this should be a soup.
8. Blend the soup with a stick blender, as smooth or chunky as you like.
9. Return the meatballs and simmer for at least 5 minutes.
10. Break the spaghetti into short lengths, stir it in and simmer for about 10–12 minutes until tender, stirring so it doesn't stick.
11. In the last minute, stir through torn basil and a little Parmesan. Serve topped with more Parmesan and basil.

recipes.title: The first dish I make every winter!
ingredients: Chicken thighs, bone-in skin-on – [description: 6 medium]; flour, salt, and pepper for coating
Cannellini beans (or haricot) – tinned, drained; mash some to thicken [description: 4 × 400 g tins, 960 g drained]
Olive oil – for tray and frying [description: 1 tbsp]
Black pepper – [description: ½ tsp]; salt to taste
Oven: 180°C (fan notes on site may differ):
steps: Season chicken: Salt and pepper (one side is enough if keeping it simple), dust with flour so the skin crisps.
Oven-start sausage and bacon: Oil a tray; add sausages and chopped smoked bacon. Roast about 20 minutes until sausages plump and bacon cooks.
Prep veg and beans: Dice onion and carrot small; mash some of the drained beans to thicken the sauce later.
Colour the chicken: Fry in oil about 6–8 minutes for a golden crust (not cooked through). Set aside.
Build the base: Soften onion and carrot in the pan; add garlic, tomato purée, thyme, bay, stock, beans (mashed + whole), and optional mushrooms.

Assemble and bake: Combine with sausages, bacon, and chicken in a wide shallow casserole (single layer for chicken). Bake until the chicken is done and the sauce is rich — site timing: about 25–30 minutes in a hot oven after assembly (check notes: cook until chicken reaches 75°C / 165°F). Serve with crusty bread or mash.

recipes.title: REAL UK HOT DOGS! — We Batter Ours!
ingredients: 150 g self-raising flour — 1¼ US cups / 1 UK cup + 1 tbsp, plus extra for dusting
¼ tsp food-grade citric acid — 1 g
¼ tsp fine salt — 1.5 g, plus extra for serving
200 ml water — 13⅓ tbsp / 0.85 US cup / 0.70 UK cup
Rice flour, for coating the sausages before battering (used in the video)
Butter, for the rolls (from the video)
steps: 1. Put the sausages in an oven tray with a little oil and cook at 190°C for about 20 minutes, turning halfway, until browned and cooked through.
2. Let the sausages cool for 7–8 minutes, pat off the fat with kitchen paper, then coat them in rice flour so the batter will stick.
3. Make the batter: whisk the self-raising flour (about 150 g), salt and warm water into a smooth batter. Don't add the citric acid yet.
4. Heat the oil for deep-frying to 175–180°C, filling the pan only about one third full. Set a rack over kitchen paper on a tray.
5. About a minute before frying, whisk the citric acid into the batter. It fizzes and makes the batter lighter and crispier, so don't mix it in ahead of time.
6. Dip the sausages in the batter and fry a few at a time until crisp and golden, patching any bare spots with extra batter. Fry a few drips of batter for 'scraps'.
7. Drain on the rack and let them rest for a minute.
8. Split and butter the rolls, add some scraps and a battered sausage, then season with malt vinegar, salt and ketchup. Serve with mushy peas.

recipes.title: Creamy Shredded Chicken Curry – Chicken Bharta
ingredients: Cooked rotisserie chicken, skin and bones removed – 600 g, coarsely shredded
Full-fat plain yoghurt, beaten – 100 g / 6 tbsp + 2 tsp
Double cream or heavy cream – 60 ml / 4 tbsp / ¼ US cup / 0.21 UK cup
Water for the gravy – 120 ml / 8 tbsp / ½ US cup / 0.42 UK cup
Hard-boiled eggs – 2, one chopped and one quartered
Hot water for soaking – 120 ml; discard after soaking
Fresh water for blending – 45 ml / 3 tbsp
Fine salt – ½ tsp / 3 g, then adjust to taste
Chicken stock — 1 chicken stock cube dissolved in water, or plain water (used in the video for the gravy)
Black pepper — a little (added in the video; not in the description)
steps: 1. Shred the cooked chicken. Blend the tomatoes to a purée (or finely chop them).
2. Soak the cashews in hot water, drain, then blend with about 3 tbsp fresh water to a thick paste. Hard-boil the eggs.
3. Finely chop the onions, green chillies and coriander.
4. Heat the oil and butter (or ghee) in a pan, add the cumin seeds, bay leaf, cardamom and cinnamon, then the onion. Cook for 6–8 minutes, or up to 10–12, until golden.
5. Add the garlic and ginger paste and the green chilli and cook for about a minute.
6. Lower the heat and add the ground coriander, cumin, Kashmiri chilli, salt, turmeric and a little black pepper. Stir for a minute to bloom the spices.
7. Add the tomato, raise the heat and cook for about 8 minutes into a thick paste until the raw tomato smell has gone and oil starts to separate. Add a spoonful of stock if it catches.
8. Turn the heat low and stir in the cashew paste a spoonful at a time, letting it cook for a minute.
9. Stir in the remaining stock or water, then remove the bay leaf, cinnamon and cardamom if you like.
10. Add the shredded chicken, then the cream. Stir in one chopped boiled egg and heat gently for 5–7 minutes until the chicken is hot through, adding water if it gets too thick.
11. Turn off the heat and stir in the coriander, kasuri methi and garam masala. Serve topped with the quartered egg.

recipes.title: Chicken Coq au Vin Without the Long Wait
ingredients: Plain flour, for dusting — 2 tbsp / 16 g
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 medium red onion or 3 shallots, finely diced — 150 g
Dry red wine — 500 ml / 2 US cups / 1¾ UK cups
Chicken stock — 300 ml / 1¼ US cups / 1 UK cup + 1 tbsp
Bouquet garni — 3 thyme sprigs, 1 bay leaf and a few parsley stalks, tied together
Jarred pickled silverskin onions, drained weight — 200 g / 1¼ US cups or 1 UK cup
Button mushrooms, left whole if small or halved — 250 g
steps: 1. Season the chicken breasts with salt and pepper, dust with flour on both sides and leave skin side up for about 5 minutes while you prep the veg.
2. Tie the thyme, bay leaf and parsley stalks into a bouquet garni. Drain the pickled silverskin onions, soak them in water for a while to remove some vinegar, then drain and pat dry.
3. Finely dice the onion, carrot and celery, chop 3 garlic cloves and thinly slice the other 2. Halve any large mushrooms.

4. Heat the oven to 200°C. Heat a splash of olive oil in a pan over medium-high heat and fry the chicken skin side down for about 4–5 minutes until golden, then a couple of minutes on the other side. Rest on a tray.
5. Fry the bacon lardons in the same pan until browned, then lift them out.
6. Add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 5–6 minutes to soften. Add the chopped garlic for about 30 seconds.
7. Lower the heat a little and stir in the tomato purée for about a minute, then 1 tbsp flour for about a minute.
8. Pour in the red wine gradually, add the bouquet garni and simmer until reduced by about half.
9. Add the chicken stock and simmer for about 15 minutes until reduced by half and the sauce coats the back of a spoon.
10. Meanwhile roast the chicken in the oven for about 15 minutes until cooked through, then rest.
11. In another pan, fry the silverskin onions in a little olive oil over moderate heat, then add some butter and the sliced garlic for about a minute. Lift out.
12. Fry the mushrooms until coloured, add the remaining butter, then return the bacon, onions and garlic. Take off the heat and stir in the parsley.
13. Strain the sauce to remove the veg and herbs.
14. Slice the chicken thickly and serve on mashed potato with the bacon, onion and mushroom garnish and the red wine sauce.

recipes.title: Samosa Style Loaded Baked Potatoes
ingredients: Onion, finely chopped — 150 g / ⅝ UK cup / ¾ US cup
Frozen peas, thawed — 100 g / ½ UK cup / ⅔ US cup
Fresh ginger, finely grated — 1 tbsp / 6 g
Fine salt — ¾ tsp / 4.5 g, plus extra for the skins
Plain yoghurt — 120 g / 8 tbsp / 0.42 UK cup / ½ US cup
Fresh mint, finely chopped — 1 tbsp / 3 g
Tamarind chutney — 4 tbsp / 60 ml / 0.21 UK cup / ¼ US cup
Water — 150 ml (10 tbsp / 30 tsp / 0.53 UK cup / 0.63 US cup)
Soft brown sugar — 60 g (5 packed tbsp / ¼ UK cup / ⅓ US cup)
Salt or black salt — ¼ tsp
Cornflour (cornstarch) — a little, mixed with water to thicken the chutney (used in the video)
steps: 1. Wash the potatoes, prick them all over, score a line around each one and microwave in a covered container on high for about 12–14 minutes until tender. Heat the oven to about 220°C.
2. Heat the ghee in a pan, add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle, then fry the onion until lightly golden.
3. Turn down the heat and add the ginger and green chillies, then the ground coriander and turmeric. Stir to bloom the spices.
4. Add the peas and cook for just a couple of minutes. Take off the heat.
5. Brush the potato skins with ghee, rub with salt and bake for about 15 minutes to crisp the skins.
6. For the mint yoghurt, mix the yoghurt with the mint, lemon juice and salt, then chill.

7. For the tamarind chutney, simmer the tamarind paste, water, brown sugar, cumin, ginger, chilli powder and salt until the sugar dissolves. Thicken with a little cornflour slurry. Add water if it gets too thick, as it should be runny.
8. Stir the fresh coriander, garam masala and lemon juice into the pea filling.
9. Microwave the poppadoms for about 30–40 seconds until puffed, then crush them roughly.
10. When the potatoes are cool enough to handle, scoop out the flesh, mix it with the filling (mashed or chunky), taste for salt and pile it back into the skins.
11. Brush the tops with melted ghee and bake for 20–25 minutes until crisp.
12. Serve topped with mint yoghurt, tamarind chutney and crushed poppadoms.

recipes.title: Old Fashioned Blackberry Jam Roly Poly
ingredients: Self-raising flour — 2 cups / 250 g, plus extra for dusting
Shredded beef or vegetable suet — 1 cup / 125 g
Milk — 10 tbsp / 150 ml, adding only as needed
Thick blackberry jam — ⅔ cup / 200 g
Softened butter — 1 tsp / 5 g, for greasing the baking paper
For the crust (from the video): a little extra butter for brushing and a sprinkling of sugar
Water — boiling, a couple of centimetres in a tray for steaming
steps: 1. Mix the self-raising flour, salt and sugar in a bowl, then stir in the suet (grate it from frozen if it's soft).
2. Add the milk gradually and mix to a soft, slightly sticky dough.
3. Lay a sheet of parchment over a sheet of foil and brush the parchment with butter.
4. Stir the jam with a spoon until spreadable. Don't warm it.
5. On a floured surface, roll the dough to a rectangle of about 25 × 30 cm, keeping an even thickness.
6. Spread the jam over the dough, leaving a border. Brush water along the edges to seal.
7. Roll up loosely from the short side and place seam side down on the buttered parchment. Wrap loosely in the parchment and foil, leaving room to expand.
8. Put a tray on the lowest shelf of the oven with a couple of centimetres of boiling water to make steam. Bake the roly poly on the shelf above at about 180–200°C for about 45 minutes.
9. Open the parcel, brush the top with butter, sprinkle with sugar and bake for another 10 minutes for a crusty top.
10. Rest for 10 minutes, then slice and serve with warm custard.

recipes.title: Crispy Chicken Rissoles with Diane Sauce
ingredients: Onion — ½ medium / 75 g, finely grated and excess juice squeezed out
Garlic — 2 cloves / 2 tsp / 6 g, finely grated
Ground black pepper — ½ tsp / 1 g
Plain flour — ¼ cup / 4 tbsp / 35 g
Neutral oil — 7–10 tbsp / 105–150 ml, for shallow frying
Onion — ½ medium / 75 g, finely chopped
Garlic — 2 cloves / 2 tsp / 6 g, finely chopped
Tomato purée / concentrated tomato paste — 1 tsp / 5 g
Ground black pepper — ¼ tsp / 0.5 g
steps: 1. Halve the onion: grate one half for the rissoles and squeeze out the excess juice, and finely chop the other half for the sauce. Split the garlic between the rissoles and the sauce. Thickly slice the mushrooms.
2. Mix the chicken mince with the grated onion, garlic, beaten egg, Dijon, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, salt, pepper and panko. Add more panko if the mix is too wet. Rest for 10 minutes.
3. Divide into 8, shape into patties on a parchment-lined tray and chill for about 30 minutes.
4. For the sauce, heat a pan with just a smear of butter and fry the mushrooms without seasoning until deeply browned.
5. Lower the heat, add the rest of the butter and the chopped onion and soften for about 3 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
6. Stir in the tomato purée for about a minute. Off the heat, add the brandy (optional) and cook it out.
7. Add the stock, Worcestershire sauce, Dijon (about 2 tsp) and black pepper, then the cream. Simmer for a few minutes, season and keep warm. Add the parsley before serving.
8. Set up a flour, egg-and-water and panko station. Coat each rissole in flour, then egg, then panko, and set on a rack.

9. Heat the oil for shallow frying over moderate heat (not too hot) and fry the rissoles for about 3–5 minutes, turning a couple of times, until golden and cooked through. Fry in batches and drain on a rack.
10. Serve the rissoles with the Diane sauce and sides such as peas or mash.

recipes.title: Creamy Bacon & Pea Barley Risotto
ingredients: 300g pearl barley — , rinsed and drained  1½ US cups / 1¼ UK imperial cups
200g smoked streaky bacon, cut into small pieces
200g frozen peas — 1½ US cups / 1¼ UK imperial cups
40g finely grated Parmesan — ½ US cup / just under ½ UK imperial cup, loosely filled
100ml dry white wine, or extra stock
1,300ml hot chicken or vegetable stock, preferably low salt—you may not need it all
steps: 1. Rinse the pearl barley. Dice the onion and chop the garlic.

8. Stir in the bacon and frozen peas for a couple of minutes, then turn off the heat.

10. Serve topped with the reserved crispy bacon, with crusty bread or buttered toast.

ingredients: 350g small seedless black or red grapes — 2⅓ US cups / 1⅞ UK imperial cups
175g caster sugar — ⅞ US cup / ¾ UK imperial cup
3 large eggs, at room temperature - 150g without shells
250g plain flour — 2 US cups / 1⅔ UK imperial cups

steps: 1. Heat the oven to 180°C and line the base of an 8-inch (20 cm) cake tin. A 9-inch tin also works.

3. Beat the softened butter and caster sugar for about 3–4 minutes until light and fluffy.

recipes.title: One Cabbage, Golden Potatoes, Proper Curry
ingredients: 1 white cabbage, cored and cut into broad strips — 1 kg prepared

recipes.title: Crispy Chip Shop Tuna Scallop Burger
ingredients: 1 or 2 very large floury potato, about 600 g / 21 oz
2 tbsp mayonnaise — 30 g / 1 UK fl oz / 1 US fl oz

¾ US cup water — 180 ml / 12 tbsp / ⅔ UK cup
4 tbsp mayonnaise — 60 g / ¼ US cup / 0.21 UK cup

steps: 1. Make the dressing: mix the ketchup, mayonnaise, Worcestershire sauce, black pepper, mustard, 2 tbsp chopped pickles and the pickle liquor. Chill.
2. Make the filling: mix the drained tuna with the chopped onion, 2 tbsp chopped pickles, black pepper and mayonnaise. Add mustard if you like. Salt is usually not needed.
3. Cut the potatoes into thick slices (two per burger), cover with water, bring to the boil and cook for about 6–8 minutes until just starting to soften but not crumbling.
4. Cool the slices in cold water, drain and pat dry with kitchen paper.
5. Dust a tray with rice flour. Sandwich some tuna mix between two potato slices, press firmly and dust with rice flour. Chill for about 30 minutes to firm up.
6. Make the batter: mix the plain flour, rice flour, baking powder, salt, a little turmeric and pepper, then whisk in the water to a thickish batter. Leave out the citric acid for now.
7. Heat the frying oil to about 180°C. Just before frying, whisk in the citric acid. It fizzes and makes the batter lighter.
8. Dip each scallop in the batter and deep-fry until crisp and golden, frying a few drips of batter for scraps.
9. Toast the burger buns, spread with the dressing, add a scallop and some more dressing, then serve.

steps: Bake: We're just going to chuck it on and throw it in the oven. We're going to give that a mix. We're going to chuck that all over those ribs. And then we're going to throw some oil on and we're going to throw them in this tray.
Bake: And we're going to cook it in the oven for about an hour and 20 minutes at 160°. We're just going to hit that up with a little bit of oil. And stick it in the oven.

recipes.title: A Rich Bolognese ..You Can Afford

recipes.title: Fajita Wraps on a Budget...You Can Afford
ingredients: 150 g dry, large flat TVP pieces
400 ml hot water — about 1⅗ UK cups or 1⅔ US cups
1½ tbsp of your prepared fajita seasoning to start, about 14–17 g; add up to ½ tbsp more after tasting
Optional: salsa, sour cream and grated cheese
Black pepper — a little, added to the soaking liquid (from the video)
Lard or beef fat — optional alternative to the oil for frying (from the video)
steps: 1. Dissolve the Bovril, mushroom powder and a little black pepper in the hot water. Add the TVP pieces and soak for 20–30 minutes, turning them over often.
2. Slice the peppers and onion and separate the onion into segments.
3. After about 15 minutes, slice the TVP into strips and return them to the liquid. Keep turning for another 5–10 minutes until all the liquid is absorbed.
4. Sear the TVP strips in a hot dry pan until charred on the outside.
5. Cool briefly, then toss with 1–2 tsp cornflour (no more than about 2 tsp).
6. Heat the oil in the pan and fry the TVP in batches until crispy and charred. Set aside.
7. Add a little more oil and stir-fry the peppers and onion for about 4–6 minutes until lightly charred.
8. Add the fajita seasoning, return the TVP and add about 2–3 tbsp water to make a glossy coating.
9. Turn off the heat and stir in the lime juice.
10. Fill the warm tortillas with salsa, sour cream and cheese if you like, then roll burrito style and cut in half.

A pinch of MSG, optional (about ⅛ tsp)
A pinch of white pepper (about ⅛ tsp)

King Prawns with Chilli Bean Sauce:
400 g (14 oz) raw king prawns, peeled and deveined

steps: 1. Taste the black bean garlic and chilli bean sauces first, as both are very salty. Use them sparingly, about a teaspoon if unsure.
2. Beef: heat a wide wok until very hot, add a little oil, lower the flame and stir-fry the thinly sliced beef until browned. Remove to a bowl.
3. Add a little more oil and stir-fry the diced onion, green pepper and chilli, then the grated ginger.
4. Return the beef and add the black bean garlic sauce, the water, dark soy, oyster sauce, sugar, white pepper, Shaoxing wine and a few drops of sesame oil (plus MSG if using). Stir to coat.
5. If needed, thicken with the potato starch mixed with cold water. Turn off the heat and serve.

9. Turn off the heat and serve both dishes with rice to balance the salt and heat.

ingredients: 700 g green or Savoy cabbage, cut into thick ribbons

150g mushrooms, chopped into tiny granules — 1¾ UK cups / 2 US cups

steps: 1. Dissolve the Bovril in the boiling water, stir in the TVP and leave for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.
2. Chop the mushrooms very finely, dice the onion and celery, grate the carrot and chop the garlic.
3. Boil the red lentils for 8 minutes, then drain.
4. Heat the lard, dripping or oil in a large pan and fry the TVP for about 6–8 minutes, leaving it to catch some brown edges.
5. Add the mushrooms, then a little more fat with the onion, carrot and celery, and cook for about 5–6 minutes to soften. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
6. Stir in 3 tbsp tomato purée and cook it out briefly.

7. Add the red wine (optional), the tinned tomatoes, dark soy, Worcestershire sauce, water, oregano, thyme and bay leaves, then the smoked paprika, black pepper and MSG if using. Add salt only after tasting.

recipes.title: Sausage Rolls...You Can Afford
ingredients: This makes enough filling for approximately 16 substantial sausage rolls.
100g dry fine TVP — ¾ UK cup / 1 US cup
180ml boiling water -  ⅔ UK cup / ¾ US cup
½–1 tsp pork or chicken stock powder, depending on saltiness —  2–4g
50g dry red lentils — ¼ UK cup / ¼ US cup
100g onion, extremely finely diced — ½ UK cup / ⅔ US cup
75g button mushrooms, chopped into tiny granules —  ¾ UK cup / 1 US cup
40g softened lard for the filling — 3 tbsp
40g fine breadcrumbs — ⅓ UK cup / ⅖ US cup
Salt only after cooking a test piece
Ready-rolled puff pastry (used in the video)
Beaten egg, for sealing and glazing (from the video)
steps: 1. Blitz some of the TVP finely so the texture is more like sausage meat, then mix it with the rest.

2. Dissolve the pork or chicken stock powder in the boiling water and stir in the gelatine (optional) until it dissolves. Pour over the TVP and leave for 10 minutes, stirring now and then. Don't add salt if the stock is salty.
3. Chop the mushrooms into tiny granules and dice the onion extremely finely.
4. Boil the rinsed red lentils for 6–8 minutes, drain without rinsing and mash lightly.
5. Heat a little lard and gently cook the onion (and mushrooms) for about 4–5 minutes until soft and golden. Spread on a tray to cool.
6. Add 1 tbsp lard to the pan and cook the TVP over a very low flame for just 3–4 minutes without browning. Cool.
7. Mix the sausage seasoning: sage, thyme, onion powder, mustard powder, white pepper, mace, nutmeg, black pepper, sugar and MSG (optional).
8. Combine the onion and lentils with the TVP, seasoning, breadcrumbs and wheat gluten. Add the egg, Worcestershire sauce and softened lard, and work by hand for about 2 minutes until tacky.
9. Chill for about 1 hour so the breadcrumbs rehydrate. Fry a test piece and add salt only if needed.
10. Heat the oven to about 190–200°C. Roll the filling into sausage shapes, lay on puff pastry, brush the edge with beaten egg, roll over and seal. Cut to size.
11. Brush with beaten egg and cut vent holes in the top.
12. Bake on a lower-middle shelf for about 25–32 minutes until golden. Rest for 5 minutes, then cool on a rack.

recipes.title: How to Make Mince Go Further...You Can Afford
ingredients: 75 g dry TVP granules — approximately ¾ US cup or ⅔ UK cup

steps: 1. Dissolve the Bovril (a good ¾–1 tsp) and the Worcestershire sauce in the hot water. Pour over the TVP and leave to rehydrate for 10 minutes, stirring now and then.

recipes.title: Mince and Onion Pie You Can Afford
ingredients: Makes one 23 cm/9-inch deep pie, serving 6.
125 g dried split red lentils — ⅔ US cup / ½ UK cup
60 g dry TVP or textured soy mince — 1 US cup / ¾ UK cup
150 ml hot strong beef stock —  ⅔ US cup / ½ UK cup
250 g mushrooms, extremely finely chopped —  3 US cups / 2½ UK cups
300 g onions, finely diced — 2 US cups / 1⅔ UK cups
15 g butter, lard or dripping — 1 tbsp
400 ml strong beef stock — 1⅔ US cups / 1⅖ UK cups

½ tsp gravy browning, optional — 2.5 ml
Ready-made shortcrust pastry — enough for a base and lid (ready-rolled works)
Beaten egg — optional, for egg wash (from the video)
steps: 1. Boil the rinsed red lentils for about 8 minutes, drain and spread on a tray to steam dry.
2. Pour the hot strong beef stock over the TVP and leave for 10 minutes, stirring so it all absorbs the flavour.
3. Put the finely chopped mushrooms into a dry pan and cook for about 8–10 minutes to drive off the moisture and brown slightly.
4. Add the oil and butter, lard or dripping, then the onions, and cook for about 8 minutes. Add the garlic for 30 seconds.
5. Add the TVP, leave it for 4–5 minutes without stirring to crust up, then stir and repeat until browned.
6. Stir in the tomato purée and cook until it darkens, then the flour to cook out its rawness.
7. Add the thyme, black pepper, garlic powder, onion powder and MSG, then the 400 ml beef stock, Worcestershire sauce, balsamic vinegar, dark soy sauce, and Marmite and gravy browning if using.
8. Cook until thick, stir in the lentils and add a little water only if it's too thick. It should be a thick gravy. Cool slightly.
9. Heat the oven to 200°C with a tray inside. Line a 23 cm (9 inch) deep pie tin with pastry, add the filling and top with a pastry lid. Crimp the edges and trim.
10. Brush with egg wash if you like and cut a couple of vent holes.
11. Bake on the hot tray for about 40–45 minutes, covering with foil if the top browns too quickly. Rest for about 10 minutes before cutting.

ingredients: Dijon or English mustard — 1 tsp / 5 g

recipes.title: Satay Chicken Meatballs
ingredients: Finely grated fresh ginger: 5 g / 1½ tsp
Coconut milk: 500 ml / approximately 250ml each divided
Smooth peanut butter: 100 g / approximately 6½ tbsp
Thai red curry paste: 15 g / 1 tbsp
Brown sugar or honey: 15 g / 1 tbsp
Fresh lime juice: 30 ml / 2 tbsp / 6 tsp / ⅛ US cup / 0.11 UK cup
Chopped roasted peanuts: 20 g / approximately 2 tbsp
Chopped coriander or spring onion: 8 g / approximately 4 tbsp
Tagliatelle, noodles or rice — to serve (the video uses tagliatelle)
Lime wedges — to serve (from the video)
steps: 1. Cook the tagliatelle or noodles in salted boiling water as per the packet, then drain (or cook rice).
2. Scoop the thick coconut cream from the top of the coconut milk, using about 3 tbsp in the meatballs and the rest for the sauce.
3. Mix the chicken mince with the panko, 3 tbsp coconut cream, egg, garlic, ginger, soy sauce and a splash of oil until tacky. Add more panko if it's too wet.
4. With oiled or wet hands, shape into about 12–18 meatballs.
5. Fry the meatballs gently in the oil, turning, until crusted and about 80–90% cooked. Set aside and discard the pan oil.
6. Heat the coconut cream in a clean pan until it splits and the oil separates.
7. Fry the red curry paste in the split cream, then stir in the remaining coconut milk.
8. Add the brown sugar, soy sauce and lime juice, then stir in the peanut butter to make a thick satay sauce. Thin with water if needed.
9. Toss the noodles in the sauce, return the meatballs and simmer gently for a couple of minutes until cooked through and coated.
10. Garnish with chopped roasted peanuts, spring onion or coriander, and lime wedges.

8. Remove the foil and bake for another 20–25 minutes until crusty on top.
9. Let it cool slightly before serving. It's good topped with a fried egg and black pepper.

recipes.title: I Stuffed 3 Whole Cabbages with Beef
ingredients: 100 g finely chopped cabbage removed from the centres — approx ¾ UK cup or 1 US cup
1 small onion, finely chopped — approx 100 g
75 g cooked rice — approx ⅓ UK cup or ½ US cup
25 g breadcrumbs — approx ¼ UK cup or ⅓ US cup
1 tsp UK/US dried oregano or mixed herbs
Butter — a little, for frying the onion and cabbage (from the video)
steps: 1. Boil the whole cabbages in salted water, covered, for 8–10 minutes to soften, then drain and cool in cold water until you can handle them.
2. Blend the tomato sauce: tomatoes or passata with the tomato purée, sugar, black pepper, salt and oregano. Mix in the stock to make about 500 ml or more of sauce.
3. Cut a cone out of the centre of each cabbage, angling towards the core. Squeeze out the absorbed water by turning them upside down and pressing gently.
4. Finely chop about 100 g of the removed cabbage. Finely chop the onion and mince the garlic.
5. Fry the onion in the oil and a little butter, add the chopped cabbage for about 5–7 minutes, then the garlic for about a minute. Cool.
6. Mix the beef mince with the cooked rice, breadcrumbs, Worcestershire sauce, black pepper, salt, paprika, oregano and egg, then stir in the cooled cabbage mixture.
7. Heat the oven to 190°C. Pour some sauce into a baking dish, sit the cabbages in it and pack the filling into the centres. Pour the rest of the sauce around so it comes about halfway up.
8. Put the dish on a tray, cover tightly with foil and bake for about 1 hour 10–15 minutes. The filling should reach 71°C (160°F).
9. Uncover and bake for another 15–25 minutes to colour the tops and reduce the juices.
10. Halve and serve with the tomato sauce and mashed potato.

recipes.title: Do you remember Tender BEEF Liver with BACON and Onions
ingredients: 500 g beef liver, sliced into 1 cm strips
300 g onions, thinly sliced — approx 1¼ UK cups / 1½ US cups
60 g plain flour — approx / 4 tbsp / ½ UK cup / ½ US cup
10 g English or Dijon mustard — 2 tsp / ⅔ tbsp
500 ml beef stock  -  2 UK cups / 2⅛ US cups
2 g dried thyme — 1 tsp / ⅓ tbsp
To serve (from the video): mashed potatoes
steps: 1. Thinly slice the onions and chop the bacon. Cut the liver into 1 cm strips.
2. Cover the liver with the milk and soak for about an hour, then drain, rinse and pat dry with kitchen paper.
3. Fry the bacon in a hot pan until crisp.
4. Add the onions to the bacon fat with the butter and the brown sugar (optional) and cook for 10–12 minutes until soft and caramelised. Lift out the bacon and onions.
5. Season the flour with the salt and pepper and toss the dry liver in it, shaking off the excess.
6. Heat the oil and a little butter in a hot pan and sear the liver in batches for about 60 seconds per side until golden. Set aside.
7. Lower the heat, stir a little of the seasoned flour into the pan and cook for about a minute.
8. Add the beef stock, Worcestershire sauce, thyme and mustard and simmer gently into a gravy. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
9. Return the bacon and onions, then the liver and any juices. Warm through for just a couple of minutes, as overcooking toughens the liver. It should still be a little pink.
10. Serve over mashed potatoes.

recipes.title: Put The OOH In Batter
ingredients: 150 g plain flour — approximately 1 UK cup or 1¼ US cups
⅛ tsp citric acid — approximately 0.5 g
200–225 ml room-temperature water — approximately ¾–⅞ UK cup or ¾ cup plus 2½ tbsp–1 US cup
Plain flour — a little extra, for dusting what you're battering (from the video)
To batter (as in the video): onion rings, fish fillets or a burger
steps: 1. Prepare what you're battering, e.g. slice a red onion into rings, and dust it lightly with plain flour so the batter sticks. Don't season the onion rings, or they will sweat.
2. Mix the plain flour, baking powder and salt (or use self-raising flour and salt).
3. Whisk in the room-temperature water (about 26–28°C) to make a smooth batter.
4. Heat the oil to 180°C. The oil must be ready before the last step.
5. When the oil is hot, whisk the ⅛ tsp citric acid into the batter. It reacts with the baking powder and makes CO₂ instantly for a light, crisp coating. Too much citric acid will make it sour.
6. Dip the floured items in the batter and fry straight away, turning, until golden and crisp.
7. Drain on a rack over a tray and serve.

recipes.title: This Butter Chicken Changes Everything
ingredients: Chicken breast, cut into large chunks — 800g
Greek yoghurt — 6 tbsp | 90g | 0.38 UK cup | 0.36 US cup
Optional: orange-red food colouring, a tiny amount
Tomato passata (or a tin of tomatoes, blended) — 400ml | 400g | 2 UK cups | 2.1 US cups
Chicken stock — 250ml | 1 UK cup | 1.06 US cups
Whole cashews — 20g | 2 tbsp | scant ¼ UK cup | scant ¼ US cup
Coconut milk powder — 30g | 3 tbsp | ⅓ UK cup | ⅓ US cup
Double cream — 150ml | 10 tbsp | 0.63 UK cup | 0.63 US cup
steps: Cut the chicken: Cut the skinless, boneless chicken breasts into big chunks. Keep them big because they bake in the oven and small pieces dry out.

Marinate overnight: Mix about 6 tbsp yoghurt, about 3 tbsp garlic-ginger paste, 2 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, turmeric, ground coriander, ground cumin, garam masala, salt and lemon juice. If you like, add a tiny amount of orange-red food colouring. Coat the chicken, tip it and all the marinade into a zip-lock bag and seal it. Double-bag it in case it leaks as the chicken releases moisture. Refrigerate overnight.
Preheat: Heat the oven high, to about 220°C.
Skewer: Thread the chicken onto skewers and keep any leftover marinade.

Onions in the tray: Put a couple of spoonfuls of ghee and a tablespoon or two of butter in a roasting tray. Add the 3 chopped red onions and toss to coat. Lay the skewers across the top of the tray so the chicken juices drip onto the onions.

Roast, first stage: Roast for about 20 minutes. Take the skewers off. Stir a little garlic-ginger paste and the cashews into the onions; the cashews soften in the juices. Turn the skewers over, put them back on the tray and roast for about another 10 minutes (25–30 minutes in total).
Rest the chicken: Move the skewers to a plate or tray, cover with foil and let them rest.
Reduce the liquid: If there is a lot of liquid from the chicken in the tray, return the tray to the oven for about 10 minutes to cook it off.

Build the sauce: Stir the spices into the tray; they cook in rather than bloom. Stir in a couple of good tablespoons of tomato paste. Add the kasuri methi, chicken stock and passata. Blend briefly with a stick blender, partly not completely. Stir in the almond flour and coconut milk powder.
Roast, second stage: Return the tray to the oven for about 15 minutes so the flavours come together. Stir in the browned bits from the edges.
Finish the sauce: Stir in a couple of tablespoons of butter, the cream, a little pinch of methi, a little honey (or sugar) and about ½ tsp garam masala.
Chicken back in: Slide the chicken off the skewers into the sauce, stir, and return the tray to the oven for 10–12 minutes to heat the chicken through.
Serve: Drizzle with a little ghee or melted butter if you like. Coriander is optional; it is usually served without.

recipes.title: You’ve Never Had Coconut Chicken Like This
ingredients: Chicken pieces (bone-in or boneless) — 1 kg | 35 oz
Lemon juice — 2 tbsp | 30 ml | ⅛ UK cup | ⅛ US cup
Oil (for grilling or searing) — 2 tbsp | 30 ml | ⅛ UK cup | ⅛ US cup
Coconut oil (or any oil) — 2 tbsp | 30 ml | ⅛ UK cup | ⅛ US cup
Onion, finely chopped — 1 large (200 g | 1½ UK cups | 1½ US cups)
Mild chilli powder or paprika — 1 tsp | 2 g
Fresh tomatoes, chopped or canned — 250 g | 1¼ UK cups | 1¼ US cups
Coconut milk — 400 ml | 1⅔ UK cups | 1¾ US cups
Water (as needed) — 60 ml | ¼ UK cup | ¼ US cup
steps: Marinate: Toss the chicken with about 2 tbsp lemon juice, enough salt to coat it, and black pepper. That's the whole marinade, with no garlic or ginger. Leave it for at least 30 minutes, or overnight (the video used 40 minutes).

Char the chicken: Heat a griddle pan with a little coconut oil (or any oil). It doesn't need to be screaming hot. Lay in the chicken and leave it alone for a few minutes until charred. Turn it and colour the other side. Turn off the heat and set the chicken aside with its juices. It finishes cooking in the sauce. (For a barbecue-smoke flavour, you can grill it over charcoal instead.)
Soften the onions: Heat a little coconut oil in a pan. Add the onion and a little salt to draw out the moisture. Cook for 6–8 minutes until lightly golden. Don't rush this.
Garlic and ginger: Clear a space in the pan, add the garlic-ginger paste and cook it briefly.
Bloom the spices: Turn the heat down. Add the turmeric, cumin, coriander and mild chilli powder (or paprika). Stir steadily for a short while so the spices bloom without burning.

Tomatoes: Add the tomatoes and turn the heat up a little. Cook them down to a jammy consistency, adding a splash of water if anything catches. Take your time: it's ready when the tomatoes have broken down and the oil starts to separate at the edges. Scrape up anything stuck to the bottom.
Coconut milk: Pour the coconut milk in around the side of the pan and stir it through. This is not cooked down to split the oil. Bring it back up to a proper simmer.

Simmer the chicken: Add the charred chicken and its juices. Turn the heat down and simmer uncovered for about 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the chicken is cooked through. The sauce thickens a little but stays loose and juicy.
Season: Taste and add more salt and pepper if needed. Simmer for a couple more minutes.
Finish and rest: Turn off the heat, stir in a small handful of chopped coriander and let it rest for 5 minutes.
Serve: With potatoes, roti or rice. It's a mild, creamy, tomato-and-coconut curry. Bone-in thighs give the most tender result.

recipes.title: Chicken Jalfrezi  - Thick Masala, Not Dry!
ingredients: Chicken (boneless thigh preferred), large chunks – 700 g
Oil (mustard oil ideal, or veg oil) – 3 tbsp | 45 ml
Red chilli powder (optional heat) – ½ tsp
Water or chicken stock – 120 ml | 8 tbsp | ½ UK cup | ½ US cup
steps: Prep the veg: Smash/crack the green chillies (no need to slice). Finely dice some onion for the base. Cut the rest of the onion into large segments and separate the layers. Scoop the seeds and pulp out of the tomatoes and keep them in one bowl. Cut the tomato flesh into pieces and put it in another bowl. Cut the peppers into chunks to match the onion.
Prep the chicken: Remove the skin, check for bones, trim off gristle and cut into good-size chunks.

Marinate: Mix the chicken with about 1 tsp Kashmiri chilli powder, a little turmeric, salt, oil, garlic-ginger paste and a squeeze of lemon. Mix, then stir in the yoghurt. Marinate for 30 minutes, or overnight if you prefer.

Heat the oil: Heat about 3 tbsp mustard oil in a pan until it just starts to smoke, then turn the heat down. This burns off the raw mustard smell. (Any oil works. If you use another oil, skip the smoking step.)
Sear the chicken: Add the marinated chicken and fry until it has good colour and is about 80% cooked. Remove it to a bowl and keep the juices. It will keep cooking as it rests.
Temper: Add the cumin seeds and 2 dried red chillies to the same pan and let them sizzle.
Base: Add the finely diced onion and cook it round. Add the tomato pulp/seeds and cook until soft and quite mushy.
Spices: Over a low-to-moderate flame (not high), add 2 tsp ground coriander, a little cumin and a little red chilli powder. Stir briefly so the spices bloom without burning.
Tomato paste: Add a couple of tablespoons of tomato paste mixed 1:1 with water and cook for about 30 seconds.
Stock: Pour in the chicken stock (or water) and stir to make a sauce.
Chillies and onion: Add the smashed green chillies and the large onion segments. Cook them gently without rushing.
Chicken back in: Return the chicken and its juices and stir through.
Peppers: Add the pepper chunks and stir until a thick, glossy sauce forms.
Tomato pieces: Add the tomato flesh and cook for a couple of minutes, just enough to soften. The veg should keep some bite, so don't let it go to mush.
Finish: Stir in the fresh coriander, a pinch of kasuri methi and a little garam masala. Turn off the heat, stir, and let it sit for 1–2 minutes.
Serve: With rice or flatbreads. The sauce should be thick and coat the chicken, not swimming in oil. Optional: add 1 tsp garlic-ginger paste while frying the base if you want more garlic.

recipes.title: Pork Tenderloin in Cider Cream Sauce — So Good It Feels Restaurant Level!
ingredients: Pork tenderloin, cut into 6 medallions — 1 whole (≈ 450–500 g)
Apples, peeled and quartered — 2 medium (≈ 300 g)
Lemon honey (½ lemon juice + 1 tsp honey) — about 1 tbsp (15 ml)
Hard cider (dry) — 200 ml (¾ UK cup / ¾ US cup)
Chicken stock — 200 ml (¾ UK cup / ¾ US cup)
Fresh thyme — 4–5 sprigs (or dried — 1 heaped tsp)
Heavy cream — 120 ml (½ UK cup / ½ US cup)
Green beans tossed in butter, salt and pepper
steps: Cut the medallions: With the silver skin already removed, cut the tenderloin into about six pieces, splitting the thin end so the pieces are even.
Flatten gently: Put the pieces under cling film (it stops the meat juices splattering) and give each a light smack with a meat hammer. Pork tenderloin is tender, so don't whack it hard.
Season, then dredge: Salt and pepper both sides, then dredge in flour. Seasoning first means the seasoning stays on the meat.
Sear the pork: Heat oil and butter in a pan and sear the pork a couple of minutes per side. Take it out, cover it, and let it keep cooking gently while you do the apples.

Brown the apples: Peel and quarter the apples. Wipe out the pork residue, add a little fresh butter and colour the apple chunks all the way around. You want golden outsides and a little crunch, not mush. Move them to a bowl.
Dress the apples: Squeeze a little lemon over the apples, add a little honey (maple syrup also works) and mix. Cover to keep warm.
Start the sauce: Wipe the pan clean so there are no burnt bits. Melt butter over moderate heat and sauté the shallot (red onion or white onion also work) until translucent without burning.
Add thyme and cider: Add the thyme (the host blooms dried thyme first) with a little pepper, then pour in the hard cider — about 200 ml — to reduce by half. Apple juice can replace the cider.
Add stock: Add the chicken stock and cook it down for about four to five minutes.
Finish the sauce: Turn down the heat and stir in the cream, about a teaspoon of Dijon and about a tablespoon of wholegrain mustard. Let it thicken a little.
Combine: Nestle the pork back into the sauce with its resting juices, then return the apples and drizzle over the juices from the bowl just to warm them through.
Serve: Plate the pork and apples with plenty of sauce, a drizzle of the lemon-honey on the apples, and green beans with a little butter and a squirt of lemon. Serve with buttery mashed potato.

recipes.title: Easy Hobo Casserole -  Cheap, Filling & Comfort Food Classic!
ingredients: Ground beef or turkey — 1 lb (450 g)

Italian herbs or any herbs — 1 tsp

steps: Par-boil the potatoes: Put the cubed potatoes in cold water (salt is optional, as the canned soup is already salty), bring to a boil and cook for 7 minutes only, then drain.

Make the soup sauce: In a bowl beat the mushroom soup with the milk (rinse the can with the milk so none is wasted), a little pepper and a little Italian herbs until smooth. Cream of chicken or tomato soup also works.
Heat the oven: Preheat to 190°C / 375°F.

Brown the beef: Cook the mince in oil, seasoning with pepper and a little salt and breaking it up. Cook it at least 80% through and get a little browning. Add a little mixed Italian herbs and a little Worcestershire sauce and cook off the liquid.

Add the aromatics: Add the onions and cook until soft and translucent, then the garlic for a second or two, then about a teaspoon of paprika and more Italian herbs. You can add leftovers, carrots, peppers or mushrooms if you like.
Make the meat sauce: Tip the mince and onion mix into the soup mix and stir.
Fry the potatoes: Fry some of the par-boiled potatoes in a little oil to get colour, like little roasties. It's fine if they mash up a little.

Layer: Put the coloured potatoes in the bottom of the baking dish (the host uses an 8 by 8), add a layer of the meat mix, then more potatoes, then the rest of the meat mix, finishing with potatoes on top.
Top: Scatter on grated cheddar (optional), a little pepper and a couple of small knobs of butter.
Bake covered: Wrap tightly with foil so the potatoes steam, and bake for about 30 minutes.
Bake uncovered: Remove the foil and return to the oven for 10 to 15 minutes until golden, crusty and bubbling.
Rest and serve: Let it settle for 5 minutes, then scoop out and serve, optionally with parsley. The host serves it with baked beans; vegetables or salad also work. It freezes well in portions.

recipes.title: How to Make Sweet Pongal - Traditional Pongal Festival Special
ingredients: Raw rice (short/medium grain) — ½ US cup (100 g)
Yellow moong dal — ¼ US cup (50 g)
Jaggery (grated or powdered) — ¾ US cup (150 g)
Water (to melt jaggery) — ¼ US cup (60 ml)
Edible camphor — a tiny pinch (optional, traditional)
steps: Rinse and dry: Rinse the rice and moong dal until the water runs clear, drain, and pat dry with kitchen towel. This step is optional, but it adds a little nuttiness when dry roasting.
Dry roast the dal: Toast the moong dal in a pan over a low flame, just to dry it out with a little toasting and no colour. Take off the heat.
Boil: In another pan combine the dal, the rice, salt and water. Bring up to a boil, then knock it down to a simmer.

Simmer 25–30 minutes: Keep giving it a gentle stir, with the lid on, skimming if you like. As the water evaporates, top up with a little hot water as needed to keep a thickish porridge-like consistency.
Check the texture: After about 30 minutes it should be nice and thick. You can mash the dal and rice together, but the host prefers to leave the yellow dal visible.

Melt the jaggery: In a small pan over a gentle heat, dissolve the jaggery (coconut sugar, or light brown sugar if you can't get jaggery) in the water for about 3–4 minutes. Sieve it if you wish to remove impurities.
Combine: Stir the jaggery syrup into the rice and dal and cook for about 8 to 10 minutes, stirring and checking for evaporation (add water if needed), until nice and gloopy and thick.

Make the ghee tadka: In a pan heat about 3 tablespoons of ghee. Toast the cashew nuts lightly and add the raisins over a not-too-high flame until they puff up. Set a few raisins and cashews aside for presentation.
Finish: Stir the ghee, cashews and raisins into the pongal, then add the ground cardamom (and the edible camphor, if using) with the flame off. Stir through.
Serve: Top with the reserved cashews and raisins.

recipes.title: Ven Pongal Recipe  Soft, Creamy South Indian Comfort Food

recipes.title: Chana Dal Masala Dhaba Style Pan Method

recipes.title: Chicken Sukka Mangalorean Style  Dry Coconut Chicken

Toasted sesame seeds — ½ tsp (1 g)
steps: Boil the potatoes: Put the peeled potatoes in salted water and boil until cooked.
Infuse the milk: In a small pan warm a little milk with the sliced spring/green onions to a gentle simmer for about a minute, just to get the flavour into the milk. Don't burn it. Keep the onions in.
Brown the mince: Heat a little oil, cook off the rawness of the garlic and ginger, then add the mince, breaking it up and browning it.
Season the mince: Add the soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, chilli paste (or flakes) and sugar and cook until combined. Set aside.
Mash: Drain the potatoes and mash them with the infused milk and onions and the butter, as creamy or lumpy as you like.
Make the sauce: Whisk together the sesame paste (or peanut butter), light soy sauce, black vinegar, chilli oil, sugar and hot water until smooth. It should be pourable, so add more water if needed.
Assemble: Spoon the mash into a bowl, top with the mince, pour the sauce over, then add sesame seeds and green onion. Drizzle with extra chilli oil if you like.

recipes.title: Lemon Aval Poha Everyday South Indian Breakfast
ingredients: Thick poha (aval / flattened rice) — 1½ US cups (120 g)
Oil (vegetable or groundnut) — 2 tbsp (30 ml / ~27 g)
Green chillies, slit — 2 small (adjust to taste)
Salt — ¾ tsp (4–5 g), to taste
steps: Rinse the poha: Rinse the poha gently in water to drain off the starch, then leave it in a sieve for about 5 minutes and give it a gentle fluff with your fingers.
Temper: Heat a little oil (not too much, and turn the pan down if it's steel) and add the mustard seeds until they pop.
Add the dals and peanuts: Add the chana dal, urad dal and peanuts and toast together until there is a little colour and the peanuts are crisp.
Add aromatics and seasoning: Add the curry leaves and green chilli, then a little turmeric and salt, and give a quick turn.
Add the poha: Gently bring in the poha, sprinkle over a little water (just a little) and put a lid on for about 2 minutes.
Finish: Turn it over gently, turn off the flame, stir through the coriander and a good squirt of lemon juice.
Serve: Serve with fresh coconut and banana if you like. The host eats it with a little yogurt or curd.

recipes.title: ALOO GOBI The Most Cooked Indian Vegetable Dish!
ingredients: Potatoes, peeled, medium cubes — 400 g (2½ US cups)
Vegetable oil or mustard oil — 3 tbsp (45 ml)
Salt — 1 tsp (6 g), adjust to taste
Amchur powder (dried mango, optional) — ½ tsp
steps: Heat the oil: Heat 2–3 tablespoons of mustard oil (or vegetable oil) until it smokes a little (this burns off some of the mustard-oil fumes).
Pop the cumin: Add the cumin seeds and let them crackle and pop.
Cook the onion: Add the onion and cook, taking your time, until translucent and a little golden without burning.
Add chilli and ginger-garlic: Add the green chilli, then the ginger-garlic paste in a cleared space, cooking out the rawness.
Add the tomatoes: Add the chopped tomatoes (optional) with a little salt and cook until a little mushy.
Add the spices: On a really low flame add the turmeric, Kashmiri chilli powder, ground cumin, coriander powder and a touch of hing. Don't rush cooking the spices.
Cook the potatoes: Add the potatoes (cut quite big) and stir through. Add a splash of water, bring to a boil, turn down, put a lid on and cook about 8 to 10 minutes, stirring so nothing catches.
Add the cauliflower: Add the cauliflower with another splash of water, mix in, put the lid on and cook for 10 to 12 minutes tops. Optionally brown the cauliflower first.
Finish: Turn the flame off and add garam masala, a little amchur, a squeeze of lemon and the coriander. Mix through.
Serve: Serve with roti or paratha.

recipes.title: Old School Cottage Pie Using TINNED MINCE & Instant Mash
ingredients: White or black pepper — to taste
steps: Warm the mince: Heat butter over a gentle flame, add the tin of minced beef and onion (scrape out all the bits) and warm it all the way through for about 2 minutes.
Build the flavour: Stir in the tomato purée and cook about a minute, then add a pinch of dried thyme and a little black pepper.
Thicken: Stir in the flour, then the beef stock (from a cube or powder). Frozen peas can go in here, or mixed veg, or serve the veg on the side.
Finish the filling: Preheat the oven to 200 °C. Once thickened, add a splash of Worcestershire sauce and a little Marmite (Vegemite also works; leave it out if you have neither). Turn off the flame.
Make the mash: Pour the boiling water over the potato flakes and stir, then add the butter, a little white pepper, a little milk and a touch of salt. Leave it a minute and fluff it up.
Layer: Spread the meat mix in a dish, then top with the mash, using two forks to pull it into peaks that will go crusty. Add a little cheese on top.
Bake: Bake for 20 minutes until bubbling and golden (optionally grill 2–3 minutes for extra colour). Let it stand about 5 minutes and serve.

recipes.title: No Oven Chocolate Banana Cake — Soft, Easy & Viral
ingredients: Bananas, sliced into rounds — 2 medium (≈ 240 g peeled)
Vanilla sugar — 8 g (2 tsp), or vanilla extract — 1 tsp (5 ml)
steps: Mix the wet: In a bowl whisk the sugar, egg, vanilla (about two teaspoons), oil and milk.
Add the dry: Mix the flour, baking powder, a little salt and cocoa, then fold it into the wet mix to make the batter. Don't worry about sieving.
Slice the bananas: Peel and slice the bananas to roughly the same thickness.
Prep the pan: Use a pan with a non-stick interior and a lid. If the lid has a hole, block it with a bit of tissue so everything steams inside.
Make the caramel base: Over a low flame melt the butter, add a tablespoon of sugar and dissolve it for a little caramel base.

Lay the bananas: Starting in the middle, lay the banana slices tightly together in the pan (careful, it's hot; the host turns the flame off while arranging, then back on low). Cook for about two to three minutes without flipping.
Add the batter: On an extremely low flame pour in the batter, gently covering the bananas without disturbing them, and smooth it out a little.
Cook covered: Put the lid on and cook low and slow for about 20 to 25 minutes.
Flip: Place parchment paper and a plate on top and flip the cake out, then slide it back into the pan on the paper and cook the bottom for a couple of minutes.
Rest and serve: Turn out onto a plate, let it rest for a minute, then cut and serve.

recipes.title: FULL ROAST AIR FRYER -  COSORI TURBO TOWER Dual Air Fryer
ingredients: Beef stock or water — 120 ml (½ cup)
Beef dripping or oil — ½–1 tsp per tin
steps: Tie the beef: The chuck roast falls apart, so tie it with string into a roughly roast-joint shape.
Season: Rub with a little oil, garlic powder, rosemary salt (the host uses it on the beef and potatoes) and black pepper.
Add stock and wrap: Pour beef stock (the host uses half a stock cube) around the beef and wrap tightly in foil. Put the bottom drawer underneath to level it and catch juices.
Cook the beef covered: Cook in the bottom drawer for about an hour at 160°C.
Par-boil the potatoes: Put the cubed potatoes in cold, salted water, bring to a boil and boil for 8 minutes, then drain. Baking soda in the water is optional for fluffier edges; the host skips it.
Make the batter: Whisk the eggs, flour, a little salt and the milk for under a minute and keep it in a jug.
Uncover the beef: Take the beef out, remove the foil, take some of the juices out into a pan for gravy, and return the beef for about 10 minutes at about 200°C to get a crust.
Roast the potatoes: Toss the par-boiled potatoes in a little oil and rosemary salt, shake to rough them up, and cook in the top drawer for about 25 minutes at 200°C.
Rest the beef: Take the beef out, wrap it loosely and set aside.

Bake the Yorkshires: Put about a teaspoon of oil in each of the small cups, preheat for about 4 minutes at about 200°C in the bottom drawer, add the batter and cook about 12 minutes at 200°C without opening before about 9 minutes. The host gave his a further 2 minutes at 195°C.
Make the gravy: Mix gravy granules, warm on the stove with the reserved meat juices.
Serve: Remove the string, slice the beef and serve with roasties, Yorkshire puddings, vegetables and gravy.

From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dWWm7Oba5v8

recipes.title: Bullet Coffee with Instant Coffee No MCT, No Milk
ingredients: Hot water — 240 ml (1 cup / 8 fl oz)
Instant coffee — 1 level tablespoon (≈ 6 g / 3 tsp) — "coffee shop strength"; use 2 tsp for milder
Sweetener (honey, sugar, maple, or sweetener) — ½–1 tsp
steps: Measure: Put 1 tablespoon of instant coffee and 1 tablespoon of cow's ghee in a vessel.
Add hot water: Pour in about a cup of boiling water to dissolve the coffee.
Add flavourings: If you like, add a little maple syrup, vanilla or cinnamon (the host skips sweetener).
Froth: Use a milk frother in the mix until it has a creamy head.
Serve: Pour into a coffee mug.

recipes.title: Rajma Rice Chawal  -  No Restaurant Tricks
ingredients: Canned kidney beans, drained and well rinsed — 2 × 400 g tins (480 g drained)
Oil (mustard oil preferred, or vegetable oil) — 2½ tbsp
Salt — 1¼ tsp (7 g), adjust to taste
steps: Make the tomato base: Mix 4 tablespoons of tomato paste with about 120 ml of water and set aside.
Start the rice: Cook the basmati rice with the water and salt in a rice cooker (or on the stove).
Pop the cumin: Heat the mustard oil (vegetable oil also works), add the cumin seeds and let them splutter on a not-screaming heat.

Cook the onions: Add the onions with a pinch of salt and cook until golden with a little tinge, without burning. (The host mentions that his "reverse base" of 4–5 tablespoons of blitzed baked onions can replace this step.)
Add ginger-garlic: Add the garlic-ginger paste and cook out the rawness.
Bloom the spices: On a low flame add the coriander powder, Kashmiri chilli powder and turmeric, plus a little hing (it burns, so be careful).
Add the tomato: Stir in the tomato mix and cook on the low flame until the oil comes through and the paste is cooked out, a couple of minutes.
Add the beans: Add the kidney beans and coat well, add a little salt and the hot water. Bring to a boil, reduce to a simmer and cook for 30 minutes uncovered, stirring so nothing sticks.
Thicken: Mash a few of the beans with a masher or spoon to thicken naturally. Add a little hot water if there isn't enough sauce.
Finish: About 5 minutes from the end stir through the garam masala and the coriander; it doesn't even need further cooking.
Serve: Put the rice down, top with the rajma, and serve with onions (the host adds a little chaat masala and lemon), pickle (mango pickle), and yogurt or curd.
recipes.notes:

recipes.title: Everyday Paneer Kadhi with Rice  Simple Indian Comfort Food
steps: Whisk the base: Whisk the yogurt, besan, salt and turmeric until smooth and lump free. Letting the besan rehydrate in the yogurt is why the host mixes it first.
Colour the paneer: In a pan with a couple of tablespoons of ghee (oil also works) on a low flame, pan-fry the paneer cubes until coloured. Take them out and rest them.
Cook the kadhi: In a pan on a very low flame cook the yogurt-besan mix with the water, stirring until it thickens, about 5 minutes (longer depending on the pan).
Add the paneer: Return the paneer to the kadhi.
Make the tadka: In a small pan heat a couple of tablespoons of ghee on a lower flame and add the mustard seeds, cumin seeds, ginger, hing and the dried red chilli (broken up), then the curry leaves.
Combine: Pour the tadka over the paneer kadhi and stir through, then turn the flame off and add the coriander.
Serve: Serve with rice (or phulka), with a little extra ghee on top if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mtfbj9MA_iA
Uploaded 2025-12-26.

recipes.title: These Cheesy Garlic Potatoes Are DANGEROUSLY ADDICTIVE!
ingredients: Salt — 1 tsp (6 g) (the host uses garlic salt)
Shredded cheese (cheddar/mozzarella blend) — 1½ cups (150 g / 6 oz)
Chives or spring onion, finely chopped — 1 tbsp (4 g)
Salt and pepper — pinch to taste
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 425°F (220°C).
Season the potatoes: Cube the potatoes small, so they are bite size. Toss them with the melted butter, olive oil, garlic, salt (garlic salt), pepper and Italian seasoning.
Roast: Roast for 25–30 minutes, taking them out and turning them over a few times, until coloured.

Make the dip: Mix the sour cream, mayo, lemon, garlic powder, pepper, a tiny bit of salt, optional chilli flakes and green onion. Leave it to settle (chill about 15 minutes) so the garlic powder rehydrates.
Add the cheese: When the potatoes have a little colour, sprinkle over the shredded cheese blend and Parmesan and bake another 5–7 minutes until melted, golden and bubbly.
Serve: Top with a little more Parmesan and green onion or parsley, and serve with the dip (cocktail sticks for dipping).

recipes.title: Real Mughlai Chicken Handi  - No Cream, No Western Shortcuts!!!
ingredients: Kashmiri chilli powder – ½ tsp | 1.5 g
Oil (neutral, or ghee + oil mix) – 3 tbsp | 45 ml
Onions, sliced – 3 medium | 300 g | 3 UK cups | 3 US cups
Cashew nuts – 20 whole | 35 g (soaked 30 min, drained)
Oil or ghee – 2 tbsp | 6 tsp | 30 ml
Tomato purée – 3–4 tbsp, mixed with 6 tbsp water
Black pepper powder – ½ tsp | 1.5 g
Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek), crushed – 1 tbsp | 3 g
Fresh coriander, chopped – ¼ cup | 15 g
steps: Prep the chicken: Skin the chicken legs and cut a slash across each one so the marinade gets in.
Marinate: Rub the chicken with salt, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli powder and a little yoghurt. Don't add garlic or ginger here; they go into the cooking. Marinate for at least 4 hours.
Soak the cashews: Soak the cashews for about 30 minutes, then drain them. (Some cooks skip soaking.)

Soften the onions: Heat a little ghee, oil or a mix in a pan. Add the sliced onions with a little salt to draw out moisture. Cook gently for about 10 minutes, until soft and translucent and the raw smell has gone. Don't brown them.
Add the cashews and coconut: Stir in the drained cashews and the desiccated coconut and cook gently for 2–3 minutes.
Simmer briefly: Add a splash of water and cook gently for another 2–3 minutes on a steady, not high, heat.
Blend the paste: Turn off the heat, let it cool, then blend it to a smooth onion-cashew-coconut paste.
Garlic and ginger: Heat about 3 tbsp ghee in the cooking pot. Add the garlic-ginger paste and cook out the rawness.
Tomato: Add the tomato purée mixed with water. Cook until the oil starts to separate from the tomato.

Bloom the spices: Clear a space and add the coriander, cumin, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli powder and a little black pepper. On a low-to-moderate heat, cook for about a minute so they bloom in the oil. Stir everything together.
Add the paste and water: Stir in the blended paste, then about ½ cup (120 ml) water.
Add the yoghurt: With the heat low, add the yoghurt gently and stir it in. (You can add it before the spices instead; with this dish it makes no difference.)
Add the chicken and chillies: Add the marinated chicken and a couple of slit green chillies, then bring to a simmer.
Simmer covered: Cover and simmer for 30–35 minutes. Stir now and then so nothing sticks, and turn the chicken once so it cooks through on both sides.
Finish uncovered: Take the lid off and stir in the garam masala, kasuri methi and chopped coriander. Cook uncovered for about 5 more minutes so the methi cooks in.
Serve: Garnished with a little more coriander, with yellow rice.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O1ZhQKXmdFM
Uploaded 2025-12-24.

recipes.title: Best Way to Use Leftover Turkey – Crispy Puff Pastry Hand Pies
ingredients: Cooked turkey, finely chopped — 300 g (10.5 oz)
Cooked stuffing (sage & onion works best), crumbled — 100 g (3.5 oz)
Cream cheese or leftover gravy — 60 g (4 tbsp)
Cheddar or leftover cheese, grated (optional but recommended) — 75 g (2.5 oz)
Dijon or English mustard — 1 tsp (5 g)
Salt — ¼ tsp (taste first; leftovers can be salty)
Fresh thyme or parsley, chopped (optional) — 1 tsp
Ready-rolled puff pastry — 320 g (11 oz) (1 standard sheet) or more
Sesame seeds or poppy seeds (optional) — 1 tsp
steps: Loosen the cream cheese: Mix the mustard (English or Dijon) into the cream cheese to loosen it, and add some melted butter.
Make the filling: Add the chopped turkey (or chicken), cranberry sauce, stuffing, a pinch of thyme, black pepper, salt to taste and the cheddar, and mix.
Heat the oven: The host sets it to about 180°C (fan); the written recipe says 200°C / 180°C fan.
Cut the pastry: Cut the puff pastry into rectangles (about 4½ by 5 inches, or whatever you like).
Fill: Put a good dollop of filling on each base, leaving a border for the lid.
Top: Cut a couple of slits in the lid pieces, stretch each over the filling and squash down at the edges (a fork can be used to seal).
Glaze: Egg wash the pies and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake: Bake for about 18–22 minutes until deeply golden and puffed. Rest about 5 minutes and serve, optionally with a drizzle of gravy.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=uV0uG4koFSo

recipes.title: Real Indian Poha Recipe – How It’s Actually Made at Home!
ingredients: Thick poha (flattened rice) — 150 g (1½ UK cups / 1¾ US cups)
Green chilli, finely chopped — 1 small (or to taste)
Salt — ¾ tsp (4 g), to taste
Sev (optional, for serving) — a small handful
steps: Rinse the poha: Rinse the poha in water with a gentle stir to take out the starch, then drain in a sieve and give it a gentle fluff before cooking.
Toast the peanuts: Heat a little oil in a pan (a steel pan stays very hot, so use a low flame) and toast the peanuts without burning. Remove them to a bowl.
Temper: Add the mustard seeds until they pop, then the cumin seeds.
Cook the onion: Add the onion and cook until translucent with a little golden tinge.
Add flavourings: Add the curry leaves (leave them out if you can't get them), green chilli and a little turmeric. Potato (blanched 5 minutes and cubed small) or cauliflower can be added if you like.
Add the poha: Return the peanuts, add the poha and stir through very gently so it doesn't break up. Season with salt and sugar to taste.
Steam: Sprinkle in a little water (not much), put a lid on and steam for a couple of minutes.
Finish: Turn off the flame, add the lemon juice and coriander, and fluff gently.
Serve: Serve with a spoonful of yogurt if you like (and sev, optionally).
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=itKRyARGpnA
Uploaded 2025-12-22.

recipes.title: Easy Gingerbread Traybake Bars | Holiday Baking Made Simple
ingredients: All-purpose / plain flour — 2½ US cups (300 g)
Baking soda (bicarbonate of soda) — 1 tsp (5 g)
Optional spice boost (nutmeg or allspice) — ¼ tsp (0.5 g)
Unsalted butter, softened — ½ US cup (113 g)
Brown sugar, packed — ½ US cup (100 g)
Crystallised ginger, finely chopped — ¼ US cup (40 g)
or Chocolate chips (white, dark, or milk) — ¼ US cup (45 g)
Icing sugar / powdered sugar — 1 US cup (120 g)
steps: Mix the dry: Whisk the flour, spices, salt and baking soda (not baking powder) together.
Mix the wet: Mix the butter and sugar, then the vanilla and egg. In the video the host uses black treacle with golden syrup, half and half (the written recipe uses molasses if you can't get them).
Combine: Fold the flour mix into the wet mix with a spatula until combined; it's a stodgy, sticky mix.
Fill the tin: Line the tin with parchment paper so the bars can be pulled out. Spread the mix in and smooth it using a spoon dipped in water; it only needs to be roughly smooth.
Bake: Bake at 175–180°C for about 25–28 minutes, until nicely cooked around the outside and a little soft in the middle.
Cool: Leave in the tin until completely cool (the host cuts it a bit early and says about 2 minutes less baking would be better).
Make the glaze: Mix powdered sugar with a little vanilla, up to about two tablespoons of milk and a pinch of cinnamon until a drizzle consistency.
Cut and drizzle: Trim the edges if you like, cut into bars, open the cuts slightly and drizzle over so it runs down.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zvWZtYsy0jM
Uploaded 2025-12-21.

recipes.title: Masala Chicken Fry Using Thighs - Quick Indian Starter
ingredients: Chicken thighs (bone-in or boneless, skin removed) — 1 kg (2.2 lb), approx. 6–8 thighs
Black peppercorns (or ground) — ½ tsp (1 g)
Plain yoghurt, whisked — ½ US cup (120 g)
Kashmiri red chilli powder — ½ tsp (1 g)
Quick Tawa Flatbread (No Yeast, No Rest):
Atta flour / all-purpose flour (plain flour / maida) — 150 g – 100 g (as written in the description)
Onion (white or red), thinly sliced into rings
Lemon, cut into wedges — 1 large (~120 g) (8 wedges)
Chaat masala (optional, very light) — ¼ tsp (0.5 g)
Fresh coriander, finely chopped (optional) — 1 tbsp (3 g)
steps: Marinate: Mix the chicken with the turmeric, ginger-garlic paste, salt and lemon juice. Leave at least 30 minutes, preferably overnight.

Dry roast the spices: In a pan dry roast the cinnamon, chillies, cardamom, cloves, black peppercorns, coriander seeds and cumin seeds until crackling, not burnt, then take off the heat and roughly grind.
Cook the onions: Fry the sliced onions in oil for 10 to 12 minutes, then take them out and set aside. The oil left in the pan is infused oil that you'll use for the chicken.

Make the flatbread dough: Mix the flours with the salt, then add the ghee and the water (the host says you can split the liquid between water and yogurt for a softer bread; no raising agent) and knead to a dough. Divide into six and roll into balls.

Cook the flatbreads: Cover the dough balls, roll each out (it doesn't need to be round), and cook on a warm non-stick pan until bubbles form, flip, and cook through. Stack covered under a cloth to stay soft.
Start the chicken: Add a little more oil to the onion pan and start frying the chicken.
Add the masala: Turn the chicken over, add the ground spice mix and turn a couple of times, moving pieces around the pan so they cook evenly.
Add yoghurt: Turn the flame right down, add the whisked yoghurt and the Kashmiri chilli powder and cook until it all clings to the chicken.
Finish: Add the coriander, green chillies and lemon juice. Stir some of the onions in, or save them to go over the dish.
Serve: Serve with the flatbread, red onion rings seasoned (chaat masala) and lemon wedges.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v1UmM7j8JxE
Uploaded 2025-12-20.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: The BEST British Flapjacks Ever  Crisp Edges, Chewy Centre
ingredients: Thick slab version, for an 11 × 9 inch deep tin.
Rolled oats — 900 g (the description adds "blitz 40g", i.e. 40 g of the oats are blitzed)
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 180°C / 350°F and line the 11 × 9 inch deep tin with baking paper.

Melt the base: In a pan melt the butter with the sugars and golden syrup, then add the salt and vanilla (the host uses about two teaspoons). Heat until it looks like molten lava with a bubble around the outside, without burning. Turn the flame off.
Add the oats: Mix in the oats (a portion ground up so it sticks; quick oats also work without grinding). Add raisins or any add-ons you like (coconut, nuts). Mix until fully incorporated.
Fill the tin: Tip into the tin and use a hot-water-warmed spoon to level and squash it down, because it is very sticky.
Bake: Bake for 22–26 minutes until golden on top and darker around the edges, with the centre still soft but not liquid.
Cool: Leave in the tin at least 3 hours (the host leaves it nearly 4). For best slicing refrigerate for 1–2 hours.
Slice and serve: Take out of the tin and cut.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=mT4PYnougcU
Uploaded 2025-12-19.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F / Gas 4; Bake 22–26 minutes. It should be golden on top, edges darker, centre still soft but not liquid; Leave in the tin at least 3 hours.

recipes.title: Chicken Tikka Chaat — Sauce Makes the Difference!
ingredients: Chicken thighs, boneless and skinless — 500 g (1.1 lb)
Black salt (kala namak) — ½ tsp (2 g)
steps: Marinate: Mix the chicken with the oil, the spices, yogurt, lemon juice and the ginger-garlic paste, coating well. Marinate a minimum of 30 minutes, preferably overnight.

Cook the purée base: In a pan with a little ghee (or oil) cook the onion until a little golden tinge (don't burn it). Add the green chilli, ginger and tomatoes and cook until jammy, then the black salt and toasted ground cumin.

Cool and blend: Let the mixture cool. Blend it with about 120 ml of water, a little lemon juice, about two tablespoons of coriander stems (keep the leaves for the finish) and two teaspoons of chaat masala powder.
Char the chicken: In a wiped-out pan dry fry the chicken in batches, getting colour and char on both sides, cooking out the extra moisture. Take each batch out and rest it with its juices.
Add the purée: On a low flame add the purée to the pan and warm it through without bubbling hard, cooking out some moisture.
Coat: Return the chicken and any juices and coat it. The sauce should sit between dry and gravy: thick enough to cling to the chicken, with some moisture.
Serve: Finish with a squeeze of lemon, a dusting of chaat masala, a little coriander and lemon wedges.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y0fveXcRhoI
Uploaded 2025-12-18.

recipes.title: Lazy Chicken Enchiladas – Cheesy Oven Bake Everyone Loves!
ingredients: Tomato passata / crushed tomatoes — 400 g (1¾ US cups)
Chicken stock or water — 120 ml (½ US cup)
Flour tortillas (torn or halved) — 4–5 medium (~220 g total)
Cheddar or Monterey Jack, grated — 200 g (2 US cups)
Mozzarella (optional, for extra melt) — 100 g (1 US cup)
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 190°C / 375°F.
Cook the onion and garlic: In a pan with oil cook the onion to take away the rawness and get a little colour, then add the garlic.
