Brown the chicken: Add the chicken mince, breaking it up and cooking it until there is no pink (it isn't beef, so it must be cooked).
Season: Add the oregano, salt (only a little if using a stock cube), cumin, smoked paprika, chilli powder and black pepper.

Make the sauce: Add the chicken stock, the tomato purée and the passata (the host blends a 400 g tin of tomatoes) and simmer gently for about 8 to 10 minutes until it thickens slightly but keeps some fluid. A little sugar (up to a teaspoon) can offset the acidity of the tomato.
Layer: In a baking dish spread a layer of the sauce, then torn-up tortillas, dots of cheese, more sauce, and repeat. Finish with a thin layer of tortilla, which crisps on top.
Top: Cover with the cheese and optional mozzarella.
Bake: Bake uncovered for about 25–30 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest 5 minutes before serving.
Serve: Serve with a little sour cream, and a crisp salad, avocado or guacamole if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gofTjHs4kNw
Uploaded 2025-12-17.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 190°C / 375°F; Bake uncovered for 25–30 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: Classic Orange Steamed Sponge Pudding | Old-School British Dessert
ingredients: Optional: ½ tsp orange zest for extra flavour.
steps: Butter the basin: Butter a small (about 500 ml) pudding basin.
Cream: Cream the softened butter and sugar until light and fluffy (by hand or with a hand mixer).
Add the eggs: Beat in the eggs (the host adds a little salt) one at a time.
Fold in the flour: Fold in the self-raising flour and loosen with a couple of tablespoons of orange cordial. The batter should be at dropping consistency.
Add the syrup layer: Put four tablespoons of orange cordial and a tablespoon of sugar into the bottom of the basin.
Add the sponge: Spoon the batter over, starting at the sides so it clings, then fill in the middle.
Cover: Cover with parchment and foil (it doesn't need to be tied).

Steam: Put the basin in a steamer with water and steam for 1 hour, keeping the water topped up. (The description gives a microwave alternative: covered, no foil, 800–900W for 6–7 minutes, 1000W for 5–6 minutes, for a 1–1.2 litre basin.)
Rest and turn out: Let it settle for about 2 minutes, put a plate on and flip it quickly (it's red hot) so the orange syrup runs down the sponge.
Serve: Slice and serve with custard.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T_HMOa7gwYE
Uploaded 2025-12-16.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Steam for 1 hour, keeping the water topped up.

recipes.title: EASY Palak Paneer  Smooth & Creamy Spinach Curry
ingredients: Oil or ghee (for light frying, optional) — 1 tbsp (15 ml)
Double cream or single cream — 3 tbsp (45 ml) (optional)
Kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed (optional) — ½ tsp
steps: Blanch the spinach: Bring salted water to a boil, rip up the washed spinach (stalk ends off) and blanch it for only about 60 to 90 seconds, then put it straight into cold water.
Blend: Blend the spinach with a little of the blanching water (you want some fluid) into a purée. Green chilli can be blended in.
Colour the paneer: In a little ghee fry the paneer cubes just to colour a couple of sides (optional). Take them out.
Start the base: In a pan add ghee and the cumin seeds, then the onion and cook out the rawness. This is a no-tomato version. Add the green chilli.
Add garlic and ginger: When the onion shows a little tinge add the garlic-ginger paste for 30–45 seconds.
Bloom the spices: Turn down the flame and add the coriander, cumin, turmeric and salt, letting them release their oil without burning.
Add the spinach: Turn the flame up a little, add the spinach purée and cook about 5 to 7 minutes until it thickens a little, bringing the onion and spices through the spinach.
Finish: Return the paneer and add the garam masala, a couple of tablespoons of cream, a little ghee or butter and the kasuri methi, for no more than a couple of minutes.
Serve: Serve with rice (the host uses yellow rice) and, if you want to go Western, a dollop of cream on top.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M2Yny_C8QmM
Uploaded 2025-12-15.

recipes.title: Golden Indian Yellow Rice – Easy Rice Cooker Method!
ingredients: Basmati rice — 2 cups (UK: 400 g / US: 380 g)
Water or light stock — 3½ cups (UK: 840 ml)
Salt — 1–1½ tsp (5–9 g), adjust to taste
Onion, finely sliced — ½ cup (UK: 80 g / US: 70 g)
Frozen peas — ½ cup (UK: 70 g / US: 80 g)
steps: Rinse the rice: Wash the basmati until the water runs clear and drain most of it out.
Prep the add-ins: Fine dice the onion (optional) and bash the cardamom pods to open them and release the seeds' flavour.

Load the cooker: Put the rice in the rice cooker with the stock or water (use up to a teaspoon of salt if using stock cubes), cardamom, cloves, onion, peas, cumin seeds, bay leaves, turmeric and a couple of tablespoons of ghee.
Stir: Give it a stir to distribute the turmeric around the rice.
Cook: Close the lid and press cook. (On the stove, bring it all to a boil with the water or stock and cook until it runs fairly dry and absorbed.)
Rest: When it switches to warm, leave it for about 5 to 10 minutes.
Fluff: Remove the whole spices if you don't want them, fluff with a fork and serve. It freezes well and reheats in a couple of minutes in the microwave.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=VcKulyeNXV0
Uploaded 2025-12-15.

recipes.title: The Best Sausage & Potato Tray Bake You’ll make this week!
ingredients: English or Dijon mustard — 1 tbsp (15 g)
Honey or brown sugar (optional) — 1 tsp (5 g)
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 200°C (fan 180°C).
Prep the potatoes: Cut the potatoes into wedges (skins on, scrubbed), put them in a tray with olive oil, salt and pepper.
Roast the potatoes first: Put them in the oven for 20 minutes while you prep everything else.
Chop the veg: Cut the onions into thick slices, the green pepper into chunks and halve the tomatoes. The host also adds a whole bunch of garlic to roast, and apple wedges (skin on).

Make the sauce: In a bowl mix the mustards, Worcestershire sauce, olive oil, honey (the host uses about 1½ tablespoons of maple syrup instead, with a little apple cider vinegar, chicken stock and a tablespoon of butter), garlic and pepper. It doesn't matter if the butter hasn't melted.

Assemble: Take out the potatoes and turn them over. Add the onions, peppers, garlic, tomatoes (and apple), pour over the mustard sauce, add a little dried thyme and a pinch of caraway (optional), and lay the sausages on top.
Roast: Return to the oven for about 30–35 minutes, turning the sausages about halfway through (about 20 minutes) for colour and turning the veg in the sauce.
Check and serve: If the potatoes are done, the veg are done. Serve with the mustard sauce from the tray.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QoGfcDL75e8
Uploaded 2025-12-14.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat to 200°C / 390°F (fan 180°C / 355°F).

recipes.title: The Leek Pie You’ve Never Heard Of — A Real English Village Recipe
ingredients: Cold water — 3–5 tbsp (45–75 ml), just enough to bind
(In the video the host uses his own pastry or ready-rolled shortcrust; the captions don't describe making it.)
Beef (lean stewing cut – chuck, blade, shin) — 12 oz (340 g)
Water or light beef stock — 120 ml (½ cup)
Salt — ½–¾ tsp (depending on bacon saltiness)
Egg, beaten with 1 tsp (5 ml) water — 1
Serving (Traditional): pickled onions, brown sauce, crumbly cheese (Stilton if keeping it regional).:
Pressure cooker: High Pressure 25 minutes, 10 minutes natural release. Oven: 200°C / 400°F / Gas 6.
steps: Prep the leeks: Cut the washed, cleaned leeks into 1–2 cm pieces, all the same size.
Prep the meat: Cube the bacon (offcuts are fine, or streaky bacon) and the beef a little smaller, but not too small so it keeps structure in the pressure cooker.
Brown: Heat a little oil in a pan and brown the beef for a couple of minutes per turn, then the bacon, to add depth of flavour. Don't cook it through.

Pressure cook: Put the meat in the Instant Pot liner with at least half a cup of water and a little cornflour slurry. Pressure cook on high for 25 minutes, then natural release for 10 minutes, then manually release the pressure. (Traditionally the filling goes in the oven for about 1½ hours.) Take it out to cool.
Boil the leeks: Boil the leeks (lid on) for about 7 to 8 minutes. Keep some of the leek water to make gravy.

Make the gravy: Melt a little butter, cook out about 1½ tablespoons of flour in it, then add the meat juices (and some of the leek water) and reduce to a thick gravy. Season only with pepper; the bacon, beef and leek are the seasoning. Let everything cool before filling the pastry.
Line the tin: Roll out the pastry to fit an 8 inch spring form tin and line it. Brush the base with egg white to seal it, since leeks release a lot of fluid.
Fill: Add layers of leek and meat with some of the thick gravy, saving the rest of the gravy to serve.
Top: Roll a pastry lid, fold in and crimp, cut a couple of good vents and egg wash the top.
Bake: Bake at 200°C for 30–40 minutes until deep golden. Rest 10–15 minutes before serving with gravy, potatoes, mash or veg.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ohvb2gAbT-8
Uploaded 2025-12-13.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Cook on High Pressure – 25 minutes. Allow 10 minutes natural release; Bake at 200°C / 400°F / Gas 6 for 30–40 minutes, until deep golden; Rest 10–15 minutes before serving.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: The Softest, Creamiest Khichdi — No Pressure Cooker Needed!
ingredients: Kashmiri chilli powder — ½ tsp (1.5 g)
Salt — 1 tsp (6 g) to start; adjust later
2.5 litres (about 10 cups) for 1 cup rice + 1 cup dal; reduce for thicker khichdi, add more for looser.
steps: Rinse and soak: Rinse the moong dal and rice together until the water is clear, cover with water and soak 15 to 20 minutes, then drain.
Temper: In a pan heat the oil and a good dollop of ghee. Add the cumin seeds, bay leaf, dried chilli (broken) and a pinch of hing for about 20 seconds.
Cook the onion: Add the onion and cook 3 or 4 minutes.
Add aromatics: Add the garlic, ginger and green chilli (smacked with a knife) for about a minute.
Add the tomatoes: Add the tomatoes with a tiny bit of salt to draw out the moisture and cook until they release their sweetness.
Add spices and veg: Add salt, turmeric, Kashmiri chilli and coriander powder for a minute, then the potatoes and carrots and stir.
Add rice and dal: Add the drained rice and moong dal, stir for a minute, then pour in the water (about 2 litres plus in the open pan, since it evaporates).
Simmer: Bring to a boil, knock it down to a simmer and cook for about 30 to 35 minutes, stirring now and again and watching the water level. Don't worry about any foam.

Add peas and coriander: About 20 minutes after the dal goes in, stir in the frozen peas. Add some coriander (save some for the end). Kasuri methi can go in for the last 5 minutes (the host leaves it out).
Finish: Cook to your desired thickness (thicker if eating by hand). Turn the flame off, stir through the garam masala and drizzle over a tablespoon of ghee.
Serve: Serve with extra coriander, a blob of yogurt if you like, poppadoms, red onion and mango chutney.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_gsLKtRP174
Uploaded 2025-12-12.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: This Black Pepper BEEF Stir Fry Is Ridiculously GOOD 15 Minutes!
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper — 1–2 tsp (the heat of the dish; adjust to taste)
Crushed red pepper flakes — ½–1 tsp (optional)
Water or beef broth — ¼ cup (the host uses ½ a beef stock cube)
Rice vinegar or lime juice — 1 tsp
steps: Prep: Mince the garlic, dice the onion, and cube the peppers (the host uses red, green and yellow) roughly the same size. Slice green onion to go over the top.

Make the sauce: Dissolve half a beef stock cube in hot water. In a bowl combine it with the hoisin, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, sesame oil, rice vinegar (or lime juice), sugar and cornstarch, dissolving any lumps.

Brown the beef: Heat a little oil in a small pan and brown the beef, breaking it up and cooking out the moisture. No extra salt or pepper is needed on the meat besides a little of the black pepper from the dish.
Add the veg: Add the onions, then the garlic, then the peppers, cooking a couple of minutes so they stay a little crunchy but soften.
Add pepper and sauce: Add the black pepper, then pour in the sauce and stir until it clings. Add the chilli flakes if you like.
Serve: Serve over rice, noodles or mash with green onions, sesame seeds and a little black pepper sprinkled on top.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EtYmosHcQvs
Uploaded 2025-12-11.

recipes.title: I Added Lentils to My Bread… The Result Shocked Me!!
ingredients: Strong bread flour — 400 g (3 UK cups / 3¼ US cups); the host uses 200 g all-purpose flour and 200 g bread flour
Cooked and mashed red lentils — 100 g (½ cup / 3½ oz)
The host also adds dried rosemary (amount not stated).
steps: Cook the lentils: Rinse the red lentils and cook them for about 15 to 20 minutes, until soft and creamy, cooking the water down (or drain) and mashing them. Don't let them catch on the bottom of the pan or they'll turn bitter. Let them cool completely.
Bloom the yeast: Dissolve about a teaspoon of sugar and the yeast in the warm water and wait until it blooms.
Mix the dry: In a stand mixer bowl combine the bread flour, all-purpose flour, salt and dried herbs (rosemary) so they distribute evenly.
Add the wet: Add the mashed lentils and the yeast mix (and olive oil). With a dough hook, mix slow and then faster for 8 to 10 minutes. It's a sticky, slightly tacky dough.
First rise: Knead it briefly with a little flour, put it in an oiled bowl, cover with a bag and let it rise about an hour until doubled.
Shape: Knock back, squash out the air into a rectangle, roll up and shape into a bloomer on a tray.
Second rise: Cover and rise another 40 minutes.
Slash and bake: Preheat the oven to 220°C / 425°F. Dust with flour, slash the top 3–5 times and bake for 25–30 minutes (the host says up to 35) until golden and the base sounds hollow.
Cool: Cool on a rack completely before slicing.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SQ6SsevtKYY
Uploaded 2025-12-10.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 220 °C / 425 °F. Dust with flour and slash the top 3–4 times. Bake 25–30 minutes until golden and the base sounds hollow.

recipes.title: Creamed Tuna & Rice — The Forgotten Budget Dinner That Fed a Generation
ingredients: Canned tuna in water, drained — 2 × 160 g cans (320 g total)
Condensed mushroom soup — 2 × 295 g cans (590 g total)
Cold water for slurry — 4 tbsp (60 ml)
or Canned peas, corn, or carrots — 160 g drained (1 cup)
Plain white rice (dry) — 300 g (1½ UK cups / 1⅔ US cups)
Soy sauce (optional at table) — to taste
The host also adds a little butter, a small half onion, diced, and pepper (amounts not stated); no salt, since the tins are salty.
steps: Cook the rice: Have the rice on in the rice cooker.
Soften the onion: (Optional.) In a pan melt a little butter and cook the small diced onion with a little pepper on a low flame, just to take out the rawness and not to brown.
Make the soup base: Stir in the mushroom soups with a little of the milk to stop it catching, then the rest of the milk, stirring until smooth.
Add the tuna: Tip in the drained tuna and stir to heat through, with a little more pepper if you like.
Add the veg: Stir in the frozen vegetables (or canned or fresh).

Thicken: Mix the cornflour with the cold water and stir it in. It thickens quickly, so be careful; add water or milk if it goes too thick. Simmer briefly and leave a little fluid since it's served over rice.
Serve: Serve over the rice. Leftovers go on toast, over a jacket potato, or as a casserole base with cheese grilled on top.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nMn21JTl4io
Uploaded 2025-12-09.

recipes.title: 1 Chicken Thigh Feeds 2! | Ultimate Budget Chicken & Potato Curry
ingredients: Potato, peeled and diced small — 350 g (1½ cups)
Fresh coriander or parsley (optional) — 1 tbsp, chopped
steps: Prep: Dice the onion and cut the potatoes into small, even cubes. Remove the skin from the chicken thigh and cut the meat fairly small, so there are enough pieces to go around for two.

Colour the potatoes: Heat ghee/oil in a pan, add the cumin seeds to splutter, then the potatoes with a little salt and a little turmeric. Fry until they have colour like little roast potatoes, then take them out and set aside.
Cook the onion: Add the onions and cook with a little tinge of colour.
Add garlic and ginger: Leave a space and fry the garlic and ginger to take out the rawness, then bring it in with the onion.
Bloom the spices: Turn down the flame and bloom the spices (including pepper) gently without rushing.
Add the chicken: Turn up the flame a little, add the chicken pieces and fry them, stirring in the spices.
Add tomato: Add a good tablespoon of tomato purée, a splash of stock to loosen, then the tinned tomatoes with their juice (the host cuts up the whole tomatoes in the tin).

Simmer: Add the rest of the stock and cook about 10 minutes, then return the potatoes and cook about 7 minutes more, until the potatoes are cooked but not broken up (a few that break act as a natural thickener).
Finish: Turn off the heat and stir in the yogurt. Top with coriander and serve, with naan, chapati or rice if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ancs_L_lnbc
Uploaded 2025-12-08.

recipes.title: OLD SCHOOL Chocolate Cracknell – British School Dessert Classic No Bake!
ingredients: Golden syrup (from tin) — 200 g (150 ml / 10 tbsp)
Make as cupcakes or a slab — up to you. Optional: a touch of vanilla and a pinch of salt (amounts not stated).
steps: Melt the butter: Melt the butter in a pan over a low flame; don't let it boil.
Add the syrup: Add the golden syrup and stir in. Add a touch of vanilla and a pinch of salt if you like.
Add cocoa and cornflour: Stir in the cocoa powder and the cornflour (the host's tip for a more solid, cuttable dessert that is still soft and crunchy).
Add the cornflakes: Put the flame low (or off) and add the cornflakes, crushed (the host's tip for binding better). Keep working it until they are coated; turn off the flame.
Fill cupcake papers: For cupcakes, spoon some of the mix into paper cases.
Press into a slab: For a slab, line a dish with parchment paper, leaving an overhang so it comes out, and squash the mix down firmly.
Chill: Put it in the fridge to cool down while it's still warm.
Cut and serve: Lift out, cut into squares and serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EeuUi4MDB_I
Uploaded 2025-12-07.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: EASY Korean Chili Chicken Mash Bowl — Next Level Comfort Food!
ingredients: Chicken thighs or breast, diced — 400 g
Rice vinegar or lime juice — 1 tsp (5 ml)
For the Creamy Cottage Cheese Drizzle:
Extra honey/maple syrup or chilli oil (optional)
steps: Boil the potatoes: Put the chopped potatoes in cold, salted water and boil while you prep.
Make the chicken sauce: In a bowl mix the gochujang, soy sauce, honey or maple syrup, minced garlic and rice vinegar (or lime juice).
Make the drizzle: Beat the cottage cheese with the sesame oil, honey or maple syrup and a pinch of chilli flakes until smooth. If it's too thick add a teaspoon or two of water so it can be drizzled.
Cook the chicken: Pat the diced chicken dry and fry in a little oil for six or seven minutes, cooking out all the water and getting a little colour.
Glaze: Turn the heat down, add the sauce to the pan and stir for a minute until sticky.
Mash: Mash the potatoes with the butter and warmed milk, season with salt and pepper.
Assemble: Spoon mash into a bowl, smooth it out, top with the chicken, drizzle with the cottage cheese sauce, and finish with green onion, sesame seeds and optional chilli.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I1YBGP_DrCE
Uploaded 2025-12-06.

recipes.title: Two Tin Chickpea Masala — Ready in 10 Minutes!
ingredients: Tinned chickpeas — 1 can (400 g drained / 240 g cooked)
Chilli powder or flakes — ½ tsp (optional)
Self-raising flour — 200–220 g (1⅔ UK cups / 1½ US cups)
steps: Make the naan dough: Mix the self-raising flour, salt, kalonji (a pinch) and yoghurt, and bring together with your hands into a dough, adding a little oil to keep it soft. Cover and set aside.
Prep: Drain and rinse the chickpeas, chop the onion and garlic (keep some garlic for garlic naan), and chop the coriander.
Cook the onion: Heat the oil, add the onions with a little salt, and take the rawness out (colour is optional).

Add the garlic and bloom the spices: Turn down the flame, add the garlic and bloom the curry powder, paprika, cumin, chilli and a little turmeric (about a quarter teaspoon), with a little salt. Don't rush.
Add tomato: Add a good tablespoon of tomato purée and a little sugar to balance the acidity, turn up the flame a little and add the tin tomatoes, chopping them in the tin with scissors.
Add the chickpeas: Add the water and chickpeas and cook about 5 minutes (or longer for a thicker sauce). Put it on the back burner while you do the naan.
Make clarified butter: Put a lump of butter in a bowl, put the bowl in boiling water with a lid on; the milk solids drop to the bottom and the butter on top is clarified.
Cook the naan: Divide the dough into four, roll out into naan shapes, and cook in a warm, dry non-stick pan until bubbles form, then flip and press down with a spatula or tissue so it puffs up.
Brush: Brush the naan with clarified butter, rub with garlic, and add coriander if you like.
Finish the curry: Add a squeeze of lemon and the coriander, stir through, and serve with the naan.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7O1vq_baXpc
Uploaded 2025-12-05.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: How to Make Yang Chow Fried Rice at Home just like the restaurant!
ingredients: Cold cooked jasmine rice — 3 cups (400 g)
BBQ pork (char siu), diced — ⅓ cup (70 g)
Poached chicken, diced — ⅓ cup (70 g)
Frozen peas & carrots — ½ cup (80 g)
steps: Blanch the proteins: Bring salted water to a boil in a small pan. Blanch the chicken (sliced across), then the shrimp, then just warm the char siu pork through. Take them out.
Scramble the eggs: Wipe out the wok, add a little oil over a not-screaming flame and gently scramble the beaten eggs. Don't overcook them. Take them out.
Fry the garlic and rice: Add a little oil and the garlic, then the rice, breaking it up gently.
Season: Add a little soy sauce (the host adds a little dark soy for colour as well) and a little MSG. No extra salt is needed. Turn it gently so you don't break the rice, and let it catch a little.
Add everything back: Add the peas, the chicken, shrimp and pork, and the egg.
Finish: Add the green onion (keep a little for garnish) and a shake of white pepper, stir through and serve.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OHkjCtaK0tw
Uploaded 2025-12-04.

recipes.title: My Favourite Budget Soup — Thick, Hearty, Ham & Veg Goodness
ingredients: Potatoes, peeled and cubed (1–1.5 cm) — 250 g
steps: Prep: Dice the onion, mince the garlic, dice the carrots and celery, and cube the potatoes smaller than the carrots so everything cooks within about 30 minutes. Cube the ham.
Sauté the onion: Heat the oil in a deep pan and sauté the onions with the bay leaf, salt, pepper, turmeric, smoked paprika and chilli flakes to take the rawness out, not to colour.
Add the garlic: Add the garlic.
Add the carrots and celery: Add the carrots and celery with a little salt and cook about five to six minutes on a not-too-high flame.
Add the potatoes and tomatoes: Add the potatoes, then the tin of tomatoes (the host chops whole tomatoes in the can with scissors).

Add lentils and stock: Add the rinsed red lentils and the stock. Bring to a boil, knock it down to a simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, open or lidded, stirring now and again as the lentils sink to the bottom.
Check the potatoes: When a fork goes in with a little resistance, add the ham and warm through for four or five minutes.
Finish: Stir through the lemon juice and the parsley.
Serve: Serve with crusty bread and butter. It freezes well in portions.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=q1W_6s5jp8U
Uploaded 2025-12-03.

recipes.title: The Cheapest Curry You’ll Ever Make —Costs Pennies… and Tastes Unreal!
ingredients: Tin of tomatoes (diced or crushed) — 400 g
steps: Cook the lentils: Put the rinsed and drained red lentils in a pan with the stock or water, bring to a boil, then simmer about 12 minutes, adding water if needed, until plump with some texture.

Make the naan dough: Mix the self-raising flour, salt and yogurt (the host adds a little oil to keep it soft) into a dough. It's a little tacky, so cover it. (Note: self-rising flour in the US already has salt.)
Start the curry: In a pan sauté the onion in a little oil with a little salt and pepper until a tinge of colour.
Add garlic and ginger: Add the garlic and ginger and cook until the rawness leaves.
Bloom the spices: Turn the pan down and add the curry powder, cumin, chilli flakes and turmeric, toasting gently in the low flame.

Add tomato: Add the tomato juice from the tin, then a good tablespoon of tomato paste and about a teaspoon of sugar (optional) if the tomato is too sour. Cut up the tinned tomatoes with scissors in the can and add them. Cook about 3 minutes.
Add lentils: Add the cooked lentils and cook for about 15 minutes.
Make clarified butter: Put a little butter in a bowl, add boiling water, cover; the milk solids sink and the butter on top is clarified.
Cook the naan: Divide the dough into four, roll each out and cook in a dry warm non-stick pan until bubbles form, pressing with a tissue, cloth or spatula, then flip.
Brush: Brush the naan with clarified butter, rub with garlic and add coriander.
Serve: Serve the curry with coriander on top, basmati rice and the naan.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bUVhHzE67I4
Uploaded 2025-12-02.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Poor Man’s Cottage Pie You’ll Make Every Week!
ingredients: Minced beef (or mixed beef & pork) — 300 g
Frozen peas — 80 g (½ cup) (the host used 220 g mixed frozen veg)
Beef stock (cube or powder) — 300 ml (1¼ cups)
Tomato paste (optional but great) — 1 tbsp (18 g)
Optional: extra 30 g (¼ cup) cheese for browning.
Oven 200°C (400°F) for 20–25 minutes. Air fryer 180°C for 10–12 minutes.
steps: Heat the oven and boil the potatoes: Preheat to 200°C. Put the cubed potatoes in salted water and boil.
Soften the onion: In a pan heat the oil and cook the onion with a little salt and pepper (if using fresh carrots, fry them with the onion at the start).
Brown the mince: Add the mince (the host's was frozen and broke down as it defrosted), a pinch of dried thyme and pepper. Salt can come afterwards.
Add the flour: Stir in a good tablespoon of flour and cook out the rawness.
Add flavour: Add the Worcestershire sauce (or soy sauce) and a tablespoon of tomato paste.
Make the gravy: Add the gravy mix or stock and simmer for about 10 minutes until thick, not swimming and not dry.
Add the veg: Stir in the frozen veg (peas). Turn off the heat.
Mash: Mash the potatoes with butter and milk around the side, with salt and pepper.

Assemble: Put the filling in an 8 by 8 inch (20 cm) dish, spoon the mash around the sides first and then fill in the middle, and rough up the top with a fork for crevices to crisp. Add a little cheddar if you like.
Bake: Bake 25–30 minutes (the description says 20–25) until bubbling and golden.
Serve: Serve with buttered cabbage, broccoli or anything you like. It freezes in portions.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R0rQ1x7xEzI
Uploaded 2025-12-01.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 20–25 minutes, or until bubbling and golden; Air fryer: 180°C for 10–12 minutes.

recipes.title: POOR MAN’S WELLINGTON!
ingredients: Tomato sauce or passata — 2 tbsp (the host uses a tablespoon of tomato paste with a little water)
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 200°C / 390°F.
Slice the potatoes: Slice the peeled potatoes as thin and even as you can (the host uses a slicer; a knife works).

Lay the shingles: Line a tray with parchment paper and brush with olive oil. Lay the potato slices out overlapping like roof tiles. Brush the top with oil, season with salt and pepper, scatter over the mozzarella and a pinch of thyme.
Bake the base: Bake the potato base for 25–30 minutes until golden.

Cook the filling: Meanwhile, cook the onion in oil and a little butter, add the garlic, then the beef (breaking it up) with salt, pepper and thyme. Stir in tomato paste with a little water for a thick tomato sauce, then the curry powder, Worcestershire sauce, smoked paprika and chilli flakes. Keep it thick and moist, not dried out. Add the coriander or parsley (keep a little for the top).
Add cheese: Take off the heat, let it cool, and stir in the mozzarella.
Fill: Take the potato base out (leave the oven on) and let it cool briefly. Spread the mince about an inch inside the edge, leaving about an inch at the top since it squashes out.
Roll: Using the parchment, roll the potato over the filling like a log.
Top: Add a little mozzarella and a little mature cheddar on top.
Crisp: Return to the oven at 200°C for 15–20 minutes until the outside is crispy.
Rest and serve: Rest about 5 minutes, slice through the crusty top and serve with parsley and onion gravy.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GYYlzlax1DI
Uploaded 2025-11-30.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the oven to 200°C / 390°F; Bake the potato base for 25–30 minutes; Return to the oven at 200°C / 390°F for 15–20 minutes until the outside is crispy.

recipes.title: Leftovers REALLY! EASY Ultimate Christmas/Thanksgiving Leftovers Recipe!
ingredients: Cooked turkey (shredded or cubed) — 200 g (1⅓ cups)
Cranberry sauce (not too sweet) — 120 g (½ cup)
Cooked vegetables (carrots, peas, sprouts, green beans) — 150 g (1 cup) (optional)
Grated cheese (cheddar or gruyère) — 120 g (1 cup)
Milk or leftover gravy + milk mix — 300 ml (1¼ cups)
Double cream or single cream — 120 ml (½ cup)
Dijon or English mustard — 1 tsp (5 g)
Dried sage or thyme — 1 tsp (1 g) (the host uses poultry seasoning)
Crushed stuffing crumbs — 3 tbsp (20 g) (optional, adds a crunchy top)
Baking dish approx. 8 × 10 inch (20 × 25 cm), greased. Oven: 175°C / 350°F.
steps: Heat the oven and tear the bread: Preheat to 175°C / 350°F (the host's oven was at 190°C). Grease the baking dish and tear or cube the stale bread.
Make the custard: In a bowl mix the eggs, garlic powder, milk, cream, salt, black pepper, mustard (a good teaspoon of Dijon) and herbs (poultry seasoning).
Soak: Add the bread to the custard, mix, and let it soak for about 10 minutes.
Add the fillings: Mix in the turkey (or chicken) and any leftover veggies.
Layer: Put half in the dish, add the cranberry sauce and a little cheddar, then the rest of the bread pudding mix.
Top: Scatter over the rest of the cheese and Parmesan (and stuffing crumbs, if using).
Bake: Bake for 35–45 minutes until golden, bubbling, firm in the centre and crisp at the edges.
Rest and serve: Rest about 7 minutes and serve with onion gravy, and potatoes or mash if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=26JMZmaKOuY
Uploaded 2025-11-29.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Grease a baking dish (approx. 8 x 10 inch / 20 x 25 cm). Preheat oven to 175°C / 350°F; Bake 35–45 minutes until golden brown, firm in the centre, and crisp at the edges.

recipes.title: Can Your Air Fryer Do THIS? 4 CHRISTMAS Bakes at the Same Time! COSORI TURBO TOWER Dual Air Fryer
ingredients: Hot water crust pastry (see the host's hot water crust video)
Branston Pickle (Original) — 3 tsp total (½ tsp per pie)
Sesame or poppy seeds — ½ tsp (optional)
Icing sugar for dusting after baking — optional
Brie, cut into 1.5–2 cm cubes — 120–150 g
Cooking times from the description: Bake 18–22 min at 165°C; 6 min at 175°C to crisp; bake 8 min at 165°C.:
steps: Mix the sausage meat: Mix the pork mince with salt, black pepper, sage, nutmeg, breadcrumbs and a little water, working it for several minutes until sticky.
Mix the pork pie filling: Mix pork mince (the host also adds small cubes of pork shoulder) with salt, black pepper, white pepper, sage, nutmeg and water, working it until sticky.
Roll the sausage rolls: Roll the sausage meat into a thin sausage, lay it on the puff pastry, roll up, and cut into minis. Put them on a lined sheet with one vent cut in each and chill in the fridge.

Make the pork pies: Grease mini tins and line them with the hot water crust, stretching it up the sides and patching any holes (a little thinner than for a big pie so it cooks in the air fryer). Fill with pork, make a hollow, add about half a teaspoon of Branston, close it over, add lids, vent, and brush the lip with egg wash so the lid seals. Chill about 15 minutes.
Make the mince pies: Line six tins with ready-rolled pastry, add the mincemeat, add little lids.
Make the brie bites: Cut squares of puff pastry, put a cube of brie and a little cranberry in the middle, brush lightly with egg wash and pinch the corners together.
Egg wash: Egg wash the sausage rolls, pork pies and mince pies, and sprinkle sesame seeds on the sausage rolls.

Load the air fryer: Put the pork pies and mince pies in the top basket on bake (not air fry), and the mince pies under the sausage rolls on a vented tray in the bottom basket. Set bake at 165°C for 18 minutes.

Finish: After that, the host bakes the sausage rolls at 175°C for about 6 minutes to crisp, and the brie bites for 8 minutes at 165°C. Let the pies cool before removing them from the tins (the host's pies stuck).
Serve: Serve warm. The host found the sausage rolls and brie bites excellent and says to skip the Branston in the pork pie.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Bsfxm6ARL9U
Uploaded 2025-11-28.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: A 2-chamber, 10.8L double-stack air fryer that lets you cook more in less space; Bake 18–22 min 165°C; 6 mins 175°C to crisp; Bake  8 mins 165°C.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: The BEST Homemade Tartare Sauce — Ready in 5 Minutes!!
ingredients: Dill pickles or relish, finely chopped — 2 tbsp (20 g)
Finely chopped shallot or onion — 1 tsp (5 g)
Salt — ⅛ tsp or to taste (0.5 g) (optional)
Fresh dill or parsley, chopped — 1 tbsp (3 g) (optional)
steps: Chop: Finely chop the onion (or shallot), the pickles, the capers and the fresh dill, as fine or as chunky as you like.
Mix: Put the mayonnaise in a bowl and stir in the onion, capers, pickle and dill, the pepper (the host uses white pepper), a teaspoon of Dijon and a squirt of lemon juice.
Season: Taste; it's salty enough from the capers, but add a little salt if you like.
Chill: Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes so the flavours meld. It keeps a couple of days.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_JOUOyVUjbY
Uploaded 2025-11-28.

recipes.title: These Apple Pie Egg Rolls Are Outrageously Good!
ingredients: Egg roll wrappers (spring roll wrappers in the UK) — 10–15 pieces
Egg, beaten (for sealing) — 1 large (the host uses a cornstarch-and-water glue; amounts not stated)
Melted butter — 1 tsp (5 ml) (optional, but improves browning)
Caramel Dip (shown in the video; quantities not stated):
Butter (a couple of tablespoons), sweetened condensed milk, brown sugar, salt and a splash of vanilla
steps: Cook the apples: Melt the butter in a pan, add the peeled, diced apples, a little salt, a splash of vanilla, about 3 tablespoons of brown sugar, nutmeg and cinnamon. Cook for about 8 minutes, moving them around, so the apples are cooked but still chunky (or mash a few for a little sauce).
Cool the filling: Let it cool completely, or it will make the wraps soggy.
Heat the oven: Preheat to 200°C.
Fill and roll: Put a little filling on each egg roll wrapper, bring in the sides, roll up and seal with the glue (egg, or the host's cornflour-and-water). Place seam-side down on a tray.
Coat: Mix the sugar and cinnamon. Brush the rolls with butter and sprinkle with the cinnamon sugar.
Bake: Bake for 15–18 minutes until crisp and coloured.

Make the caramel: Melt a couple of tablespoons of butter with sweetened condensed milk, brown sugar, a little salt and a splash of vanilla, and cook for about 8 minutes, stirring so nothing catches. Cool a little. (The host says it lasts about 3 weeks in the fridge.)
Serve: Brush the baked rolls with a little melted butter, and serve with the caramel dip or drizzled over.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LQ2B6nyFrtg
Uploaded 2025-11-27.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: 400°F / 200°C for 15–18 minutes.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: How to Make Stem GINGER Cubes in Syrup 18 Month Shelf Life!
ingredients: Fresh young ginger root, chopped — 250 g (8.8 oz)
Lemon juice — a few drops (optional, to balance sweetness)
2 kg batch (shelf-stable commercial style; yields about 8–10 medium jars; the batch made in the video):
Fresh young ginger root, chopped — 2 kg (4.4 lb)
Optional: replace up to 500 g of sugar with light brown sugar for deeper caramel flavour.
steps: Peel the ginger: Use young ginger (old ginger won't absorb the syrup). Take the skin off with a spoon; it flakes off.
Cube: Cut the ginger into small cubes of about 8 to 10 mm.
Boil three times: Put the ginger in cold water, bring to a boil and boil for 15 minutes, drain, and repeat with fresh cold water, three boils in total, to remove the bitterness.

Day 1 syrup: In a pan bring 2 litres of water and 1 kg of sugar to a gentle boil, stirring to dissolve. Add the ginger, bring to a boil and simmer for 30 minutes, stirring so the bottom comes to the top.
Rest: Turn off the flame and leave it to cool, covered with a towel, for about 12 hours.

Day 2: Add another 1 kg of sugar, about a litre of water and 60 ml of lemon juice, stir, bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for 1 hour, stirring, until it has cooked down a little but still has a runny syrup.
Sterilise jars: Sterilise jars in the oven at 140°C for about 20 minutes and keep them hot (syrup shouldn't drop below about 90°).
Jar: Fill the jars with more ginger than syrup, but enough syrup to cover, and put lids on.
Water bath: Process in a boiling water bath, with water above the jars, for 15–20 minutes. The host says the sealed jars are shelf-stable for 18 months; once open, they last 3 months in the fridge.
Use: Use in baking and desserts. The leftover syrup is excellent on ice cream.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vxaoyN56CH4
Uploaded 2025-11-27.

recipes.title: This Potato “Lasagna” Might Be Better Than the Real One…!
ingredients: Potatoes, thin sliced 2–3 mm — 900 g–1 kg
Italian seasoning — 1 tsp (or dried oregano / dried thyme)
Condensed soup, mushroom or chicken — 1 can (295 g / 10.5 oz)
Parmesan or cheddar, grated — 60 g (½ cup)
steps: Prep: Dice the onion, mince the garlic, remove the spinach from the stalks and rinse it, and slice the potatoes about 3 mm thick (if thicker, add about 10 minutes to the cooking) and the mushrooms.

Cook the filling: In a pan heat a little olive oil and butter, cook the onion with a tiny bit of salt and pepper to take out the rawness, then add the garlic. Cook the mushrooms until most of the moisture is gone and they have a little brown, then wilt the spinach in briefly. Take off the heat.
Make the sauce: Mix the condensed mushroom soup with the milk, pepper, nutmeg, a teaspoon of Dijon and the Italian herbs (the host uses oregano and thyme if you don't have Italian herbs).

Layer: In an 8 by 8 dish put a layer of potatoes, some sauce, a layer of the spinach and mushroom, and a little mozzarella; squash it down, then repeat with more sauce, spinach-mushroom, mozzarella, Parmesan and cheddar.
Top: Finish with potatoes, the last of the sauce, mozzarella, Parmesan and a little black pepper.
Cover and bake: Cover loosely with foil so the potatoes steam, and bake for 45 minutes at 180°C / 350°F (the host's was 35–40 minutes at about 190°C).
Uncover: Remove the foil and bake 30–35 minutes more until golden and bubbling.
Rest and serve: Let it set about 10 minutes before cutting. It is a loose layered dish since no flour is used in the sauce.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fcj4YX7qCYM
Uploaded 2025-11-26.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Cover with foil and bake 45 min at 180°C / 350°F.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: You’ll Never Make Pork the Same Way Again! | Apple-Stuffed Pork Loin
ingredients: Fresh or dried sage — 1 tsp (1 g)
Apple, peeled, cored, thinly sliced — 1 medium (about 150 g)
Fresh sage, chopped — 1 tbsp (or 1 tsp dried)
Potatoes (the host leaves the skins on); veggies (carrots, sprouts, apple) with olive oil.
Pork roasting juices and browned bits from the pan, if you have them
Dry apple cider — 1 cup (240 ml) (or sparkling apple juice for a non-alcoholic version)
Chicken or pork stock — 1 cup (240 ml)
Optional: 1 tsp (5 ml) cream or knob of butter to finish
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to about 190°C.
Par-boil the potatoes: Boil the scrubbed, skin-on potatoes in salted water for 8 minutes only, then drain and shake in the colander to roughen the edges.

Make the stuffing: Cook the onion in butter with a little salt (and pepper) until the rawness is gone, then bloom the thyme and sage in the pan. Add it to the breadcrumbs with about 2 tablespoons of water and mix. It should be a fairly dry stuffing that takes on the juices as it cooks.
Prep the apple: Peel and slice an apple into reasonably thick slices.
Cut the slits: Cut slits into the pork loin about 2 cm apart, not going all the way to the bottom.
Stuff: Push stuffing down into each slit, then tuck apple slices in alongside it.
Tie: Tie the loin with string (any simple knots, so it holds together).
Season: Rub the pork with a little olive oil, salt, pepper and sage.
Roast: Roast uncovered for about 1 hour 20–30 minutes (the host's was about an hour and a half) or until the internal temperature reaches 68–70°C / 155–158°F. Baste the top if you like.

Add the stuffing tin and veg: Put the extra stuffing in a small tin with a little butter on top. Toss the potatoes in oil (rosemary salt), and the carrots, sprouts and apple pieces in oil and salt, and add them to the oven about 40 minutes before the end; roast for 45–55 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.

Make the gravy: Melt the butter, cook out the flour, then add the cider and stock, stir until thick, and add Dijon, pepper, salt and a little apple sauce, apple jelly or honey. Stir in the pork roasting juices if you have them.
Rest and serve: Take the pork out, cover with foil to rest, cut the string, slice and serve with roast potatoes, veg, the stuffing and the gravy.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ncS4-gB5tjI
Uploaded 2025-11-25.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Roast uncovered for 1 hour 20 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes, or until internal temperature reaches 68–70 °C / 155–158 °F; Boil potatoes for 8 minutes, drain, and shake in the colander to roughen edges slightly; Roast for 45–55 minutes, turning halfway through, until golden and crisp.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: You’ll Make This Creamy Chicken Potato Dinner EVERY Week!
ingredients: Chicken breast, cubed 1.5–2 cm — 500 g (≈ 1.1 lb)
Mixed veg or peas — 150 g (1 cup)
Dried thyme or parsley — 1 tsp (1 g)
Salt (only if needed) — ¼ tsp (1.5 g)
Potatoes, peeled and sliced 0.3–0.5 cm — 500 g
Olive oil or melted butter — 1 tbsp (15 ml / 13 g)
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 190°C (375°F).
Brown the chicken: In a pan with a little oil (the host uses oil and butter) quickly fry the cubed chicken with salt and pepper, but only most of the way through; it finishes cooking in the dish.
Start the layers: Put the sliced onion in the baking dish, add the chicken.
Make the sauce: In a bowl mix the soup with about a cup of milk, thyme, pepper, garlic powder, paprika and the mustard.
Add veg and sauce: Add the mixed veg (and carrots), then pour the sauce over.
Top with potatoes: Lay the potato slices on top, sprinkling a little milk between layers (the host's tip so there is enough fluid to steam the potatoes). Season lightly with salt and pepper.
Bake covered: Cover with foil (it will bubble) and bake 35 minutes.

Bake uncovered: Remove the foil, dot the potatoes with a little butter and oil, add a fleck of cheddar if you like, and bake another 25–35 minutes until the potatoes are golden and the sauce is bubbling.
Serve: Serve with a little parsley on top.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2tbIHK1KwuQ
Uploaded 2025-11-24.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Cover with foil and bake at 190°C (375°F) for 35 minutes.

recipes.title: Gingerbread MILLIONAIRE'S Bars – Festive Twist on a Classic!
ingredients: Unsalted butter, melted — 115 g (1 US stick / 8 tbsp)
Golden syrup or molasses — 2 tbsp (40 g)
Golden syrup (or corn syrup) — 2 tbsp (40 g)
Ground ginger — ½ tsp (optional, for a spiced caramel twist)
Butter or coconut oil (for shine) — 1 tbsp (15 g)
Oven 175°C (350°F). Tin: 20 × 20 cm (8 × 8 inch), lined with parchment (the host uses an oblong 10 × 7 tin).
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 175°C (350°F) and line the tin with parchment paper (no greasing).
Make the base dough: Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar, salt, cloves, cinnamon and ginger, then add the milk, melted butter and golden syrup and bring it together with a spoon into a dough.
Press into the tin: Press the dough into the tin with your hands and smooth it out.
Bake: Bake for 12–15 minutes until firm. Cool completely.

Make the caramel: In a pan melt together the sugar, a pinch of salt, butter, sweetened condensed milk and two tablespoons of golden syrup (and optional ginger). Cook low and slow for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and again so it doesn't stick.
Pour: Let the caramel cool a little, but keep it pourable, and pour over the base.
Chill: Cool, then chill in the fridge for at least an hour.
Melt the chocolate: Melt the chocolate with a splash of milk, off the flame, then stir in a little butter for gloss. Let it cool a little.
Top: Spread the chocolate over the caramel (the host adds uneven waves), with a sprinkle of sea salt if you like, and let it set in the fridge.
Cut: Lift out of the tin and cut with a warm knife.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UN7-jCUvX7o
Uploaded 2025-11-23.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 175°C (350°F). Line a 20x20 cm (8x8 inch) tin with parchment; Bake for 12–15 minutes until firm. Cool completely.

recipes.title: LORNE + BRU The Most Epic SCOTTISH Breakfast EVER!
ingredients: Ground pork (20–25% fat) — ½ lb (227 g)
Fine breadcrumbs — ½ US cup (60 g)
Cold water — ¼ US cup (60 ml)
Full-Can Irn-Bru Pop Rolls (330 ml can recipe, makes 12 large rolls):
Bread flour, or mixed with all-purpose/plain flour — 500 g
Instant yeast — 10 g (1 tbsp + ½ tsp)
Note: the tin was 10 × 10 inch per the description (the host also mentions an 8 × 8 tin with 9 balls).
steps: Mix the dough: Combine the flour (the host uses 50/50 plain and bread flour), salt, sugar and yeast, then stir in the can of Irn-Bru and the melted butter.
Knead: Knead in a stand mixer for about 8–10 minutes to a sticky orange dough.
First rise: Bring together into an oiled bowl, cover, and leave about an hour to an hour and a half until doubled.
Soak the crumbs: Stir the breadcrumbs into the water and let them rehydrate. This gives a better mouth feel.
Mix the sausage: Combine the beef, pork, salt, black and white pepper, nutmeg, coriander and the crumbs, and squash it together until it's a sticky meat mix (about 10 minutes).
Pack and chill: Pack the mixture tightly into a square tin and chill at least 4 hours (overnight is better, or freeze before cutting).
Shape the rolls: Deflate the dough and divide it into 9 to 12 balls, arranging them in the tin.
Second rise: Let them rise about 40 minutes somewhere warm.
Glaze and bake: Beat the egg yolk with the milk, brush gently over the tops, and bake at 190°C / 375°F for 14–18 minutes until golden (the host says 12–15 minutes). Cool.
Slice and fry: Slice the sausage 1.3–2 cm thick and fry in butter and oil for 3–4 minutes each side until a good crust forms and it's cooked through.
Serve: Put the sausage in the rolls, with brown sauce and a fried egg if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KC1dgNZXFic
Uploaded 2025-11-22.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Makes 12 large breakfast rolls; Bake at 190°C / 375°F for 14–18 minutes until golden.

recipes.title: EASY Cheesy GARLIC BOMB Pull Apart Bundt Bread with Hot Cheese Dip
ingredients: All-purpose / plain flour — 3 cups US (360 g)
Soft butter — ¼ cup US (60 g / 4 tbsp)
Mozzarella, shredded — ½ cup US (55 g)
Pinch of salt — ⅛ tsp (1 g)
Melted butter — ¼ cup US (60 g / 4 tbsp)
Fresh garlic, minced — 2 cloves (2 tsp / 8 g)
Pinch of salt — ⅛ tsp (1 g)
Hot Cheese Dip for the Centre (ramekin):
Cream cheese, softened — 1 cup US (225 g)
Parmesan, grated — ½ cup US (50 g)
Mayonnaise — ¼ cup US (60 ml / 4 tbsp)
steps: Bloom the yeast: Stir the sugar into the warm water, add the yeast and leave until it froths. If it doesn't, start again with fresh yeast.
Make the dough: Mix the all-purpose flour with the salt, add the yeast mixture and olive oil, and knead about 8–10 minutes (the host uses a stand mixer).
First rise: Put the dough in a greased bowl, cover, and leave somewhere warm for 1 hour or until doubled.
Make the filling: Mash the softened (not melted) butter with the garlic powder, dried parsley, salt and the mozzarella.
Divide and fill: Knock back the dough, divide it into about 8–12 pieces, roll into balls and flatten each. Put about a teaspoon of filling in each one and seal it up.
Fill the tin: Grease a bundt tin and arrange the balls seam side down, joined together.
Second rise: Cover and let rise 20–30 minutes until puffy.
Make the dip: Mix the cream cheese, garlic, Parmesan, chili flakes, black pepper, lemon juice, mayonnaise and mozzarella together and spoon into ramekins.
Bake: Put the bundt tin and the ramekins on a tray and bake at 170–175°C (340°F) for 30–35 minutes until the bread is golden and the dip is bubbling.
Glaze: Mix the melted butter, fresh garlic, parsley (and Parmesan, salt) and brush over the bread as soon as it comes out, letting it run down. Brush on more once it's glazed.
Serve: Turn out, keep the dips hot, then tear and dip.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AGjUMpJOFlI
Uploaded 2025-11-21.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake at 170–175°C / 340°F for 30–35 minutes until golden.

recipes.title: Easiest Italian Sausage & Pepper Bake  - Rich Tomato Basil Sauce!
ingredients: Hot water or stock — 2½ cups (600 ml)
Dried basil — 1 tsp (1 g) (the host used Italian seasoning)
Crushed chili flakes — ¼ tsp (0.5 g) (optional)
Salt — ¼ tsp (1.5 g) (taste and adjust)
Dried short pasta (penne, rigatoni, shells, fusilli) — 250 g (9 oz)
steps: Prep the tray: Preheat the oven to 200°C / 400°F. Put the sausages in a tray with the sliced onion, peppers and a little olive oil, add salt and pepper if you like, and stir.
Bake the sausages first: Bake for 20 minutes to brown them slightly.

Make the sauce: Whisk the condensed soup with the water (rinse the can out with some of it), the chili flakes, black pepper, oregano and Italian seasoning, olive oil, balsamic vinegar, tomato paste and a little sugar. Go easy on salt, since the soup is salty.
Add the pasta and sauce: Take the tray out, turn the sausages so the other side browns, and stir in the dry pasta and the sauce, making sure pasta and sausages are under the liquid.

Bake again: Return to the oven. After about 15 minutes, stir (you can slice the sausages into coins and put them back in), then bake a further 20 minutes or so (description: 25–30 minutes) until the pasta is cooked and the sauce is thick and starting to dry out at the edges.
Finish and serve: Top with Parmesan and chopped fresh basil. For a baked cheese top, add cheddar and bake another 5 minutes. Serve with garlic bread if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YzUmXz-q2O4
Uploaded 2025-11-20.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Set to 200°C / 400°F; Bake the sausages first for 20 minutes to brown them slightly; Bake a further bake 25–30 minutes, after pasta and sauce.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: This Creamy Potato & Pea Soup Will Warm Your Soul!
ingredients: Potatoes, peeled and diced — 500 g (17.6 oz)
Fresh rosemary, finely chopped — 1 tsp (2 g)
Cream or vegan alternative — 120 ml (½ cup)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Extra peas, cream swirl, or chopped herbs
steps: Sweat the veg: In a pan with the olive oil, cook the carrots, celery and onion with a little salt and black pepper for about 5 minutes to soften and take the rawness out of the onions. Add the butter (the host's addition for flavour).
Add garlic and spices: Clear a space and cook the garlic briefly, then stir in the smoked paprika, chili flakes, oregano, thyme, rosemary and nutmeg and let them bloom in with the veg.

Add potatoes and stock: Stir in the potatoes and the vegetable stock (or chicken stock). Bring up to the boil, then reduce to a simmer, uncovered, for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then so nothing sticks.
Add the peas: Add the frozen peas. Keep a few pieces of potato and some peas aside for garnish.
Blend: Blend with a stick blender until thick but still with some lumps (add a little boiling water if too thick).
Add cream: Stir in the cream (about 120 ml), warm gently, and check the seasoning.
Serve: Serve topped with the reserved potato and peas.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4MTwnfgJUYU
Uploaded 2025-11-19.

recipes.title: Sweet & Savoury Char Siu Chicken – The Ultimate Weeknight Roast
ingredients: Chicken thighs — 4 pieces (≈ 600 g / 1.3 lb) (the host uses bone-in, skin-on)
Honey or maple syrup — 1 tbsp (20 g / 20 ml)
Red food colouring — a few drops (optional)
steps: Make the marinade: Mix the garlic, ginger, five-spice, hoisin, light and dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, sesame oil, maple syrup or honey and sugar. Add a little red colouring if you want that takeaway colour (wear a glove, since it stains).
Marinate: Coat the chicken thoroughly and leave for about 4 hours (overnight is better).
Prep the tray: Preheat the oven to 200°C / 400°F. Line a tray with foil and fit a rack, and lay the chicken on top (skin side down first).
First roast: Roast about 20–25 minutes.

Baste and flip: Baste with more marinade, flip, and cook for another 10–20 minutes until slightly charred, the skin is crisp and the juices run clear. The sugars catch easily, so watch it. (The host notes you can boil leftover marinade as a glaze, because of the raw chicken juices.)
Shine and serve: Spoon the chicken's own juices over for extra shine and serve sliced over rice or noodles.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_JSvMX3jy8I
Uploaded 2025-11-18.

recipes.title: The Easiest Bakewell Ever – No Pastry Needed!
ingredients: Tinned strawberry pie filling — 200–250 g (about 1 US cup, enough to cover the base in a thin layer)
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 170°C / 325°F.
Mix the dry ingredients: Combine the plain flour, baking powder, sugar, ground almonds and a little salt.
Make the batter: Add the egg, melted butter, milk and almond extract and stir to a pourable batter. If it's too thick, add a little more milk or water.
Add the filling: Spoon the pie filling into the glass dish (jam also works; lemon curd or cherries are other options the host mentions).
Pour the batter: Pour the batter over the filling, going round the sides first, then the middle, so it holds the filling in.
Top: Scatter flaked almonds over the top with a pinch of sugar.
Bake: Bake for about 35–42 minutes at 170°C / 325°F until the top is golden, risen and sponge-like. It may sink in the middle, which is fine.
Serve: Cool a little, then serve with cream or ice cream.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2ojLTTjCL5A
Uploaded 2025-11-17.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven to: 170°C / 325°F; Bake for 35–42 minutes at 170°C / 325°F, until the top is golden, risen, and sponge-like.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: One Bite and You’ll Understand Why TEXAS Loves This Lasagna!
ingredients: Black beans, rinsed — 1 cup (170 g drained)
Flour or corn tortillas — 8 medium (about 20 cm / 8 in each)
Shredded cheese (Cheddar, Monterey Jack, or Tex-Mex blend) — 2 cups (200 g)
Jalapeño or green chilli, minced — 1 (optional seeds)
steps: Make the salsa: Mix the tomatoes, onion, chilli, coriander, garlic, salt, pepper, cumin, smoked paprika, tomato paste, a splash of water and the lime juice (or use a jar of salsa).
Brown the beef: In a pan with a little oil, break up the beef with salt and pepper and cook off the water that comes out. Clear a space for the garlic, add the onions and cook.
Season: Add the taco seasoning, then the tomato sauce, black beans, corn and the salsa. Cook a little to bring it together, but don't dry it out; keep some juiciness. Take off the heat.

Layer: Preheat the oven to 190°C / 375°F. Spread a little of the filling in the dish, then add a layer of tortillas cut to fit (use the trimmings too), sour cream, filling and cheese. Repeat, finishing with a top layer of filling and more cheese.
Bake covered: Tent loosely with foil (or oil the foil so the cheese doesn't stick) and bake 25 minutes.
Bake uncovered: Remove the foil and bake about 10 minutes more until golden and bubbling.
Serve: Cool a little, then serve with sour cream, cilantro and a squeeze of lime.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=f5O8XstcYm0
Uploaded 2025-11-16.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Cover with foil and bake at 375 °F (190 °C) for 25 minutes.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: This Pie Has Australia Divided… Curried SAUSAGES in a Crust!
ingredients: Tomato ketchup — 1 tbsp (15 g) (optional, for sweetness)
Worcestershire sauce — 1 tsp (5 ml) (optional, for depth)
Apple, peeled and finely diced — 1 (optional, old-school style)
Butter or oil — 1 tbsp (15 g), more if needed
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Cornstarch — 1 tbsp mixed with 2 tbsp (30 ml) cold water (optional, for extra thickness)
Ready-rolled shortcrust pastry — 1 sheet (for base and sides)
steps: Brown the sausages: Cook the sausages in a pan to brown and nearly cook through, then take them out to cool.
Cook the veg: Drain off excess oil, add butter, and cook the onion and carrot with salt and pepper until the onion's rawness is gone.
Add flour and curry: Stir in the flour and curry powder and cook a minute to cook out the rawness and bloom the spices.

Add stock and flavourings: Add the beef stock, Worcestershire, ketchup, golden raisins and diced apple, and cook it down thick and sturdy so it holds in the pie. If it isn't thick enough, stir in the cornstarch mixed with water.

Finish the filling: Add the frozen peas and the cut-up sausages and stir. Cool the filling completely before it goes into the pastry. (The host mentions you can add some cold mashed potato to hold the filling together.)
Line the tins: Roll out the shortcrust and line the pie tins up the sides and bottom, trimming and patching as needed.
Fill: Pack the filling in firmly.
Add the lid: Dampen the edge with egg wash, cut a couple of vents in a puff pastry top, stretch it over the filling and fold the edges in.
Glaze and bake: Brush with egg wash, put on a tray and bake at 200°C / 400°F for 25–35 minutes until golden and crisp.
Serve: Let the pies rest a minute, pop out of the tins, and serve with tomato sauce (ketchup).
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6d3XoN6LW6E
Uploaded 2025-11-15.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake in a preheated oven at 200 °C / 400 °F for 25–30 minutes, until golden and crisp.

recipes.title: This Doner Kebab Will Ruin Takeaways Forever!!
ingredients: Tomato paste — 1 tbsp (optional, for colour and richness)
Squeeze of lemon juice or dash of hot sauce (optional, for tang)
Greek yoghurt (or thick plain yoghurt) — ½ cup (120 ml / 120 g)
Salad: red onion, tomato, lettuce, cucumber (amounts not stated); optional Sriracha.
steps: Mix the meat: Combine the lamb, beef, spices, salt, pepper, grated garlic, grated onion (with some juice squeezed out, not all), tomato paste and yoghurt. Mix by hand about 6–7 minutes until nice and tacky and fully incorporated.
Rest: Leave about 20 minutes (or overnight) so the flavours come together.
Shape: Spread the mix thinly on parchment paper, squash it flat, and roll up tightly. Place the roll in a deep tin, since it will release a lot of fat.
Bake: Preheat the oven to 250°C / 450°F. Bake the roll for 15 minutes (the host cooks 15–20).
Drain and broil: Drain the excess liquid, unwrap the roll, break it up or leave in chunks on a baking tray, and broil (grill) for 5–7 minutes until browned and slightly crisp on the edges.
Make the flatbreads: Mix the self-raising flour, salt and yoghurt into a dough, split into four, roll out and cook in a non-stick pan until it bubbles, flip, and keep warm under a tea towel.
Make the garlic sauce: Mix the yoghurt, mayo, pepper, salt, parsley, garlic and lemon (or hot sauce).
Assemble: Fill flatbreads with salad, meat and the garlic sauce, and wrap in foil or parchment if you want the takeaway style.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=hox9fxT1OZc
Uploaded 2025-11-14.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 250 °C / 450 °F. Place the roll in an oven-safe dish and bake for 15 minutes.

recipes.title: Stretch One Tin into Ten! CORNED BEEF Rolls Everyone’s Talking About!
ingredients: Tinned corned beef — 1 tin (340 g / about 12 oz)
Milk — 2 tbsp (30 ml), or water, over the breadcrumbs
Grated cheese — 30 g (2 tbsp) (optional, for richness)
Puff pastry — 1 sheet (approx. 320 g / 11 oz), cut into 4.5 × 5 inch pieces
Sesame seeds — a few (the host adds on top; amount not stated)
Oven: 200°C / 400°F (fan 180°C / 350°F). Line a tray with baking paper.
steps: Soak the crumbs: Mix the breadcrumbs with a couple of tablespoons of milk to rehydrate a little.
Cook the onion: Fry the finely diced onion in a little oil with a pinch of salt to take out the rawness, then let it cool.

Mix the filling: Mash up the corned beef, then mix in the mashed potato, breadcrumbs, pepper, mustard powder, dried parsley, Worcestershire sauce, the cooled onions and a sprinkle of cheddar. If your mash is very moist, increase the crumbs from 30 g to 50 g. No extra salt is needed, since corned beef is salty.
Preheat: Heat the oven to 200°C / 400°F and line a tray with parchment.
Fill and roll: Spoon filling onto the pastry, brush a little beaten egg on the edge, roll it up and place seam side down on the tray.
Glaze: Cut three slits in the top for steam, brush with egg wash and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Bake: Bake 20–25 minutes until puffed and golden brown.
Serve: Serve warm with ketchup or whatever you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Eke37-Guj_8
Uploaded 2025-11-13.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven: 200 °C / 400 °F (fan 180 °C / 350 °F). Line a tray with baking paper; Bake for 20–25 minutes until puffed and golden brown.

recipes.title: EASY Old Fashioned Batter Top Apple Pie - No Pastry Needed!
ingredients: Apples (peeled, cored, chopped) — 3 medium (about 450 g / 1 lb / 3 cups chopped)
Extra sugar, for sprinkling — 1 tbsp (12 g)
Oven: 180°C (350°F). Tin: 8-inch (20 cm) round or square.
steps: Prep the apples: Peel, core and cube the apples (any size) into the tin or a tub.
Season the apples: Mix in the sugar, cinnamon and lemon juice (the host also adds a pinch of salt).
Heat the oven: Preheat to 180°C (350°F).

Make the batter: Whisk the flour, baking powder, sugar, vanilla, milk, egg, melted butter and a pinch of salt to a thickish batter, not as runny as pancake batter. Add a little more milk or water if needed.
Top: Spoon the batter evenly over the apples in the 8-inch tin (apples poking through is fine). Sprinkle sugar on top and, the old-fashioned way, dot with butter.
Bake: Bake 35–40 minutes until golden and a skewer in the centre comes out clean.
Serve: Serve warm with cream or custard. The host notes it also works with apple and blackberry or with pears.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UB_0tTZ_-fs
Uploaded 2025-11-12.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Heat oven to 180°C (350°F); Bake for 35–40 minutes, until golden and a skewer inserted into the centre comes out clean.

recipes.title: Johnny Marzetti  - One of the most important dishes in modern American cooking!
ingredients: For an 8 × 8 in / 20 × 20 cm dish, makes 4 servings.
Green bell pepper, chopped — 1 medium (150 g)
Salt — 1 tsp (6 g), or to taste
Dried macaroni (or rotini) — 1 UK cup (≈ 140 g raw)
Shredded cheddar or mild cheese blend — 1 UK cup (≈ 120 g)
Extra cheese for topping — ½ UK cup (≈ 60 g)
Worcestershire sauce — 2 tbsp (30 ml), for depth
Sliced mushrooms — ½ cup (75 g), added with the onion
Swap ¼ of the beef for Italian sausage for a richer flavour
steps: Boil the pasta: Cook the elbow macaroni in salted boiling water until just cooked, then drain (no pasta water needed).

Start the base: In a pan with olive oil cook the onion and pepper for a couple of minutes to loosen them and remove the rawness. Clear a space and cook the garlic about 30 seconds, then add the ground beef and break it up (the host's was frozen and defrosted in the pan).
Season: Add salt and pepper to taste (plus Worcestershire and dried oregano if using the later version).
Make the sauce: Add the tinned tomatoes with their juice (chopped), the tomato paste and the sugar, and cook uncovered for about 10 minutes into a thick, tomatoey sauce.
Combine: Heat the oven to 175°C / 350°F. Stir the pasta into the sauce.
Layer: Put half in the dish, add mozzarella and cheddar, then the rest and more cheese on top.
Bake covered: Set the dish on a tray (it may bubble over), cover loosely with foil and bake 20 minutes.
Brown: Remove the foil and bake another 5–10 minutes until the cheese is bubbly and golden.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=27jBJ41vsC0
Uploaded 2025-11-11.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven 175 °C / 350 °F.

recipes.title: Chicken Curry Hand Pies with a Creamy Twist – The Ultimate Flaky Snack!
ingredients: Chicken breast, small cubes — 400 g / 14 oz (about 2 cups diced)
Fresh coriander or parsley, chopped — 1 tbsp (3 g)
Ready-rolled shortcrust or puff pastry — about 500 g / 1 lb, cut 4.5 × 5 inch
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 200°C / 400°F.
Brown the chicken: Cube the chicken small (it shrinks) and cook in oil with salt and pepper until the water cooks off and it takes a little golden colour. Take it out of the pan.
Cook the aromatics: Melt the butter, cook the onion until the rawness goes, then add the garlic and ginger.
Add the spices and flour: Bloom the curry powder and turmeric, then stir in the flour and cook out the rawness, keeping it moving, to form a curry paste.
Make the sauce: Add the evaporated milk (not sweetened condensed) and chicken stock over a low flame and stir until thick and creamy.
Finish the filling: Return the chicken, add the peas and coriander, and check the seasoning. Let it cool completely.
Fill: On a lined tray, put filling on the pastry pieces. Cut slits in a top piece so it stretches over like a lattice, then lay it over and press down.
Seal: Crimp the edges with a fork and brush all over with egg wash.
Bake: Bake 20–25 minutes until golden brown.
Cool and serve: Cool a minute on a rack before cutting.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=weqAyszTxIo
Uploaded 2025-11-10.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 200 °C / 400 °F.

recipes.title: Fail Proof Gluten FREE YORKSHIRE Pudding Recipe – Crisp, Airy, Delicious!
ingredients: Gluten-free plain flour blend — 100 g (¾ cup US / ⅔ cup UK) (the blend recipe is in the next entries: xluIs26cxic)
Vegetable oil — 1 tbsp (15 ml), plus extra for the tins
steps: Make the batter: Whisk the salt and flour with the eggs, milk and water into a batter.
Rest: Let the batter sit about 15 minutes to rehydrate the flour. Heat the oven to 230°C / 450°F.
Warm the oil: After about 10 minutes, put a little oil (about ½ tsp per cup) in the tin and warm it in the oven for 5 minutes. (The host says next time he would only warm it a minute or two.)
Fill: Give the batter a stir and pour into the warm tin.
Bake: Bake 20–25 minutes for mini puddings, or 30–35 minutes in a large tin, pulling them before the tops burn.
Serve: Serve warm; the host eats them with mustard.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RAAL9VfvvC8
Uploaded 2025-11-09.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven to 230 °C / 450 °F (210 °C fan); Bake 20–25 minutes (mini puddings) or 30–35 minutes (large tin).

recipes.title: Gluten Free Flour Blend
ingredients: To make 1 kilo, multiply all by 10.
steps: Combine: Put the rice flour, cornstarch and tapioca flour in a bowl.
Mix: Mix until evenly blended. (The host says gluten-free flour is normally about 58–59% rice flour with the remainder corn flour or arrowroot and tapioca.)
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xluIs26cxic
Uploaded 2025-11-09.
Short video, brief method.

recipes.title: Gluten Free Baking Powder
ingredients: Bicarbonate of soda / baking soda (base) — 1 part
Cornstarch or arrowroot starch (to absorb moisture and keep it free-flowing) — 1 part
In the video the host measures with a teaspoon: 2 tsp cream of tartar, 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda, 1 tsp cornflour, which makes roughly 1 tablespoon.
steps: Mix: Mix all the ingredients thoroughly in a small bowl.
Store: Store in an airtight jar away from heat or moisture.
Use: Use 1 tsp per 120 g (1 cup) of flour in most recipes.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=X8bM8iEz57c
Uploaded 2025-11-09.

recipes.title: Golden Pear & Caramel Tart – Dessert Perfection!
ingredients: For the Pastry (or use ready-rolled, as in the video):
Unsalted butter, chilled and cubed — ½ cup (115 g)
Ripe but firm pears, peeled and halved — 3
Caramel sauce, for brushing the base — 2 tbsp (30 ml)
Crushed pecans or almonds for garnish (optional)
steps: Line the tin: Roll out the pastry to fit the 8-inch tin, tuck it in with the overhang on, dock it, and add screwed-up parchment with baking beads.
Blind bake: Bake at 190°C / 375°F for 15 minutes, remove the beads and bake another 10 minutes until golden. Cool, then trim.
Poach the pears: Heat the water with vanilla, sugar and cinnamon, add the pears and poach 10–12 minutes until soft but not soggy. Cool slightly and slice.
Lower the oven: Drop the oven to 175°C / 350°F.
Make the caramel: Put the water and sugar in a pan and don't stir; let it go amber. Off the heat, swirl in the butter, then whisk in the cream as it bubbles, and add the sea salt.
Assemble: Brush the base with some of the cooling caramel (about 2 tbsp), arrange the pear slices, and spoon some caramel between and over the pears, saving some for drizzling.
Bake: Bake at 175°C / 350°F for 15–20 minutes until lightly caramelised.
Serve: Cool so it sets up, pop out of the tin, and serve with extra caramel (and cream or ice cream).
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=poR9cJJDKhU
Uploaded 2025-11-08.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake blind at 375°F (190°C) for 15 minutes. Remove beans and bake for another 10 minutes until golden. Let cool; Bake at 350°F (175°C) for 15–20 minutes until lightly caramelised.

recipes.title: Move Over Mac & Cheese – This Cheesy Cauliflower Bake Wins Every Time!
ingredients: Cauliflower, cut into florets — 1 large (about 1 kg / 2.2 lb)
Double cream (heavy cream) — 200 ml (7 fl oz)
Salt — ½ tsp (3 g) (adjust to taste)
Streaky bacon, cooked crisp and chopped — 6 rashers (≈ 120 g / 4.2 oz)
Parmesan cheese, grated (for topping) — 2 tbsp (15 g)
Oven: 190°C / 375°F. The host uses an 8 × 8 glass dish.
steps: Cook the bacon: Fry the streaky bacon (not too crisp), then chop it up.
Start the potatoes: Prick the potatoes with a fork, cut halfway round, and microwave 10 minutes. Rub with a little olive oil and sea salt and put in the oven.
Boil the cauliflower: Boil (or steam) the florets in salted water for a short time, then drain into the baking dish. Heat the oven to about 190°C.

Make the cheese sauce: Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook out the rawness, then add the milk and cream. Season with pepper (nutmeg if you like), a teaspoon of English mustard, the garlic powder and paprika.
Add cheese: Stir in most of the cheddar and the mozzarella (keep some back for topping), then the bacon and the cream cheese.
Assemble: Pour over the cauliflower, top with a little mozzarella and cheddar, the panko mixed with melted butter, and the grated Parmesan.
Bake: Bake on a tray alongside the potatoes at 190°C / 375°F for 20–25 minutes until golden, bubbling and crispy on top.
Serve: Split the jacket potato, spoon the bake over, and top with a little bacon and something green. For a vegetarian version, leave out the bacon.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fW_7M3BJJew
Uploaded 2025-11-07.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake at 190°C / 375°F for 20–25 minutes, until golden, bubbling, and crispy on top.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Traditional British Egg Sauce – The Forgotten Classic for Fish & Ham
ingredients: English mustard or Dijon — 1 tsp (5 ml), optional (the host uses about ½ tsp Coleman's)
Hard-boiled eggs, peeled and chopped — 3 large
A small squeeze of lemon juice (optional, for brightness)
Optional to serve (amounts not stated): ham, asparagus cooked in butter, Parmesan.
steps: Boil the eggs: Hard-boil the eggs, then peel and chop them as big or small as you like.
Make the roux: Melt the butter, stir in the flour with the white pepper and salt, and cook out the flour without rushing (turn the heat down if the pan is too hot).
Add mustard and milk: Stir in the mustard, then add all the milk at once and stir gently as it thickens. If it gets too thick, add a splash of milk.
Fold in the egg: Fold in the chopped egg and just warm it through over a very low flame.
Finish: Optionally stir in a splash of cream and a knob of butter, then the parsley.
Serve: Serve warm with ham and asparagus (the host blanches packet ham for a minute and cooks asparagus in butter, adding a squirt of lemon). A little white pepper on top.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Dh3PNtXVCvw
Uploaded 2025-11-06.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Easiest Clarified Butter Ever  - Just Hot Water & Butter!
ingredients: Unsalted butter — 225 g (1 cup / 16 tbsp / 8 oz) (≈ 250 ml melted)
Boiling water — enough to fill a large bowl halfway (approx. 1 litre / 4 cups)
steps: Set up: Put the butter (a pack) in a heatproof bowl and pour boiling water around/into the bowl as in the video, so the butter melts gently.
Cover and wait: Put the lid on and leave it alone for a good 5 minutes or so.
Separate: Take the lid off. The butter will have separated: the milk solids drop to the bottom, and a little skin may sit on top.
Strain: Strain through a sieve lined with a cloth into a glass jar. If you can see faint solids, strain again for pure clarified butter.
Store: Keeps on the counter about two weeks, or in the fridge for one month.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kuTpzPY1BM0
Uploaded 2025-11-06.

recipes.title: Crispy ITALIAN Chicken Meets Caprese – The Irresistible Italian Twist You’ll Crave!
ingredients: Boneless, skinless chicken breasts — 2 (about 1½ lb / 680 g)
All-purpose / plain flour — ½ cup (65 g)
Grated Parmesan cheese — ¼ cup (25 g)
Dried Italian seasoning — amount not stated
Salt and freshly ground black pepper — to taste
Ripe tomatoes, thinly sliced (or cherry tomatoes) — 2 medium
steps: Prep the chicken: Butterfly the breasts roughly halfway through so they are about the same thickness (or pound them out).
Season: Season the chicken itself with salt, pepper, paprika and garlic powder, on both sides, then dredge in flour so the seasoning is trapped on the chicken.
Egg and crumb: Dip in beaten egg, sprinkle with a little Parmesan and Italian seasoning, then press into the breadcrumbs. Let the breaded chicken rest while it sticks.
Fry: Shallow-fry in oil over a moderate flame (not too high so the inside cooks), turning a couple of times, until golden. Drain on a tray.
Top: Put tomato slices and mozzarella on the chicken, with a little more Parmesan if you like.
Broil: Put under the broiler (grill) until the mozzarella just softens, without melting all over.
