Serve: Drizzle with balsamic glaze and top with fresh basil. The host suggests serving it with roasted vegetables or over pasta.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gYs_7uSQsks
Uploaded 2025-11-05.

recipes.title: Balsamic glaze perfect for drizzling!
ingredients: Brown sugar or honey — 2 tbsp (25 g)
Cracked black pepper — ½ tsp (2 g) (optional)
Dried thyme — 1 tsp (optional, for depth; the host uses it in the video)
steps: Combine: Put the balsamic vinegar, brown sugar, black pepper and thyme in a pan.
Reduce: Bring to the boil, then simmer about 15 minutes until it starts to thicken. Have a window open.
Check: It's ready when it coats the back of a spoon, but go only a little thicker, since it thickens as it cools. If it goes too thick, add a little water.
Strain: Strain out the thyme if you want a clear glaze.
Store: Cool, then keep in a bottle or jar in the fridge up to 1 month. If it sets too firm, warm the bottle in warm water.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BnNZqDkI98g
Uploaded 2025-11-05.

recipes.title: I Flipped a BRITISH CLASSIC — You Won’t Believe This Toad in the Hole!
ingredients: Olive oil — 1 tbsp (15 ml) (the host also adds butter to the dish; amount not stated)
Potatoes, peeled and cubed — 1 kg / 2.2 lb (about 6 medium)
Oven: 220°C / 425°F. Deep roasting dish approx. 10 × 8 inch (25 × 20 cm); the host uses a 10 × 10 tin.
steps: Make the batter: Whisk the flour, eggs, salt (and pepper if you like) and milk to a batter and set aside. Heat the oven to 220°C / 425°F.
Boil the potatoes: Boil the peeled, cubed potatoes in salted water.

Brown the sausages: Put the sausages in the dish with a little butter or oil and bake about 10 minutes, shaking so they brown all round. They are not cooked fully, because they finish in the dish. Take them out.
Mash: Mash the potatoes with butter, milk, salt and pepper (and a little cheddar if you like).
Build the base: Put the mash into the dish with the buttery sausage juices, compact it and fluff the top so the batter can sink in.
Add the sausages and batter: Tuck the sausages down into the mash, then pour the batter over so it comes over the top without lifting the sausages.
Bake: Bake 30–35 minutes until the batter is golden, crisp and puffed and the sausages are cooked through (75°C / 165°F).
Serve: Serve with peas and onion gravy. The host's onion gravy: fry sliced onions in butter and oil until coloured, add gravy granules (or a cube) and water, and cook until it thickens.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_VzJUPG7WKE
Uploaded 2025-11-04.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven to 220°C / 425°F. Deep roasting dish (approx. 10 × 8 inch / 25 × 20 cm); Bake for 30–35 minutes, until the batter is golden, crisp, and puffed and sausages are cooked through (75°C / 165°F).
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Corned Beef & Cabbage Pie – Classic Flavour, Easy & Delicious!
ingredients: Green or white cabbage, shredded — 3 cups (250 g / 9 oz)
Dijon or English mustard — 1 tbsp (15 g)
Beef stock or gravy — ½ cup (120 ml)
Pinch caraway seeds or any herbs of choice (optional)
Corned beef, diced or flaked — 1 can (340 g / 12 oz)
Egg, beaten, or milk for glaze — 1 egg
steps: Prep: Mince the garlic, dice the onion reasonably small, and prepare the cabbage (the host cuts some into cubes and shreds some so you can still see cabbage).

Cook the filling: In a pan with oil and butter, cook the onion until the rawness goes, then the garlic. Add a pinch of caraway (or thyme) and the cabbage, season with pepper (the host skips salt since corned beef and gravy granules are salty) and wilt and lightly colour about 7 minutes.
Flavour: Stir in the Worcestershire, Dijon and the stock or gravy. You want a moist but not wet filling. Flame off and let it cool completely.
Line the tin: Roll out the pastry into an 8-inch tin, trim the overhang, and brush the inside with egg white to seal it and avoid a soggy bottom. Beat the rest of the egg for the egg wash.
Fill: Break up the corned beef (don't mush it) and stir it through the cold cabbage with the mashed potato if using, then pack into the pastry.
Lid: Cover with a pastry lid, fold in and seal the edges, cut a couple of slits for air, and egg wash the top.
Bake: Put on a tray and bake at 200°C / 400°F about 25–30 minutes until golden and crisp.
Rest: Leave a good 10 minutes before slicing so the filling sets. It's also good cold.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YybKS5r5GAU
Uploaded 2025-11-03.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven to 200°C / 400°F; Bake for 25–30 minutes until golden and crisp; Rest for 10 minutes before slicing to allow the filling to set.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: EASY Creamy Chicken & Broccoli Alfredo Bake - New Family Favourite!
ingredients: Cooked chicken breast — 350 g / 12 oz or more
Grated Parmesan cheese — ½ cup (50 g)
steps: Prep the chicken: Use cooked chicken (the host baked his in advance, or use rotisserie) and shred it.
Boil the pasta: Boil the penne in well-salted water for 8 minutes, then add the broccoli florets to blanch for about 2 minutes. Drain into a bowl.

Make the sauce: Melt the butter, cook the garlic briefly, add the flour and cook about a minute, then season with salt and pepper. Whisk in the milk and cream all at once and let it thicken. Take off the heat and stir in the Parmesan (add a splash more milk if too thick).
Combine: Add the chicken, a pinch of nutmeg, and the sauce to the pasta and broccoli and stir well.
Top: Preheat the oven to 190°C / 375°F. Oil the dish lightly (optional), add the mixture, and top with mozzarella, Parmesan and pepper.
Bake: Bake about 25–30 minutes until melted and golden.
Serve: Rest about 5 minutes, then serve with parsley. The host says the sauce wants a heaped teaspoon of English mustard (or Dijon) stirred in for more flavour.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KRNv74iY-oo
Uploaded 2025-11-02.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven to 190 °C (375 °F); Bake for 25–30 minutes.

recipes.title: Easy Banana Cream Pie – Silky Custard & Fresh Bananas!
ingredients: Crushed digestive biscuits or graham crackers — 200 g (7 oz)
Granulated sugar — 25 g (2 tbsp) (optional; the host skips it with digestives)
Heavy or whipping cream — 250 ml (1 cup)
Oven: 180°C (350°F). Tin: 9-inch (23 cm) pie dish or springform tin.
steps: Make the crust: Mix the crushed biscuits, melted butter and sugar (if using) until combined, and press firmly into the 9-inch dish, up the sides to make a lip.
Bake or chill: Bake at 180°C (350°F) for 8 minutes, or chill for 30 minutes for a no-bake version. Cool completely.
Start the custard: Lightly beat the egg yolks. In a pan stir together the milk, sugar, cornstarch, salt and vanilla, and heat to thicken.
Temper: Once it starts to thicken, stir a little of the hot mix into the yolks, then pour them back in and cook until it's a thickish pourable custard. Stir in the butter and let it cool a little.
Layer: Put the sliced banana on the base and pour the custard over. Press cling film on the surface to avoid a skin.
Chill: Cool, then refrigerate about 4 hours or more to set.
Whip the cream: Whip the cream with the powdered sugar and vanilla.
Finish: Unwrap and remove from the tin, smooth the whipped cream on top (or pipe it), and decorate with banana slices and grated chocolate or sprinkles.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WsJpXcSn_zo
Uploaded 2025-11-01.

recipes.title: BACON & EGG Hand Pies – The Ultimate Grab and Go Breakfast!
ingredients: Cream cheese or cheese sauce — 100 g (3.5 oz)
Cheddar cheese (optional, for extra melt) — 50 g (1.8 oz)
Fresh chives or parsley, finely chopped — 1 tbsp
Tomato, in small cubes — amount not stated (shown in the video, not in the description)
steps: Boil the eggs: Hard-boil the eggs, then cool and chop them.
Cook the bacon: Fry the bacon until crisp, then let it cool. Pour off the fat, leaving a little in the pan.
Cook the tomato: Cook the diced tomato lightly in the pan, just to soften and intensify the flavour, then let it cool.
Mix the filling: Combine the cream cheese, bacon, tomato, chopped eggs, cheddar, herbs, pepper and salt (go easy on salt if the bacon is salty).
Cut and fill: Cut the pastry to size and pile the filling high on each piece. Cut slits in a top piece so it opens up and stretches over the filling, and the pies can be overfilled.
Seal and glaze: Crimp the edges with a fork, preheat the oven to 190°C, and brush with beaten egg.
Bake: Bake 20–25 minutes until puffed and golden.
Serve or freeze: Eat warm with any sauce. They can be baked, cooled, frozen and reheated.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AsIw8R6VNaQ
Uploaded 2025-10-31.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake at 190 °C (375 °F) for 20–25 minutes, or until puffed and golden.

recipes.title: The Sausage Bake You’ll Make Every Week – Creamy Mustard Perfection!
ingredients: Cumberland sausages — 6–8 large links (≈ 700 g / 1.5 lb)
Green or Savoy cabbage, shredded thickly (about 1 inch pieces in the video) — amount not stated
Cornflour (optional, for thickening) — 1 tsp (3 g) mixed with 1 tbsp (liquid)
Potatoes, peeled and cubed (amount not stated), boiled with a little baking soda; oil and rosemary salt (optional)
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 200°C (400°F).
Start the sausages: Toss the sliced onion and the sausages with the oil in a roasting tin (sausages on top of some of the onion) and bake about 10 minutes.
Par-boil the potatoes: Boil the cubed potatoes with a little baking soda for 7 minutes only (it froths as starch comes off). Drain.
Make the sauce: Mix the Dijon, wholegrain mustard, chicken stock, cream, cornflour, salt and pepper.

Build the tray: Take the tray out, push the sausages to one side, and put the cabbage and garlic in so the sausages sit on top, letting the juices soak down. Pour the sauce over the cabbage and dot with a little butter.
Add the potatoes: Toss the potatoes with oil (and rosemary salt) in a second tin and put both in the oven side by side.

Bake and turn: Bake 30–35 minutes, turning the sausages part way so they colour all round (and flipping the potatoes if you like), until sausages reach 70–75°C (160–165°F) and the sauce is bubbling and lightly golden at the edges.
Serve: Serve the cabbage with its sauce, the sausages, and the roast potatoes, with parsley if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1e3gqKdl_h0
Uploaded 2025-10-30.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Boil 7 mins baking soda; Add to oven 35 minutes; Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F); Bake for 10 minutes; Bake for 30–35 minutes, until sausages are cooked through (internal temp 70–75°C / 160–165°F) and the sauce is bubbling and lightly golden around the edges.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: You Won’t Believe What 3 Potatoes Can Do! Better Than Pizza??
ingredients: Medium potatoes, grated — 3 (450 g / 16 oz / 3 cups)
Italian seasoning/herbs — 1½ tsp or to taste
Salt — 1 tsp (6 g) or to taste
Fresh basil or parsley, chopped — a handful (2 tbsp / 4 g)
steps: Squeeze the potatoes: Grate the potatoes, wring them out in a tea towel, loosen and squeeze again to remove as much water as you can.
Cook the veg: Cook the thinly sliced onions in olive oil for a couple of minutes, add the peppers with a pinch of salt, and cook about 5–6 minutes, then let it cool.
Make the batter: Mix the flour, eggs, milk, salt, a little pepper and Italian seasoning into a thick batter (lumps will rehydrate), then mix in the squeezed potato.
Combine: Stir in the cooled onions and peppers.

Bake the base: Spread on a tray lined with parchment, with a little smear of oil (do not wet the paper), so the base crisps. Bake at 180°C / 350°F for 30–35 minutes until set and golden at the edges. (The host forgot the parchment and says the crust would be crispier with it.)
Top: Add sliced tomato, torn basil and the grated cheese.
Finish: Return to the oven about 15 minutes until the cheese melts and turns golden.
Serve: Cool a little and cut.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YYBdZ28ZJtQ
Uploaded 2025-10-29.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven at 180 °C / 350 °F for 30–35 minutes until set and golden at the edges; Return to the oven for 15 minutes more until the cheese melts and turns golden.

recipes.title: Classic BRITISH Mince & Mash – Simple, Nostalgic, Delicious!
ingredients: Minced beef — 450 g (1 lb), ideally 15–20% fat
Beef stock cube (or 1 tsp / 5 g bouillon powder) — 1
Gravy granules — 15–30 g (1–2 tbsp), adjust for thickness
Salt — ½ tsp (3 g) or to taste
Onion powder ½ tsp or a pinch of dried thyme — optional, for extra depth
Potatoes, peeled and chopped — 800 g (1¾ lb)
steps: Cook the onions: In a pan with a little butter (the host uses clarified butter), cook the onion with a pinch of salt until the rawness is gone.
Boil the potatoes: Boil the peeled potatoes in salted water until fork tender, drain, and mash with the butter and milk, salt and pepper.
Brown the mince: Add the mince to the onions, break it up, season with salt and pepper and cook off the pink.

Add flavour: Crumble in the stock cube, add the Worcestershire sauce and dried thyme, then clear a space for the garlic. Stir in the tomato paste and cook out the sourness, add onion powder and the frozen veg.
Simmer: Add enough water to cover and cook uncovered about 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until reduced and thickened.
Thicken: Dissolve the gravy granules in boiling water (as for normal gravy), stir in and cook about 5 minutes more until moist and glossy.
Serve: Pile the mash on a plate and serve the savoury mince alongside or on top.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QSHuMhwqn5E
Uploaded 2025-10-28.

recipes.title: BRITISH RAG PUDDING - A Classic Northern Dish!
ingredients: Dried sage — ¼ tsp (the host uses about ½ tsp in the video)
Beef stock — 150 ml (≈ ½ cup US)
All-purpose flour — 1 tbsp (≈ 8 g), for thickening
Dried thyme — a little (the host adds it to the pastry; amount not stated)
steps: Cook the filling: Sauté the onion in a little oil with thyme and sage, then add the mince and brown it. Season with salt, pepper and Worcestershire.
Thicken: Stir in the flour, then the beef stock. Cover and cook about 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and gloopy. Let it cool.
Make the pastry: Mix the self-raising flour, salt and (optionally) thyme with the suet, then add cold water to bring it together into a dough without working it too much.
Roll and fill: Roll the dough into a rectangle, spread the filling over it leaving the edges clear, wet the edge, and roll it up, sealing the ends.
Wrap: Soak the cloth in water, wring it out, flour it, and roll the pudding in it seam side down, not too tight. Tie the ends with string.
Steam: Steam for 1 hour.
Serve: The traditional way is to slice and serve. For the modern finish, bake at 180°C / 350°F for about 10–15 minutes to a golden crust. Serve with chips and gravy.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nFxQ2LFfCZg
Uploaded 2025-10-27.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake (180°C / 350°F for about 10–15 minutes).
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Ham & Cheese Breakfast Bites – No Pastry Needed!
ingredients: Large flour tortillas, cut into strips to fit a 12-hole muffin tin — 6
Diced cooked ham — 100 g (3.5 oz / ¾ US cup)
Grated cheddar cheese, divided (½ for inside, ½ for topping) — 75 g (2.6 oz / ¾ US cup)
Milk (or cream for richer flavour) — 120 ml (½ US cup)
Olive oil or melted butter, for brushing — 1 tbsp (15 ml)
Pinch dried herbs (thyme, parsley, or chives)
Dried chili flakes — optional (amount not stated)
Oven: 180°C / 350°F. Tin: 12-hole muffin tin, lightly greased.
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 180°C / 350°F and lightly grease a 12-hole muffin tin.
Make the egg mix: Beat the eggs with the milk, salt, pepper, thyme (and chili flakes if you like) and pour into a jug.
Cut the tortillas: Cut the tortillas square-ish to fit the tin (about 2 inches high); the host cuts each to give strips and rolls two up into each cup.
Line the tin: Roll up the tortilla strips and put them in each hole as a shell, and brush with a little oil, butter or bacon fat for crisping.
Bake empty: Bake the empty shells for 5 minutes.
Fill: Open up the rings, add some cheese, tuck in the ham (a little spoon helps), then pour in the egg mixture. Top with more cheese.
Bake: Bake on a tray for 18–22 minutes until golden, puffed and just set in the middle.
Serve: Cool a minute and serve, with a little parsley if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=435KFCUwmak
Uploaded 2025-10-26.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Heat to 180 °C / 350 °F. Lightly grease a 12-hole muffin tin; Bake empty for 5 minutes; Bake for 18–22 minutes until golden, puffed, and just set in the middle.

recipes.title: Forgotten classic BRITISH Apple Dumplings – Just Like Grandma Made!
ingredients: Shredded suet (beef or vegetable) — 125 g (butter does the same job)
Medium cooking apples (Bramley, Granny Smith, or similar), peeled and cored — 4
Butter — 30 g (2 tbsp), divided into small cubes
A little milk or water, to seal (the host brushes with milk)
Caster sugar, for sprinkling if baking (optional)
steps: Make the pastry: Mix the self-raising flour, suet and salt, and add the water to bring it together into a dough. Divide into four pieces.
Make the filling: Mix the brown sugar, dried fruit and mixed spice.
Prep the apples: Peel and core the apples (the host uses a corer, since the filling goes in the hole).

Assemble: Roll a piece of dough out so it will come all the way over an apple. Put a knob of butter in the hole, set the apple upside down on the pastry and pack the fruit, sugar and spice into it. Bring up the pastry, brush with milk and seal, then turn it over so the seam is on the bottom.
Bake: Place seam side down on a tray, brush with milk and sprinkle with sugar. Bake at 190°C / 375°F for about 45–55 minutes until golden and a skewer finds soft apple.
Or steam (traditional): Wrap each dumpling loosely in greased baking parchment, then foil, leaving space to expand, and steam for 45–50 minutes.
Serve: Serve hot with custard.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Pc3Tj-Drw8Y
Uploaded 2025-10-25.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake at 190°C / 375°F for 45–55 minutes until golden and crisp.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Cabbage and Beef Black Bean Stir Fry
ingredients: Beef (sirloin, flank, rump; the host uses chuck roast), thinly sliced — 350 g
Cabbage, roughly chopped — 250 g (9 oz / 3 cups)
Dried red chillies — 6–8 pieces (adjust to taste)
Fermented black beans (rinsed and roughly mashed) — 1 tbsp (15 g)
Shaoxing wine (or dry sherry) — 1 tbsp (15 ml)
Dark soy sauce — ½–1 tsp (5 ml)
Sesame seeds — a sprinkle (optional; amount not stated)
steps: Marinate the beef: Mix the thinly sliced beef with about a tablespoon of light soy sauce, a tablespoon of Shaoxing wine, a little white pepper and cornflour (cornstarch). Leave about 10 minutes.
Prep: Chop the cabbage into good chunks (removing the core), mince the garlic, and break the dried chillies into chunks (seeds carry the heat).
Make the sauce: Mix the soy sauce, dark soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, oyster sauce, sugar, white pepper and cornstarch with a little water.
Sear the beef: Stir-fry the beef in oil until it has a tinge of colour, then take it out.
Aromatics: Add a splash more oil if needed, then the garlic, the black beans and the dried chillies for only about 20 seconds (dried chillies burn quickly).
Cabbage: Add the cabbage and stir-fry, adding a small splash of water to lift the fond off the pan, just until softened.
Combine: Return the beef, add the sauce and toss to coat everything. Flame off.
Serve: Finish with white pepper, spring onions and sesame seeds, with rice or noodles.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=42ox57kujiA
Uploaded 2025-10-24.

recipes.title: The Best Ever Bacon-Wrapped Meatloaf — Oozing with Cheese!
ingredients: Onion, finely chopped — 1 small (about ½ cup / 75 g)
Shredded mozzarella or cheddar cheese — 1 cup (120 g) (or 1 cup cubed cheese for a thicker centre)
Dijon or yellow mustard — 1 tsp (5 ml)
Oven: 180°C / 350°F (the host mentions 170°C). Tin: 2 lb loaf tin lined with parchment.
steps: Soak the crumbs: Mix the breadcrumbs with the milk and let them soak.
Make the glaze: Mix the ketchup, brown sugar and Dijon.

Mix the meat: Combine the beef and pork with the beaten eggs, garlic, salt, pepper, thyme, oregano, paprika, onion and Worcestershire, then the soaked crumbs. Mix lightly by hand and don't overmix, so the loaf stays light, moist and crumbly.
Line the tin: Line the loaf tin with parchment, lay bacon slices across the tin overhanging the sides.
Fill: Press half the meat into the tin, make a well, add the mozzarella and cheddar, and cover with the rest of the meat, sealing the cheese in so it doesn't leak.
Wrap and flip: Fold the bacon over, then invert the loaf onto a tray. Preheat to 180°C / 350°F. Brush the glaze over the top and sides.
Bake: Bake uncovered 50–60 minutes, brushing with remaining glaze about 10 minutes before the end, until the internal temperature reaches 70°C / 160°F.
Rest and serve: Cool about half an hour, then slice and serve with mashed potato and gravy.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oyeagmZnqlY
Uploaded 2025-10-23.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat your oven to 180°C / 350°F; Bake uncovered for 50–60 minutes, brushing with remaining glaze halfway through; The internal temperature should reach 70°C / 160°F.

recipes.title: Is This the New British Chinese? You’ll Want this Every Week!
ingredients: Pineapple chunks (fresh or canned, drained) — 1½ cups (200 g)
Carrot flowers (optional, shown in the video; amount not stated)
Sweet chili sauce — ½ cup (120 ml)
Honey — 1 tbsp (15 ml) (the host uses maple syrup)
Rice vinegar or apple cider vinegar — 1 tbsp (15 ml)
Ginger, finely grated — ½ tsp (1 g) (optional)
Cornflour/cornstarch — 1 tbsp, mixed with 2 tbsp water (slurry)
Fresh coriander or parsley, chopped — 1 tbsp (≈ 3 g)
Sliced chili or spring onions, for garnish (optional)
steps: Prep the tray: Preheat the oven to 190–200°C. Put olive oil in the tray, add the sliced onion, peppers, garlic and pineapple, with salt and pepper, and mix.
Add the sausages: Put the sausages on top of the vegetables and roast uncovered about 25 minutes, turning them about 15 minutes in so they brown all round.
Make the glaze: Stir together the sweet chili sauce, soy sauce, honey (or maple syrup), vinegar (and garlic and ginger if not already in the tray).
Glaze: Take the tray out, turn the sausages, pour the sauce over and stir to baste, leaving the sausages on top. Return to the oven about 20–25 minutes (or longer) for sticky brown colour.
Thicken: Stir in the cornflour slurry (it makes a thicker, stickier sauce) and return to the oven.
Serve: Serve over rice (or crusty bread or chips), finished with fresh coriander or parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-xljP0tvpWw
Uploaded 2025-10-22.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F); Return to the oven for another 20–25 minutes or even longer.

recipes.title: EASY Cheesy Mexican Chicken ONE TRAY Bake – Corn, Beans & Lime Crema
ingredients: Chicken thighs or breasts — 800 g / 1.75 lb (4–6 pieces)
Black beans (drained and rinsed) — 1 cup (170 g)
Red bell pepper, diced — 1 large (≈ 150 g)
Tomato passata (or crushed tomatoes) — 1 cup (240 ml)
Sour cream or Greek yogurt — ½ cup (120 ml)
Water — 1 tbsp (15 ml) (to thin slightly if needed)
Sliced jalapeños or avocado, lime wedges — optional
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 200°C (400°F).
Mix the tray base: In a tray combine the black beans, diced red pepper and onion, corn, cumin, salt, black pepper, a little olive oil and the passata.

Season the chicken: Mix the olive oil, chili powder, smoked paprika, salt, pepper, minced garlic, cumin and lime juice. Coat the chicken (marinate if you have time; the host leaves it about 5 minutes).
Assemble: Nestle the chicken on the tray and spoon any remaining sauce over it.
Roast: Roast uncovered 25–30 minutes until the chicken is nearly cooked through.
Add cheese: Sprinkle the shredded cheddar over the tray and return to the oven 10–15 minutes until the cheese is melted, bubbling and golden and the chicken reaches 75°C (165°F).
Make the crema: While it bakes, stir the sour cream with the lime zest, lime juice, salt and a touch of water to a drizzle.
Serve: Serve over rice or with crusty bread, with the crema, chopped coriander and lime wedges. Leftovers go well in wraps.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LLhjixQUMeg
Uploaded 2025-10-21.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F); Roast uncovered for 25–30 minutes (chicken should be nearly cooked through); Return to oven for another 10–12 minutes, until the cheese is melted, bubbling, and golden, and the chicken reaches 75°C (165°F) internally.

recipes.title: British Tomato Corned Beef Pie – Simple, Savoury & Budget Friendly
ingredients: Onions, finely chopped — 2 medium (about 250 g / 9 oz)
Tomatoes, chopped (fresh or tinned) — 400 g / 14 oz
Beef stock or water — 125 ml (½ cup)
Salt and pepper — to taste (the host skips salt because corned beef is salty)
Mixed herbs or thyme — 1 tsp (4 g) (optional)
Sugar — a little, to balance acidity (optional)
Note from the description: mix a little mashed potato with the corned beef to make it go further.
steps: Prep: Dice the onions and tomatoes (dice rather than slice if you want bits of tomato in the pie).
Cook the onions: In butter with a little oil, cook the onions about 5–7 minutes until the rawness is gone, adding thyme to bloom in the fat.
Add tomatoes: Add the tomatoes and cook down a little (keep some tomato pieces), with black pepper (and chili flakes if you like).
Build the sauce: Add the Worcestershire sauce, tomato paste and beef stock and cook about 8 minutes to thicken. A pinch of sugar balances the acidity. Turn off the heat and let it cool completely.
Add the corned beef: Break up the corned beef without mashing it to mush and stir it into the cool mixture (a little cold mashed potato can go in too).
Line the tin: Preheat to 200°C / 400°F. Line the pie tin with pastry (paper under the base helps slide it out), leaving an overhang. Brush the base with egg white to seal against a soggy bottom.
Fill and lid: Pack in the filling, add a pastry lid, fold the edge over to seal, cut a couple of vents so it can steam, and egg wash.
Bake: Bake 30–35 minutes until golden brown.
Rest: Let it cool about 10 minutes, then lift it out and cut. Serve with chips, peas or mashed potato.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EZPeVJMbrSE
Uploaded 2025-10-20.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 200 °C / 400 °F / Gas 6; Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden brown.

recipes.title: EASIEST Creamy Chicken Bacon Ranch Pasta Salad – Good Anytime of the Year!
ingredients: Chicken breasts or tenderloins — 680 g (1.5 lb), about 3 cups cooked, cubed
Bacon — 8 strips (100 g / 3.5 oz), diced and crisped
Red onion, finely diced — ½ small (50 g)
Cheddar or Monterey Jack cheese, shredded — 100 g (3.5 oz)
Cucumber, cubed — amount not stated (added at the end in the video)
Sour cream or Greek yogurt — 120 g (½ cup)
Buttermilk (or milk + 1 tsp lemon juice) — 60 ml (4 tbsp)
steps: Cook the pasta: Boil the pasta in salted water about 8 minutes, until it still has a little chew. Drain, rinse under cold water and set aside.
Prep: Chop or slice the onion, lettuce, tomatoes and cucumber and cube the chicken.
Cook the bacon: Fry the bacon until crisp and remove, leaving the fat.
Cook the chicken: Cook the chicken in the bacon fat with salt and pepper, about 8 minutes, until it has a little colour. Let it cool.
Make the ranch: Whisk the mayonnaise, sour cream, buttermilk (or make it with 1 cup milk and 1 tbsp vinegar, left 5 minutes), garlic powder, onion powder, dill, parsley, salt, pepper and lemon juice.
Toss: In a large bowl combine the pasta, onion, corn, tomatoes, bacon, chicken, cheese and parsley, then the lettuce and dressing.
Chill: Refrigerate about half an hour.
Serve: Serve topped with a little Parmesan or green onion.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qpo5cHssuh4
Uploaded 2025-10-19.

recipes.title: The Secret to Ultra Crispy Hash Browns with a Creamy Potato Centre!
ingredients: Raw potatoes, grated and squeezed dry — 600 g (about 4 medium)
Chopped chives or grated cheese — 30 g (¼ cup) (optional)
steps: Make the mash: Peel, dice and boil potatoes in salted water, drain, and mash with the butter and milk (chives optional) and season.
Grate and squeeze: Peel and grate the raw potatoes, wring out in a tea towel, loosen the cloth and potato, and squeeze again until most of the moisture is out. Season only after squeezing.
Season the shreds: Mix the dried potato with the salt, pepper and most of the melted butter (keep a little back).
Prep the tray: Preheat the oven to 200°C / 400°F. Butter a tray, including up the sides, for a buttery crust.

Layer: Spread half the grated potato in the tray, add a little cheese (optional), then a layer of mashed potato, then the rest of the grated potato, pressed down so the raw potato adheres to the mash.
Butter and bake: Brush the top with the reserved melted butter. Bake uncovered 35–40 minutes until the top is crisp and golden brown (for extra crispiness, grill/broil for the last 5 minutes).
Serve: Cool a little, cut into portions and serve with an egg. It can be frozen when cooked and reheated.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KUXDEU0tV_E
Uploaded 2025-10-18.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat the Oven to 200°C / 400°F; Bake uncovered for 35–40 minutes, or until the top is crisp and golden brown.

recipes.title: HOW TO MAKE the EASIEST One Tray Autumn Dinner
ingredients: Chicken thighs (bone-in, skin-on) — 6 pieces (≈ 1.2 kg / 2.6 lb)
Smoked paprika — ½ tsp (1.5 g) (optional, for extra depth)
Carrots — amount not stated (baby carrots in the video)
Streaky bacon, chopped — 6 rashers (≈ 120 g / 4 oz, or more)
Red onion, cut into wedges — 1 large (≈ 150 g)
Chopped parsley or thyme leaves; instant gravy (gravy granules and boiling water)
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 200°C (400°F).
Prep the veg: Trim the sprouts, remove any bad leaves and halve them. Put them in the tray with the garlic, carrots, onion wedges and bacon, a little olive oil, salt and pepper.
Season the chicken: Season the chicken thighs on both sides with salt, pepper and smoked paprika and sit them on the veg.
Make the glaze: Mix the maple syrup, Dijon, apple cider vinegar and melted butter. Spoon a little over the veg and chicken, keeping some back.
Cover and bake: Cover with foil and bake about 30–40 minutes.

Uncover: Remove the foil, add the rest of the glaze, and roast uncovered 25–35 minutes, until the chicken skin is golden and the internal temperature reaches 75°C (165°F) and the sprouts are cooked through.
Gravy and serve: Make instant gravy with gravy granules and boiling water on the stove if you like, and serve the chicken and veg with mash, garnished with parsley or thyme.

recipes.title: Is this just the EASIEST French Onion Pasta Bake – Cheesy, Creamy & Loaded with Flavour!
ingredients: Half and half (or single cream + milk mix) — 1 cup (240 ml)
Mustard powder — 1 tsp (2 g) (the host used Dijon mustard; amount not stated)
Balsamic vinegar — ½ tsp (2.5 ml) (optional, for extra depth)
Yellow onions, thinly sliced — 3 medium (15 oz / 425 g)
Garlic, minced — 3 large cloves (~1 tbsp / 15 g)
Pasta (rigatoni, penne, or fusilli), dry — 10 oz (280 g)
Parmesan cheese, freshly grated — ¾ cup (75 g)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Gruyère or cheddar (the host also uses these in the dish and on top; amounts not stated)
steps: Boil the pasta: Cook the pasta in salted water as per the packet, keeping a little chew (al dente), and save some pasta water.

Caramelise the onions: The quick way: in a pan with a little water, oil and butter, a little sugar and salt, cover and steam until soft, about 20 minutes. Remove the lid and cook, stirring, until golden brown. Set aside.

Cook mushrooms and beef: Sauté the mushrooms in oil and butter about 7–8 minutes. Add the beef and cook with thyme, parsley, oregano, salt and pepper. Clear a space and fry the garlic, then add a splash of Worcestershire, a little red wine (optional), balsamic and hot sauce.
Make the sauce: Stir in the flour and cook out the rawness, then add the beef broth, scraping up the fond, and the mustard. Add the half-and-half and simmer.
Combine: Stir in the caramelised onions and the pasta, and add some pasta water so it has a bit of runniness. Stir in most of the Parmesan, Gruyère and mozzarella (save some for topping).
Top: Tip into a baking dish and top with the reserved Parmesan, Gruyère/cheddar and mozzarella (and buttered breadcrumbs if using).
Bake: Bake at 190°C / 375°F for 20–25 minutes until bubbling and golden.
Serve: Dress with a little parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=K9-49pgKTBI

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake at 190°C / 375°F for 20–25 minutes, until bubbling and golden.

recipes.title: Best Ever British Style Minced Beef Pasties – Flaky & Rich!
ingredients: Salt — ½ tsp (3 g) or to taste
Brown sugar — 1 tsp (4 g) (optional, to balance acidity)
Puff pastry sheets — about 2 sheets (≈ 500 g / 1 lb), cut 4.5 × 5 inch or as big as you like
steps: Start the filling: In a pan with olive oil and butter cook the onion to take out the rawness, then the garlic, the grated carrot and the dried thyme (let it bloom in the fat).
Brown the mince: Add the beef, break it up and cook, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Flour and flavour: Stir in the flour to soak up the fat, then the Worcestershire sauce, tomato paste (cook out the rawness), a little brown sugar, the ketchup and beef stock.
Simmer: Turn the heat down and simmer 8–10 minutes, stirring, until thick and moist. Cool completely.
Fill: Preheat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Cut the pastry to about 4.5 × 5 inch, put filling on each piece, fold the pastry over and press the edges down with a fork.
Vent and glaze: Cut a couple of slits for steam and brush with egg wash (or milk).
Bake: Bake 20–25 minutes until puffed and golden brown. Cool 5 minutes.
Store: The pasties can be frozen and reheated (about 180°C in an air fryer for 5 minutes); serve with chips and beans if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CtLBL74ikkI

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 200 °C (400 °F); Bake for 20–25 minutes, until puffed and golden brown. Cool for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.title: ONE Tray Garlic LEMON CHICKEN Dinner – Easy & Comforting!
ingredients: Chicken thighs (bone-in, skin-on) — 6 (can be scaled down to one)
Green cabbage — 1, cut into 6 wedges (one per thigh)
Potatoes, washed, in chunks — amount not stated
Lemon — juice of 1 (the host used the juice of half a big one), plus slices
Butter, melted — amount not stated (plus a little extra butter dotted on the cabbage)
Chicken stock — amount not stated (a little to wet the tray bottom, the rest added later)
Salt (the host uses celery salt; rosemary salt also suggested) and pepper — amounts not stated
Fresh rosemary (or dried) and dried thyme — amounts not stated
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to about 170°C.
Prep the cabbage: Cut the cabbage into wedges, one per chicken thigh, and put in the tray over a little chicken stock to wet the bottom.
Add garlic, lemon and potatoes: Dot garlic around the tray, add the lemon juice and some lemon slices, and scatter in the potato chunks.
Season the chicken: Mix melted butter, olive oil, pepper and salt and rub it all over the chicken thighs.

Assemble: Dot a little butter on the cabbage so it bastes down through the leaves. Add the rest of the chicken stock around the tray. Lay the chicken on top and add lemon slices, rosemary and a little dried thyme.
Cover and roast: Cover with foil and roast about 50 minutes.
Uncover: Take the foil off and roast another 25–30 minutes until the chicken is cooked and crisp.
Serve: Serve the chicken with the buttery lemon juices over the cabbage and potatoes.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G_1EdWo25ew

recipes.title: Italian Apple Cake – So Easy, So Moist, Tangy & Perfect with Coffee!
ingredients: Apples, peeled and chopped — 2 large (about 300 g / 2 cups chopped); the host uses about three
Sour cream — 200 ml (≈ ¾ UK cup)
Butter (unsalted, melted) — ½ cup (≈ 115 g / 8 tbsp)
Icing sugar — a light dusting (optional; amount not stated)
Oven: 180°C (350°F). Tin: 8 inch springform, lined, on a tray.
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 180°C (350°F) and line the 8-inch tin (on a tray in case it leaks).
Mix the dry ingredients: Whisk the flour, baking powder, salt and cinnamon.
Make the batter: Beat the eggs with the sugar and melted butter until fluffy, then add the vanilla and sour cream and stir in the dry mix.
Prep the apples: Peel, core and slice or dice the apples (any variety; don't use too many or the cake will be too moist).
Layer: Put a little batter in the tin for a cakey bottom, add some apples, then the rest of the batter and apples, spacing the apples through.
Bake: Bake 35–40 minutes (check at 30) until a skewer in the centre comes out clean and the top is golden.
Cool: Leave in the tin about 5 minutes, then turn out onto a rack and cool completely.
Serve: Dust lightly with icing sugar and serve with Greek yogurt.

recipes.title: The Ultimate Sweet-Spicy Chicken Stir Fry in 20 Minutes
ingredients: Maple syrup or light brown sugar — 2 tbsp (30 ml)
Rice vinegar or apple cider vinegar — 1 tbsp (15 ml)
Cornstarch — 1 tsp (5 g) mixed with 2 tbsp (30 ml) cold water
Chicken breast or thigh — 450 g (1 lb / 2 cups diced)
Oil (vegetable, peanut, or sesame) — 2 tbsp (30 ml)
Spring onion or scallion, chopped — 2 (30 g)
Toasted sesame seeds and a lime wedge
steps: Make the sauce: Mix the Sriracha, maple syrup, soy sauce and vinegar. Keep the cornstarch slurry (1 tsp cornstarch in 2 tbsp water) to add in the pan.

Cook the chicken: In a pan with a little oil (and some sesame oil) stir-fry the chicken until it has some colour, then take it out. (Tip from the host: if the cubes are too big, split them with a wooden spoon once they start cooking.)
Cook the veg: Stir-fry the carrot, red pepper, spring onion and broccoli with a splash of water to help it along.
Aromatics: Clear a space and stir in the garlic and ginger.
Combine: Return the chicken, add the sauce and the cornstarch slurry, and cook until thick and sticky. Flame off.
Serve: Serve over rice or noodles with sesame seeds and green onion. For less heat, use just 1 tbsp Sriracha (the host says a little ketchup also works).
recipes.notes:

recipes.title: Rich & Velvety CHICKEN NOODLE Soup – One Pot Comfort Classic!
ingredients: All-purpose flour — 3 tbsp (25 g) (up to 4 tbsp for a thicker soup)
Heavy cream (or evaporated milk) — 1 cup (240 ml)
Grated Parmesan — 2 tbsp (10 g) (optional, for richness)
Lemon juice — 1 tbsp (15 ml) (optional, to balance flavour)
Fresh parsley, to serve (amount not stated)
steps: Sweat the veg: In a pan with oil and butter cook the onion with a little salt and pepper to soften, then add the celery with the dried thyme and parsley, then the garlic until it has a tinge.
Add carrots and butter: Stir in the carrots and a little more butter.
Make the roux: Stir in the flour and cook about a minute to cook out the rawness.
Add the stock: Pour in the chicken stock and simmer about 10 minutes to soften the veg.
Add chicken and noodles: Stir in the shredded chicken. If it gets too thick, loosen with a little boiling water. Add the noodles and cook about 8 minutes, leaving a little chew.
Make it creamy: Stir in the cream, then the Parmesan.
Finish: Turn off the flame and add a squeeze of lemon juice.
Serve: Serve with fresh parsley. The host says you can add peas, sweetcorn or chili flakes.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5koAnoYLdjo

recipes.title: Easiest AUTUMN Dessert Classic Apple Cobbler – Warm & Buttery!
ingredients: Apples, peeled, cored, sliced about 1 cm — 900 g (about 6 medium)
Mixed spice (or ground cinnamon 1 tsp (3 g) plus ground nutmeg ¼ tsp (0.5 g))
Pinch of salt (optional; the host adds a little)
Demerara or brown sugar for sprinkling — 1 tbsp
Butter dots over the apples; custard to serve
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 180°C (350°F) and butter the dish.
Prep the apples: Peel, core and slice the apples about 1 cm thick (vary the thickness for texture).
Make the filling: Toss with the white and brown sugars, mixed spice (or cinnamon and nutmeg), lemon juice, a little salt, and the cornflour mixed with the water.

Make the topping: Mix the flour, baking powder, sugar and salt, rub in the cold butter to breadcrumbs (the host uses melted butter for the dish base), then add the milk and vanilla and bring together into a soft dough without overworking.
Assemble: Put the apple mix in the dish, dot a little butter on top, then dollop the topping over, leaving gaps so it steams and puffs up. Sprinkle with sugar.
Bake: Bake 35–40 minutes until the top is golden brown and the fruit is bubbling.
Serve: Serve warm with custard, cream or ice cream.

recipes.title: Tomato TART - – Simple, Rustic, Irresistible!
ingredients: Ripe tomatoes (mix of cherry and large), sliced — 400 g (14 oz)
Ricotta or cream cheese — 100 g (3½ oz)
Grated mozzarella or cheddar — 75 g (2½ oz)
Fresh thyme or basil leaves — a few sprigs
steps: Line the tin: Roll the pastry to fit the tin, press it into the flutes with an overhang, trim, and dock the base.
Blind bake: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Add parchment and baking beads and bake 12–15 minutes, remove the beads and bake another 5 minutes.
Prep the tomatoes: Slice the large tomatoes about half a cm thick and keep the cherry tomatoes to mix in.
Make the cheese layer: Mix the cream cheese (or ricotta) with the mozzarella.
Mustard base: Spread the Dijon mustard over the base of the baked case, then spread the cheese mix over it.
Layer: Overlap the tomato slices on top, mixing in the cherry tomatoes. Drizzle with olive oil, add torn basil (or thyme), salt and pepper and a little more mozzarella.
Bake: Bake 25–30 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Serve: Cool about 10 minutes and serve with salad or chips (fries), topped with fresh basil.

recipes.title: German Pork Knuckle with Beer Gravy - COSORI TURBO TOWER Dual Air Fryer
ingredients: Oil, garlic powder, salt, black pepper (light), caraway seeds — amounts not stated (rubbed on as a mix)
Beer, for the tray and for brushing — amount not stated
Apple cider vinegar and a little water — amounts not stated (brushed on to crisp the skin)
Carrot, celery, onion, chopped — amounts not stated
Potatoes, par-boiled — amount not stated; oil, rosemary salt, dried thyme
Baby carrots and larger carrots — amount not stated; olive oil, salt
The strained beer and vegetable broth from the tray, plus water, more beer or stock if needed
steps: Mix the rub: Mix oil with garlic powder, salt, a little black pepper and caraway seeds and smear it over the pork (the host goes light so the skin doesn't burn).
Set up the tower: Chop the carrot, celery and onion into the tray and add beer, not so high that it touches the basket. The pork sits above so the juices drip down.
Bake: Cook on bake at 160°C. (In the video the host finds the knuckles sit too close to the top element, so they are moved to the bottom drawer.)
Score and crisp: Score the softened skin lightly, brush with beer, and air fry about 180°C for about 25 minutes.
Make the beer broth: Tip the veg and the fat-rich beer juices from the tray into a pan with a bay leaf and soften the vegetables further, then strain.

Potatoes and carrots: Par-boil the potatoes, toss in oil, rosemary salt and dried thyme, and air fry in the top basket; toss the carrots in olive oil and salt and add them for the last 10 minutes or so.
Glaze the skin: Brush the pork skin with apple cider vinegar and a little water to crisp it. Air fry the top drawer at 190°C for about 12 minutes and the bottom at 205°C for about 12 minutes.
Make the gravy: Melt butter, cook out flour, then add the strained beer broth (plus water, beer or stock) until thickened.
Rest and serve: Rest the pork briefly, then serve with the roast potatoes, carrots and gravy, and mustard if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y50QK6tlkRI

recipes.title: EASY SLOW Cooked - Creamy Mushroom Chicken with Thyme and some Veggies
ingredients: Chicken thighs or breasts — 800 g (1 lb 12 oz) (the host uses bone-in, skin-on thighs)
Veggies of choice, anything from the fridge (the host used carrot, celery and a little leek) — amounts not stated
Cornstarch slurry — 1 tbsp cornstarch mixed with 1 tbsp water
Optional garnish: chopped parsley or extra thyme leaves
steps: Prep the veg: Dice the onion, carrot, celery and leek, mince the garlic and halve or slice the mushrooms.
Season the chicken: Pat the thighs dry, season with salt, thyme and a little flour (and paprika or chili if you like).
Brown the chicken: Fry in oil and butter skin side down until golden on both sides (it doesn't need to cook through). Set aside.

Start the veg: In the same pan cook the onion, other veg, garlic and mushrooms with pepper and thyme (no extra salt since the stock is salty), stir in about a tablespoon of flour, then the chicken stock, scraping up the fond. Flame off.
Slow cook: Tip into the slow cooker with the chicken on top. Cook on LOW for 6–7 hours or HIGH for 3–4 hours until the chicken is tender (the host cooked on high for the video).
Finish: Stir in the cream, then the cornstarch slurry to thicken (the sauce won't thicken by itself).
Serve: Serve over rice, mash, pasta or with green beans.

recipes.title: 1970s Meatless Stew with Dumplings - classic budget dish
ingredients: Celery — a little (shown in the video; amount not stated)
Pinch of herbs (optional; the host uses dried thyme)
Butter or oil, for frying the onion — amount not stated
Suet (or cold grated butter) — 60 g (4 tbsp)
steps: Fry the onion: Cook the diced onion in a little butter with a pinch of thyme, salt and pepper to take the rawness out.
Add veg: Add the carrots and celery with a splash of water to start softening, then the potatoes.
Add soup and water: Pour in the can of soup and a full can of water (rinse the can with it). Stir.
Simmer: Bring to the boil, then reduce to a simmer for about 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until a fork just goes into the potato.

Make the dumplings: Mix the self-raising flour with salt, a little pepper and thyme, rub in the suet (or butter) like pastry for about a minute, then add cold water to form a dough that isn't soggy, without overworking it. Divide into 8 dumplings, shaping with fingers and thumbs rather than squashing.
Add and steam: Drop the dumplings into the stew, put the lid on and steam about 20 minutes.
Serve: Serve hot; the dumplings are fluffy inside with a stodgy bottom where they sat in the soup.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N1ISIXOvsX0
Uploaded 2025-10-06.

recipes.title: Meat and Batter Pudding  - Modern version
ingredients: Dripping or oil — 2 tbsp (28 g / 30 ml)
Beef stock or gravy — 250 ml (1 cup)
steps: Make the batter: Whisk the flour, salt, milk and eggs together; a few lumps are fine. Set aside.
Prep the veg: Dice the onion, celery and garlic and cube the carrots (smaller, as they cook longer) and potatoes.
Brown the beef: In oil (and a little butter) cook the onion briefly, then add the mince with salt and pepper, breaking it up and cooking off any water.
Add the rest: Stir in the garlic, thyme, carrots, celery and potatoes and cook about 5–6 minutes. Add the tomato puree, Worcestershire sauce and stock.
Simmer: Cook about 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the veg starts to soften.
Assemble: Spread the filling evenly in a deep baking tray and pour the batter gently over the top.
Bake: Bake at 200°C / 400°F / Gas 6 for 40–45 minutes until golden and puffed (the host recommends having the tray hot in the oven first). Serve with peas.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=692u7-zsVyQ

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake at 200 °C / 400 °F / Gas 6 for 40–45 minutes, until golden and puffed.

recipes.title: Chicken Stew That Tastes Like a Holiday in Greece!
ingredients: Chicken thighs (bone-in, skin-on or boneless) — 4–6 medium
Red bell pepper, chopped — 1 large (200 g)
Tinned chopped tomatoes — 400 g (14 oz / 1 can)
Black olives (pitted), whole or halved — 80 g
Salt — ½ tsp (3 g) or to taste
Self-raising flour — 200 g (1½ cups UK / 1⅔ cups US)
Cold water — 90–100 ml (6–7 tbsp), enough to form a soft dough
steps: Prep the veg: Chop the pepper, mince the garlic, chop the onion and cube the carrot small, since carrot takes longer to cook.

Season the chicken: Dust the thighs with a little mixed herbs and garlic powder, plus salt, pepper and a little dried thyme, then dust with a little flour and flip and season the other side. The flour gives a bit of crustiness. Bone-in, skin-on is optional; boneless thighs can be prepped the same way.

Brown the chicken: Heat olive oil with a little butter (butter for flavour, oil to stop it burning) over a lowered flame and brown the thighs, skin side down if skin-on. It doesn't need to cook through, as it goes in the oven for 20–25 minutes and back in the stew for about 10.
Trim the fat: Take the chicken out. If there is too much oil in the pan, remove some, but don't throw it away as it is good cooking oil.

Cook the veg: Add the carrots (scraping up the fond) and onion to cook out the rawness, then clear a space and add the garlic for about 30 seconds until it just takes a light colour. Add the red pepper.
Bloom the herbs: Add dried thyme, oregano or a good pinch of Italian seasoning, and a bay leaf, and stir so the flavour releases before adding liquid.
Add tomatoes and stock: Add the tinned tomatoes (chopping them with scissors in the pan) and the chicken stock, and bring to a simmer.
Return the chicken: Nestle the chicken back in without fully submerging it, and set aside while you make the dumplings.

Make the dumplings: Mix self-raising flour, baking powder, a pinch of salt, thyme and oregano, then add about 3 tablespoons olive oil and rub it in with your hands. Add water to bring it into a dough, without overworking it.
Add the olives: Stir the black olives (halved or whole) into the stew and give them a couple of minutes. Heat the oven to about 190–200°C.

Assemble: Take the chicken out, tip the stew into a suitable dish or tray, nestle the chicken back in, and drop small dumplings over the top, staggered. They will rise even if they sit on the chicken. Fresh parsley can go in now or at the end.

Bake and serve: Bake in the oven until the dumplings are puffed and golden (the description gives 20–25 minutes). Finish with parsley and serve a scoop of stew, a couple of dumplings and chicken. The dumplings are crispy on top and a little stodgy where they sat in the juice.
recipes.notes:

Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 200°C (180°C fan) / 400°F / Gas 6 for 20–25 minutes, until the dumplings are puffed and golden brown.

recipes.title: Easy German Red Cabbage – Sweet, Savoury & Perfect with Roast Meats!
ingredients: Red cabbage, finely shredded — 1 medium (about 1 kg / 2.2 lb)
Apples, peeled, cored, and grated or thinly sliced — 2 medium (250 g)
Unsalted butter or goose fat — 3 tbsp (45 g)
Red wine vinegar (or apple cider vinegar) — 100 ml (⅓ cup + 1 tbsp)
Red wine or apple juice — 200 ml (¾ cup + 1 tbsp)
Ground cloves — ¼ tsp (instead of whole cloves)
Ground cinnamon — ½ tsp (instead of a stick)
Redcurrant jelly or cranberry sauce, to finish — 2 tbsp (optional; the host used 1 tbsp redcurrant jelly)
Apple sauce, to finish — 2 tbsp (as used in the video)
steps: Prep the cabbage: Remove the outer leaves, then slice the red cabbage thinly with a knife (or mandoline), by whichever method you're comfortable with.
Prep the apples: Peel, core and slice (or dice) the apples. Leaving the skin on is up to you.
Soften the onions: Melt about 3 tablespoons of butter in a pot and cook the onions for up to 5 minutes until they soften.

Add apples and spices: Add the ground cinnamon (½ tsp) and ground clove (¼ tsp), plus the apples, and cook about a minute. Add about 3 tablespoons brown sugar and caramelise it for a minute. Let the spices bloom.

Add the cabbage in stages: Stir the cabbage in a little at a time so it breaks down and doesn't overflow, adding a little salt, then some red wine and red wine vinegar, and keep adding until all the cabbage is in. Add pepper.
Add the bay leaves: Add two bay leaves. Using powdered spices means there are no whole spices to fish out later.

Simmer: Cover with a lid and simmer for about 45–50 minutes, turning it over now and then, as the bottom cooks while the top only steams. You're looking for tender cabbage with a little bit of crunch, or cook it softer if you prefer.
Finish: Remove the bay leaves, stir in one tablespoon of redcurrant jelly (or cranberry sauce) and two tablespoons of apple sauce, then turn off the heat and check the seasoning.
Optional stock: For more savoury depth, add stock at the same time as the red wine and vinegar: vegetable stock to keep it vegetarian, or beef stock if serving with meat.
Serve: Serve with roast meats, or cold with cold meats and mashed potato.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jZJIbzmBiSE
Uploaded 2025-10-03.

recipes.title: Stuffed Cabbage Meets LASAGNA – A Comfort Bake You’ll Love
steps: Blanch the cabbage: Remove the core and stalk and pull off the leaves. Blanch them in simmering (optionally salted) water for about 2–3 minutes, just to soften them. Cooling in ice water is optional.
Dress the leaves: Stack the leaves, toss with a knob of butter and a little salt and pepper, and set aside. They will release juice as they sit.

Start the meat sauce: Sauté the onions in a little oil and butter to cook out the rawness, then add the garlic for 30 seconds or more, then the mince, breaking it up. Season lightly (Parmesan is going in later) with pepper.
Season the meat: When the meat is about 80% cooked add Italian seasoning, extra dried oregano and smoked paprika. Optional extras: chopped bacon and caraway seeds.

Add tomato: Add a tablespoon of tomato purée and the passata, plus a little sugar if you like. (The host suggests making passata by blending a budget tin of tomatoes with a tablespoon of purée and a little water.)
Reduce the sauce: Cook uncovered for about 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until thickened and moist but not wet.

Make the béchamel: Melt butter, add the flour and cook out the rawness, then add all the milk at once and whisk or stir until thick and lump-free (loosen with milk or water if too thick). Add pepper, nutmeg, Parmesan and mozzarella (cheddar also works).
Heat the oven: Preheat to about 180°C.

Layer: Start with a little meat sauce on the bottom, pressed down for a bit of crispness, then a layer of cabbage, a smear of white sauce, cottage cheese or ricotta and a little cheese. Repeat in whatever order, finishing with cabbage, sauce, oregano and Parmesan. Don't squash it down.
Bake covered: Cover with foil and bake for about 30–40 minutes.
Brown: Remove the foil and cook another 15–20 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Rest and serve: Let it set for about 15 minutes before slicing. There will be some cabbage juice underneath.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lw9TTWTgvgo
Uploaded 2025-10-02.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 180 °C (350 °F).

recipes.title: CLASSIC British teatime TREAT sweet SCONE using mayonnaise 30 Mins!
ingredients: Milk — 120 ml (8 tbsp / ½ cup), plus extra for brushing the tops
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to about 200°C (fan 180°C) and line a baking tray with parchment paper.
Mix the wet: Stir together the mayonnaise, milk and a splash of vanilla. All the fat (oil and egg) is in the mayonnaise, which is why it works.
Add the dry: Add self-raising flour, baking powder, sugar, salt and the dried fruit (the host used mixed golden and dark raisins).
Combine gently: Cut the mix in with a spoon, then bring it together gently with your hand without overmixing. If it's too wet add flour; if too dry add a bit of milk.
Shape: On a lightly floured surface, pat the dough down to about 2½ cm thick. Cracks don't matter.
Cut: Cut out rounds with a cutter and place them on the lined tray, without overworking the dough. The odd end piece won't rise as high.
Glaze: Brush the tops with milk for a nice colour.
Bake: Bake for 12–15 minutes until they have some colour, then cool on a rack for a minute.
Serve: Split and serve with butter, or with jam and cream. They don't taste of mayonnaise, and it keeps them moist.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UtXODmugjkg
Uploaded 2025-10-01.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 200 °C (fan 180 °C) / 400 °F / Gas 6; Bake 12–15 minutes until risen and golden.

recipes.title: Cheese & Onion Potato Pie  - OLD-school COMFORTING pie.
ingredients: Ready-made shortcrust pastry — enough to line and top an 8-inch tin
Onions, finely sliced — 2 medium (about 250 g / 1¾ cups)
Butter (or oil) for the onions — 2 tbsp (28 g)
Potatoes — 500 g (about 4 medium; 3½–4 cups diced, cooked, mashed)
Butter, for the sauce — 2 tbsp (28 g)
Mustard — 1 tsp (optional, for flavour; the host used a heaped spoon of English mustard)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Beaten egg or milk — for glazing (an egg white is also used to seal the base)
steps: Boil the potatoes: Peel the potatoes, cut out any eyes, cube them and put them in salted water. Bring to the boil.
Prep the onions: Slice or dice them — either works (the host does one of each).
Cook the onions: Cook them in butter and a little oil with a pinch of salt and black pepper for 12–15 minutes until golden, without rushing or burning.
Start the sauce in the same pan: Add a couple of tablespoons of butter and about the same amount of flour to the onions and cook out the rawness of the flour.
Add the milk: Pour in all the milk at once and stir; it thickens without lumps (apart from onion). Stir in English mustard (Dijon also works). Loosen with more milk if it gets too thick.
Add cheese: Stir in most of the cheese, keeping a little back, until you have a really thick sauce so everything holds together in the pie. Turn off the heat.
Mash lightly: Drain the potatoes and mash them with plenty of chunks left. Stir them into the sauce for the pie filling and let it cool a little.
Heat the oven: Preheat to about 200°C.
Line the tin: Roll out the pastry, line the 8-inch tin up the sides with a bit of overhang, trim any excess, and dock the base.
Seal the base: Brush the base with egg white to form a seal that prevents a soggy bottom. Beat a whole egg for the glaze (milk or milk and water also works).
Fill and lid: Fill the pie, roll out the lid, lay it over, crimp the edges and cut air vents. The host decided not to add the extra cheese inside.
Glaze and bake: Egg wash the top, set the pie on a tray as it may bubble over, and bake for about 35–40 minutes until golden.
Rest and serve: Leave it to set about 10 minutes. To remove it from the tin, place another tin on top and flip, then turn it back onto a plate. Serve with carrots, veg or anything you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BSY3MUKEQFk
Uploaded 2025-09-30.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) / 400°F for 35–40 minutes, until golden.

recipes.title: Cheese Scones No Butter – Milk Only - 30 mins!
ingredients: Grated cheddar cheese — 100 g (1 cup / ~3.5 oz), plus a little extra for sprinkling on top (optional)
Milk — 175 ml (¾ cup / 6 fl oz), plus a little for brushing
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to about 200°C (180°C fan) and line a baking tray.
Mix the dry: Stir together the self-raising flour, baking powder and a little salt.
Add cheese: Stir in the cheese, saving some for the tops. (The host says a little powdered mustard also works well but leaves it out here.)

Add the milk: Pour in all the milk and mix just enough to make a dough, then bring it together with your hand. If too sticky add flour; if too dry add a little more milk or water. Don't overmix, so the scones rise.
Shape: Push the dough out on your work surface to about 2½ cm thick.
Cut: Cut rounds, optionally dipping the cutter in flour, and place them on the lined tray fairly close together but not touching, which helps them rise. Cracks don't matter.
Top: Brush the tops with milk and add a little cheese on each for brown, crispy cheese. Don't overdo it.
Bake: Bake for about 12–15 minutes until golden, risen and with a hollow sound.
Cool and serve: Rest a minute, move to a rack, then split and slap butter on while warm.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3E3IXtbFQ3Y
Uploaded 2025-09-29.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 200°C (180°C fan) / 400°F. Line a baking tray; Bake 12–15 minutes until golden and risen.

recipes.title: German Onion Tart  - Zwiebelkuchen
ingredients: Shortcrust pastry (ready-rolled) — to line the tin (no quantity given in the description; the host used an 8-inch tin, although a 10-inch is ideal)
Egg white — a little, to brush the base
Onions, thinly sliced — 600 g (about 4–5 medium; the host sliced roughly 900 g–1 kg)
Smoked bacon or pancetta, diced — 150 g
Sour cream or crème fraîche — 200 ml
Salt — ½ tsp (3 g), adjusted for the saltiness of the bacon
Ground black pepper — ½ tsp (2 g)
Federweißer (young wine) or a good German lager
steps: Slice the onions: Slice them thinly.
Line the tin: Roll out the ready-rolled pastry, fit it into the tin, work it into the bottom and trim off the excess. Dock the base with a fork. It isn't blind baked.
Seal the base: Brush a thin coat of egg white over the pastry to avoid a soggy bottom, then chill it in the fridge while you make the filling.
Make the custard: Beat the eggs with salt, a pinch of nutmeg, black pepper, sour cream, cream and a pinch of caraway seeds. Set aside.
Cook the onions: Fry the onions in a couple of tablespoons of butter with a little salt (go carefully, depending on the bacon) for about 15 minutes until golden and soft, cooking out the moisture.
Add the bacon: Add the smoked bacon (cubed streaky) and cook it with the onions so the fat adds flavour. It will cook more in the oven. Turn off the heat and let it cool.
Heat the oven: About 190°C.
Assemble: Push in some of the onion and bacon mix gently without making it too solid, pour over some custard, then add more onion mix so the custard seeps through everything.
Bake: Bake for 35–40 minutes until golden and just set.
Cool and serve: Let it cool until warm, then turn it out and serve with a blob of German mustard and a beer or glass of wine.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oVdlMBTDatc
Uploaded 2025-09-28.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake at 190°C (170°C fan) / 375°F for 35–40 minutes, until golden and just set.

recipes.title: Budget Friendly Chilli Using Condensed Tomato Soup – Easy 30 Minute Recipe
ingredients: Red onion, finely diced — 1 medium (~150 g)
Garlic cloves, crushed — 2 cloves (≈ 10 g / 2 tsp minced)
Chilli powder — 1–2 tsp (≈ 2–4 g), to taste (the host used about 1 tsp of a very hot one)
Batchelors Cream of Tomato Condensed Soup — 1 can (295 g)
Kidney beans, drained — 1 can (400 g; ~240 g drained)
Salt, a little oil, butter and cheddar — to finish
steps: Microwave the potatoes: Cut a slit about halfway through each scrubbed potato, prick all over with a fork, and microwave for 10 minutes.
Crisp in the oven: Rub them with a little oil and salt (the salt flavours and dries the skin) and bake in a hot oven for about 20 minutes to crisp the skins, while you make the chilli.
Start the chilli: Cook the diced onion in a little oil, then add the mince, breaking it up, and cook off the water it releases.
Add garlic: Add the crushed garlic and let it cook without burning, as burnt garlic is bitter. Add a little salt.
Add the spices: Stir in the ½ tsp cumin and chilli powder (about 1 tsp in the video) and bloom for 20–30 seconds.
Add soup, water and beans: Add the condensed soup, rinse the can with 100 ml of water and add that, then add the drained kidney beans.

Simmer: Simmer for about 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and it has lost the tomato soup colour. The host notes it's the can's recipe; a pinch of oregano or tomato purée would be an optional change, but wasn't added here.
Finish the potatoes: Cut the baked potatoes open, loosen with a fork, add butter and cheddar, and return briefly to the oven to melt the cheese.
Serve: Spoon the chilli over the jacket potatoes and top with cheese. It also works over rice or noodles.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tKSzIU35arg
Uploaded 2025-09-27.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: 230 oven.

recipes.title: COSORI TURBO TOWER PRO SMART Dual Air Fryer - 3 layers FULL ENGLISH breakfast done IN ONE  GO!
ingredients: Baked beans, in a ramekin — 120 g / 4 oz
steps: Set up the machine: Use both baskets and the stainless rack for the three-tier system. Don't press Match or Sync. Choose Air Fry on both baskets at 180°C: 15 minutes for basket one and 10 minutes for basket two, so you can pull trays out and put them back.
Sausages first: Spray the top tray and put in the sausages (description: about 12–15 minutes in all). Start the cook.
Add black pudding (+3 min): Pull the tray, add the black pudding beside the sausages with a little spray over the top (description: 8–10 minutes).
Prep the veg: Put butter and mushrooms in a small tray, and the tomatoes in another with salt, pepper and a little oil.
Add bacon (+5 min): Put the bacon in the top tray; pull and flip it partway. Put the mushrooms and tomatoes in the bottom drawer (description: about 10 minutes).
Add beans (+9 min): Put the beans in a ramekin in the bottom drawer (description: 6–7 minutes), stirring once. Grease a couple of ramekins with butter and crack the eggs in.
Make fried bread: When the top drawer is done, stack the sausages, black pudding and bacon, and soak the bread in the pan juices from the bacon and sausage for fried bread.

Finish the bottom basket: Take out the tomatoes, mushrooms and beans. Put the eggs in the bottom basket, with the silver tray over the top holding the toast and fried bread. Cook the bottom basket only at 160°C for about 6 minutes, flipping the bread and toast partway.

Plate up: Plate the bacon, sausages, black pudding, tomato, mushrooms and beans, then add the toast, fried bread and eggs (runny yolk in the video). The whole cook took nearly 17 minutes rather than 15.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=waamFgrS_3k

Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Easy Mongolian Ground Beef Noodles – 20 Minute Dinner Recipe
ingredients: Ramen noodles (dried, Japanese-style) — 300 g (10.5 oz; about 4 blocks)
Crushed red pepper flakes — 1–2 tsp (optional, for heat)
Cornstarch + water — 1 tbsp + 2 tbsp (optional, for thickening)
steps: Prep: Slice the onion (it threads through the noodles) and mash the garlic.

Soften the noodles: Bring a pan of water to the boil, add the dried noodles and bring back to the boil, then turn off the heat and let them stand, loosening them as they soften, rather than boiling 4–5 minutes. They cook through while you make the sauce.
Brown the beef: In a pan (oil only if the meat is lean), cook and break up the mince, cooking off any water if it was frozen. Season with a little white (or black) pepper.
Add onion: Add the onion and soften it to take out the rawness.
Add garlic: Clear a space and cook the garlic in the fat until it just has a tinge of colour, then stir it all in without blackening it.
Prepare a slurry: Mix 1 tbsp cornflour with 2 tbsp water and keep it on standby in case the sauce needs thickening.
Make the sauce: Add the brown sugar, soy sauce and store-bought hoisin. Soy gives sourness and hoisin and sugar give sweetness, so cut the sugar if you want it less sweet.
Add the noodles: Drain the noodles, toss with a couple of drops of sesame oil to stop them sticking, then add to the pan and stir through to coat in sauce and beef.
Finish: Add chilli flakes (a good heaped teaspoon; the host likes Korean flakes), turn off the heat, and serve topped with green onion and roasted sesame seeds.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nfG93hCxEGk

recipes.title: Sausage & Mushroom STROGANOFF - Comfort on a plate in 30 Minutes!
ingredients: Whole sausages (pork, beef, or chicken) — 4 large (about 400 g / 14 oz sliced)
Mushrooms (button or chestnut), sliced — 250 g (9 oz / 2½ cups)
Sour cream or crème fraîche — 100 g (3.5 oz)
Fresh parsley — 2 tbsp (6 g), or 1 tsp dried
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Mashed potatoes (or rice or buttered noodles)
Something green, such as green onion, chives or parsley
steps: Prep: Slice the mushrooms (cut off the end to make a flat side so they sit still), dice the onion and mince the garlic.

Boil-fry the sausages: Put the sausages in a pan with some water and a little olive oil. They plump up and cook as you turn them. When the water has boiled off the oil takes over and browns them. Take them out.
Trim the fat: If there is a lot of fat from the sausages, take some out but leave some for flavour.
Cook the aromatics: Add butter and cook the onions to take out the rawness, then the garlic, then the mushrooms, stirring so they pick up a little colour.

Season: Stir in the parsley (a heaped teaspoon dried, or fresh at the end) and about a teaspoon of paprika, plus pepper. No salt, as the sausages are salty enough. Add Worcestershire sauce and a teaspoon of Dijon mustard.
Add the stock: Add the beef stock (cube, powder, whichever) and turn down to a simmer.
Slice the sausages: Cut them into thick chunks and stir them back into the sauce gently.

Flour, if needed: The host skipped flour because he used powdered beef broth. If using a cube, which gives basically water, stir a tablespoon of flour in with the mushrooms and cook out the rawness before adding the stock.
Add sour cream: Turn the heat very low and stir in about 100 g sour cream; too much heat can make it curdle.
Serve: Plate over mashed potato with a divot, spoon over the sausages, mushrooms, onion and sauce, and add a bit of green for colour.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Qz-D89LA7kM
