recipes.title: German Style Fried Potatoes Bratkartoffeln
ingredients: Waxy potatoes, sliced — 600 g (about 4 medium; 4 cups sliced)
Green cabbage, shredded — 200 g (about ¼ small head)
Bacon bits or diced streaky bacon — 150 g (1 heaping cup)
Sunflower or rapeseed oil — 3 tbsp (45 ml)
steps: Slice the potatoes: Slice them (or boil whole and slice afterwards, as you prefer).
Par-boil: Boil the slices in water for about 7 minutes, until a fork only just goes in. Salt the water carefully, especially with salty bacon. Drain.
Prep the rest: Shred the cabbage, mince the garlic, cube the onion (any colour), and chop the bacon bits into small pieces.
Cook the bacon: In a pan, cook the bacon until it has some colour (it will keep cooking later). Take it out, leaving the fat in the pan for flavour.
Cook onion, cabbage and garlic: Cook the onion in the bacon fat until it loses its rawness, add the cabbage and then the garlic until lightly tinged and soft. Remove to a bowl.
Fry the potatoes: Add a little oil and fry the potatoes in batches, without overcrowding, until they have some colour, turning them with the back of the spoon. Set aside.

Bring it together: Add butter to the pan, then the bacon with its juices and the onion and cabbage, with the caraway seeds, pepper and a little salt. Cook for about a minute until the seeds start to pop and release their flavour.
Add the potatoes: Stir the potatoes through.
Serve: Serve in a pile (lightly, not squashed) topped with a fried egg and a splurge of German mustard, or as a side with sausages or at a barbecue.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JE2x4_0VU08
Uploaded 2025-09-22.

recipes.title: Blender Chocolate Fudge Cake - A Near Disaster!!
ingredients: Buttermilk — 180 ml (¾ cup) (or milk with about 1 tbsp vinegar or lemon juice, left to sit)
Warm water or coffee (38–43°C / 100–110°F) — quantity not given in the description; in the video, 1 tsp instant coffee is dissolved in warm water
Corn syrup — 60 ml (¼ cup) (cane syrup or similar also works)
steps: Make buttermilk if needed: Stir about a tablespoon of apple cider vinegar (any vinegar, or lemon or lime juice) into milk and leave it; it splits into buttermilk within a few minutes.

Prep: Heat the oven to 175°C / 350°F. Grease and line the cake tin (the description says a 9-inch tin; the host used an 8-inch for a taller cake). Put the tin on a baking tray, because the batter overflowed in the video.
Blend the wet: Put the wet ingredients in the blender jug first (buttermilk, eggs, oil, the coffee in warm water, vanilla) and blend for 20–30 seconds.
Add the dry: Add the sugar, flour, cocoa, baking soda, baking powder and salt, pulsing it in in stages. Pulse only so the gluten isn't overworked, for a moist cake.
Bake: Pour into the tin and bake, checking at about 30 minutes. The host's cake took roughly 35–40 minutes (the description says 30–35 minutes until a toothpick comes out clean).
Cool: Turn the cake out onto its paper and let it cool.
Beat the butter: For the frosting, beat the butter until light, pale and fluffy, then beat in the cocoa (sifting isn't essential).
Melt the chocolate: Melt the chocolate chips with the corn syrup and a couple of tablespoons of cream.
Finish the frosting: Add a splash of vanilla and the powdered sugar to the butter and cocoa, add the melted chocolate and beat until glossy.
Frost and serve: Slather it over the cooled cake. It stays soft and fudgy rather than setting hard.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qAcfZvIC0uo
Uploaded 2025-09-21.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Warm water or coffee (100–110°F / 38–43°C); Preheat oven to 175°C / 350°F. Grease and line a 9-inch (23 cm) round cake tin; Bake for 30–35 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean.

recipes.title: Creamy LOADED JACKET Potato Soup
ingredients: Medium baking potatoes — 4 (900 g / 2 lb, cubed after peeling and dicing)
Chicken or vegetable stock — 4 cups (950 ml)
Salt — ½ tsp (2 g), adjusted to taste
Fresh chives or spring onions, chopped — 2 tbsp (10 g)
steps: Prep the potatoes: Peel and cube most of the potatoes, and take the skins off the scrubbed ones (any amount) to bake separately. Leftover roast potatoes also work for this soup.

Bake: Spread the cubes and skins on a tray with no oil, and bake in the oven (200°C in the description) for about half an hour until they take on colour and smell like baked potatoes, with crisp skins.
Cook the bacon: Cook the bacon in a pan until crispy and remove it, keeping about a tablespoon of the fat for flavour.
Start the soup base: Add butter and cook the onions and garlic with salt and pepper until they have a little colour. Herbs or chilli flakes are optional.
Add potatoes and stock: Add the baked potatoes and the stock, bring to the boil, then simmer for about 15–20 minutes until the potatoes are soft.
Mash or blend: Mash with a potato masher or blend (stick or jug blender). Don't take it too far, as you want some potato in there. Add more stock for a thinner soup.
Add dairy: Stir in the milk and the cream.
Add bacon, skins and cheese: Chop the bacon and stir in half, saving the rest for garnish. Slice the baked skins and stir some in. Stir in half the cheese.
Finish: Stir through a couple of tablespoons of sour cream.
Serve: Ladle into bowls and top with cheese, shredded potato skin, bacon, and green onion or chives. Leave out the bacon for a vegetarian version.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=WY8qv2Vgp18
Uploaded 2025-09-20.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Oven at 200 °C / 400 °F until the skins are crisp and the flesh is fluffy.

recipes.title: Traditional Cornish Figgy ’Obbin – Rustic Raisin Pastry
ingredients: Plain flour — 225 g (2 US cups / 1 UK cup)
Baking powder (if using plain flour) — 1 tsp (5 g)
Suet (beef or vegetable) — 100 g (⅔ US cup / ½ UK cup)
Cold water or milk — 75 ml (⅓ US cup)
Milk — a little, to brush the top
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 180°C and grease a tin or dish.
Mix the dry: Combine the plain flour, baking powder (which makes it self-raising) and salt.
Add suet and fruit: Mix in the suet (the host's was melted, but packet shredded suet can just be stirred in) and then the raisins (the host used black and golden for contrast).
Add liquid: Add water (or milk, or a mix), starting with half, to make a firm, thick, stodgy dough that is not sticky or soggy. Lightly bring it together with your hands without overmixing.
Roll: Roll it out about an inch thick into an oblong, then roll it up lightly like a roll, so it isn't too dense. It doesn't matter if it crumbles.
Place in the tin: Put it in the greased tin seam side down, and tap down.
Glaze: Brush with milk for goldenness and sprinkle with granulated sugar for a crusty top.
Bake: Bake for about 35–40 minutes until golden.
Serve: Cool a little, then slice and serve warm with custard. It should be soft inside with a crusty sugared top.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=RDw4qqGBsVQ
Uploaded 2025-09-19.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 180 °C / 350 °F / Gas 4. Grease a shallow tray or dish; Bake 35–40 minutes until golden and cooked through.

recipes.title: OLD SCHOOL Mince & Onion Slice Pie – Classic School Dinner Tray Bake
ingredients: Ready-made puff pastry — 2 large sheets (big enough to cover the tray)
Onion, large, finely diced — 200 g (7 oz)
Cornflour/cornstarch — 8 g (1 tbsp), with 15 ml (1 tbsp) cold water for a slurry (only if the stock isn't already thickened)
Fresh breadcrumbs — 20 g (2 tbsp) (optional, for a softer filling)
Dried thyme or mixed herbs — ½ tsp (1 g)
Salt — 1 tsp (6 g), adjust to taste
Egg white (to brush the base) and milk and water (to glaze the top)
steps: Brown the onions: Cook the onions slowly in a little oil until they have some colour, about 5 minutes. A pinch of salt (and optionally a teaspoon of brown sugar) helps them caramelise, though you don't want a sweet pie.
Brown the mince: Add the mince, breaking it up, season with salt and pepper and brown it off (even char it a little), since this is the only way to build flavour.
Add herbs and seasonings: Stir in a pinch of mixed herbs (or dried thyme), a splash of Worcestershire sauce and a tablespoon of tomato purée.
Add stock and thickener: Pour in about 250 ml beef stock. If you use cubes rather than powder, thicken it with a slurry of 1 tbsp cornflour and 1 tbsp water; gravy powder thickens by itself.
Add breadcrumbs: Stir in a little breadcrumbs, an old-school tip that soaks up the flavour and softens the filling.
Simmer and cool: Simmer for about 10 minutes, stirring so nothing sticks, then turn off the heat and let the filling cool completely before using it.
Line the tray: Heat the oven to 200°C. Line the 12 × 9 tin with a puff pastry sheet, tucking it in and leaving an overhang. Keep the other pastry under plastic so it doesn't dry out.
Seal the base: Brush the bottom pastry with egg white to help avoid a soggy bottom.
Fill: Add the filling and level it gently.
Lid: Cover with the second sheet, fold over and crimp the edge (or press with a fork).
Glaze and vent: Brush with milk and water (no egg, as there is too much to cover) and cut a couple of vent holes.
Bake and serve: Bake for 30–35 minutes until crisp and golden, then cut into squares. Traditionally served with chips and beans, chips and gravy or chips and mushy peas.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TifzgNzOxQw
Uploaded 2025-09-18.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 200°C (180°C fan) / 400°F; Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden, puffed, and crisp.

recipes.title: Hearty Cauliflower & Potato Soup – Creamy Comfort Food
ingredients: Cauliflower, chopped — 1 large head (800 g florets)
Milk or cream (or half and half) — 250 ml
Fresh thyme — 1 tsp (or ½ tsp dried)
Salt — 1 tsp (6 g), adjust to taste
Crispy bacon, chives, cheddar, or a sour cream swirl
steps: Roast the cauliflower: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the cauliflower into florets (the stalk can be roasted too), toss with a little olive oil on a tray and roast for about 20–25 minutes. Don't season it much, as the seasoning goes into the soup. Add the garlic to the tray after about 10–12 minutes so it roasts too.
Prep the veg: Cube the onion, celery, carrot and potatoes. Size doesn't matter because it will be blended.
Start the soup: Melt butter (or use a splash of oil) in a pan and cook the carrot and celery first, being the hardest, with salt and black pepper for a couple of minutes.
Add onion and thyme: Add the onions and a pinch of dried thyme to bloom with the veg.
Add potatoes: Stir in the potatoes; a little colour adds flavour. If the pan gets ahead of the cauliflower, turn it down or add a splash of stock so nothing burns.
Add cauliflower and stock: Add the roasted cauliflower and garlic, a bay leaf and the rest of the stock. Simmer for about 20 minutes, stirring now and then. Add boiling water if you want it thinner.
Optional garnish: Once the potatoes are soft, fish out a few bits of cauliflower to garnish if you like.
Blend: Remove the bay leaf and blend with a jug or stick blender. Taste for seasoning (the host wants more black pepper).
Add cream: Gently stir in the cream (milk or sour cream also works) and warm through without boiling.
Serve: Top with bacon, cauliflower and potato, cheddar or green herbs, and serve with crusty bread. Skip the bacon to keep it vegetarian.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=APzwoz6Zd-8
Uploaded 2025-09-17.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 200°C (180°C fan) / 400°F.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Old School Mince Cobbler
ingredients: Ground beef (mince) — 500 g (17.5 oz); chicken, pork or lamb mince also work
British mixed herbs — 1 tsp (5 g) (or dried thyme or mixed herbs)
Cornflour (cornstarch) — 1 tbsp (8 g) mixed with 2 tbsp (30 ml) cold water (only if the stock is thin)
Self-raising flour — 200 g (1⅓ UK cups / 1⅔ US cups)
Grated mature cheddar — 100 g (½ cup), plus extra for sprinkling
Fresh parsley or thyme, chopped — 1 tbsp (optional)
Milk — 100 ml, plus extra for brushing (optional)
steps: Brown the mince: Cook the mince in a little oil (or butter), seasoning with salt and black pepper, and cook off the water it releases.
Add herbs: Add a pinch of mixed herbs to rehydrate in the pan.
Add the veg: Once the water has cooked off, add the onions, carrot and celery (cubed small) and cook for a couple of minutes.
Add garlic: Clear a space and cook the garlic in the oil, then stir in.
Add tomato and Worcestershire: Cook in a tablespoon of tomato purée for a minute to cook out the sourness, then add a splash of Worcestershire.
Add stock: Add 500 ml beef stock. If made from a cube and watery, thicken with 1 tbsp cornflour mixed with 2 tbsp water; gravy granules thicken by themselves.
Simmer: Cook about 10 minutes until it thickens slightly. Don't take it too thick, as it cooks further in the oven with the cobbles. Turn off and let it cool in the pan.

Make the cobbles: Mix the self-raising flour with salt, a little pepper and a pinch of herbs. Rub in the cold butter between fingers and thumbs, then stir in some of the cheese (saving some for the top).
Add milk: Add the milk and bring to a dough without overworking it, or the cobbles come out thick and stodgy.
Heat the oven: Preheat to about 200°C.
Cut out the cobbles: Put the meat mixture in a dish (11 × 9 in). Pat the dough out to about ¾ inch and cut out as many cobbles as you can fit. They don't need to be even.
Top and bake: Lay the cobbles on top, add a little more cheese, and bake for about 25–30 minutes until golden on top and bubbling.
Serve: Serve with mashed potato or veg and plenty of gravy. The top is crisp and cheesy, the bottom stodgy from the gravy and the inside light and fluffy.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MwDwdAxU2Q4
Uploaded 2025-09-16.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake at 200°C (180°C fan) / 400°F for 25–30 minutes, until golden on top and bubbling underneath.

recipes.title: PEACH PIE - Classic with a twist
ingredients: Shortcrust pastry (ready-rolled) — enough for base + lattice top (about 500 g / 17.5 oz)
Tinned peaches, sliced — 1 large tin (approx. 820 g; about 480 g drained fruit)
Ground cinnamon — ½ tsp (1.5 g), a light dusting over the baked pie
Milk, for brushing the lattice — 2 tbsp (30 g)
Extra sugar, for sprinkling — 1 tbsp (12 g)
steps: Drain the peaches: Drain them really well and pat dry with kitchen towel so the custard doesn't go soggy. Slice them (or cube them if not already sliced).
Heat the oven: Preheat to about 190°C.
Make the custard: Beat the sour cream, egg yolk, vanilla, sugar and cornflour (for thickening) until smooth.
Line the dish: Roll out the pastry to fit the 9-inch dish, fit it in, and trim to leave a small overhang.
Fill: Lay in a good layer of peaches (neatness doesn't matter), then pour over the sour cream custard so it covers the peaches. It can be baked like this as a traditional peach pie.

Make the lattice: Roll out a lid from the trimmings, lay parchment over it and flip it, then cut with a lattice cutter and pull the lattice apart on the paper. Lay it over the pie, peel off the paper, and crimp the edge. (The host's lattice came out rough.)
Glaze and bake: Brush with milk and sprinkle with sugar, put the pie on a tray and bake for about 40–45 minutes until the filling is set and the lattice golden brown.
Finish and cool: Dust lightly with cinnamon and let the pie cool completely before cutting.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dDghdKHT20g
Uploaded 2025-09-15.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven: 190°C / 375°F (fan 170°C); Bake: 40–45 minutes, until the filling is set and the lattice is golden brown.

recipes.title: Chicken Pie with a Twist | High-Protein & Delicious
ingredients: Olive oil or butter — 2 tbsp (30 g)
Thyme — 1 tsp dried or a few sprigs fresh (the host used about 1 tsp herbes de Provence instead)
Salt and black pepper — to taste
Egg, beaten, for glazing — 1 (the host skipped the glaze in the video)
steps: Prep: Cube the carrots and celery, mince the garlic, dice the onion and cube the chicken. Swap out any veg you don't like.

Cook the lentils: Bring the chicken stock to the boil, add the rinsed red lentils and simmer for about 10–12 minutes, stirring so they don't stick, until soft and creamy but not fully cooked. Turn off the heat and set aside. (Green or brown lentils would need longer.)

Sear the chicken: Heat butter and oil, spread the chicken out and season with salt, pepper and smoked paprika. Sear for a couple of minutes without browning it too far, then take it out, leaving the pan juices.
Cook the veg: Add a little more butter, then the celery and carrots with a little salt (mind the stock's saltiness) for a couple of minutes, then the onion until the rawness goes, then the garlic.
Add herbs: Stir in about a teaspoon of herbs and let it bloom for about 30 seconds, then stir in the lentils.
Make the sauce: Add a good teaspoon of Dijon mustard and the milk, and let it thicken.
Add chicken: Return the chicken and its juices and cook about 5 minutes, thickening a bit more but keeping the filling nice and wet. Turn off the heat and let it cool.
Heat the oven: About 200°C.
Line the tin: Roll out ready-rolled pastry for the base and sides (a springform tin in the video) and a lid, leaving a little overhang.
Fill and lid: Fill the pie right to the top, lay on the lid, tuck the overhang over, and cut vents. Egg or milk wash is optional.
Bake: Bake on a tray for about 25–30 minutes until golden.
Serve: Let it cool a little before cutting.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IjMcdJAqysU
Uploaded 2025-09-14.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 25–30 minutes until golden.

recipes.title: Fully Loaded Cheeseburger Impossible Pie
ingredients: Streaky bacon, cooked crisp and chopped — 4 rashers (about 100 g)
Grated cheddar — 200 g (some in the filling, the rest on top)
Mayonnaise or sour cream — 2 tbsp (30 g) (the host used 1 tbsp of each)
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 180°C (350°F) and grease a 9-inch pie dish (the host used a 9 × 13 dish).
Prep: Dice the onion (large dice so it mixes through the meat like a cheeseburger), chop the pickles, and cook and chop the bacon.
Brown the beef: Cook the mince, seasoning with black pepper and salt now as it's the only chance to season the meat, and cook off the water until you're down to the oil.
Add onion, bacon and oregano: Add the onions to cook out the rawness, a pinch of oregano and the cooked bacon. Let the mince char a little for extra flavour, then turn off the heat.
Make the batter: Mix the flour, baking powder, a little pepper and a tiny bit of salt, then add the eggs and milk. Stir in the mayo and sour cream, ketchup and American mustard.
Assemble: Spread the meat and onions in the dish without squashing them down, add the dill pickles and a little cheese, then pour over the batter and top with more cheese.
Bake: Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden brown on top and set in the centre.
Cool and serve: Let it cool down before cutting. Serve with extra ketchup and American mustard.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NblqzLiH3jg
Uploaded 2025-09-13.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 180°C (350°F). Grease a 9-inch (23 cm) pie dish; Bake for 30–35 minutes, until golden brown on top and set in the centre.

recipes.title: Mackerel or Sardine & Broccoli Crustless Quiche
ingredients: Tinned mackerel (or sardines) in tomato sauce — 2 cans, drained of excess sauce, flaked (approx. 300 g / 10.5 oz)
Broccoli florets, lightly blanched — 200 g (7 oz / 2 cups)
Tomato sauce from the tin — about 2 tbsp (as spoken in the video)
steps: Cook the onion and garlic: Soften the onion in butter with a little salt (about a minute), add the garlic, then put them in a bowl. Use the same pan for the next step.

Blanch the broccoli: Bring boiling water from the kettle to the boil in the pan, add the broccoli florets for 2–3 minutes (an ice bath isn't worth it here), then drain, keeping some crunch. Keep a couple of florets back for the top if you like.
Heat the oven: About 180°C.
Start the custard: Beat the eggs with salt, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg.
Prepare the fish: Drain the tins, keeping a bit of tomato sauce. Flake the fish with a fork without mashing it. The bones are edible, so removing them is up to you.
Finish the custard: Add the cream and milk to the eggs, plus about 2 tablespoons of the tomato sauce from the tins for richness (both tins' sauce is fine too).
Assemble: Butter a 9-inch dish and layer in the broccoli, the flaked fish spaced evenly and the onions, then a light layer of cheese, saving a little for the top.
Add the custard: Pour the custard over gently, so it finds its own way to the bottom, and top with the rest of the cheese.
Bake: Bake for 30–35 minutes at 180°C until nicely coloured and set.
Cool and serve: Let it cool, as it sets up better, and top with the reserved broccoli. Serve warm or cold with salad.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=B0eqUP-MKzY
Uploaded 2025-09-12.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven – 180°C (350°F). Grease or line a 9-inch (23 cm) pie dish; Bake – 30–35 minutes until golden and just set in the centre.

recipes.title: Ham and Potato Bake with Cheddar Crust
ingredients: For a greased 2 L / 9 × 13-inch baking dish.
Potatoes, peeled and thinly sliced — 1 kg (2.2 lb; about 6 medium)
Cooked ham, diced — 250 g (9 oz), or more
Cheddar, shredded — 200 g (7 oz) (reserve half for the topping)
Milk — 300 ml (1 cup), plus a splash more if too thick
Paprika (smoked in the video) — ½ tsp (3 g)
Salt — ½ tsp (3 g), adjust to taste
Herbs of choice — 1 tsp (the host added a little thyme and parsley)
Mustard — 1 tsp, adjust to taste (optional; English mustard plus a little Dijon in the video)
Panko breadcrumbs — 2 tbsp (15 g) (optional, for extra crunch)
steps: Slice the potatoes: Slice them roughly the same thickness and keep in water.
Par-boil: Boil in lightly salted water for only 5–7 minutes, stirring to separate the slices, then drain.
Prep: Dice the onion and cut the ham into small pieces.
Start the sauce: Melt the butter and sauté the onions with herbs, salt and black pepper to take out the rawness.
Add ham and spices: Add the ham to warm through, then the garlic powder and paprika.
Make a roux: Stir in a couple of tablespoons of flour and cook briefly, then loosen with a little milk, then add the rest of the milk and the cream. It thickens naturally.

Flavour and cheese: Add the mustard and half the cheeses (turn off the heat for this), stirring until melted. If too thick add a splash of milk, but it should be a thick sauce, as it thickens more in the oven.
Heat the oven: About 190°C.
Layer: Put about half the warm potatoes in the dish, then half the sauce, spread out, then another layer of potatoes and the rest of the sauce, levelled with a spoon.
Top: Sprinkle a couple of tablespoons of panko over, then cheddar on top with a little mozzarella.
Bake: Bake uncovered for about 30–35 minutes until bubbling with a golden crust.
Rest and serve: Leave it for about 5 minutes, then serve with any veg. It freezes well.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NS9QDycMjVk
Uploaded 2025-09-11.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake uncovered at 190°C / 375°F for 30–35 minutes, until bubbling and golden on top.

recipes.title: 10 Minute Chocolate Swiss Roll in a Frying Pan - No Oven Cake
ingredients: For 1 Swiss roll, about 8 slices. The host used a 12-inch pan.
Whipped cream (sweetened to your choice) or chocolate ganache — about 150 g
steps: Blend the eggs: Blend the eggs and sugar together.
Mix the dry: In another bowl, whisk the flour, baking powder, cocoa powder and salt.
Combine: Add the oil, milk and a squirt of vanilla to the egg mixture, then fold in the dry mix with a sturdy spatula until it's all incorporated.
Prep the pan: Use a non-stick pan with a piece of parchment cut to fit on the bottom (to help it come out), greased with a little oil.
Cook: Pour in the batter and level it, as it's a sponge. Cover with a lid and cook on the lowest heat for only about 6 minutes, without flipping, until the top is light and spongy.
Turn out and roll: Turn off the heat, lift the cake out, peel the parchment off the other side, and gently roll it up in parchment while still warm. If it cracks, it cracks.
Fill: Unroll, spread with lightly whipped cream, and roll it back up like a sandwich roll. Chill in the fridge for a couple of minutes.
Make the ganache: Melt about 150 g chocolate with a pinch of salt and a little milk in the frying pan (or over a pan of water), then turn off the heat.
Finish: Pour over the cake and chill for as long as you like to set up. The host likens the texture to a brownie.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N3igU8huuO4
Uploaded 2025-09-10.

recipes.title: Mexican Impossible Pie
ingredients: Ground beef or chicken — 500 g (1 lb)
Taco seasoning — 2 tbsp (15 g) (homemade or a packet)
Bell pepper, diced — 1 medium (120 g) (any colour)
Cheddar or Mexican cheese blend, shredded — 150 g (1½ cups)
Salsa, sour cream or guacamole, and a salad
steps: Prep: Dice the onion and pepper, mince the garlic, and have the corn ready.
Make the batter: Mix the flour, baking powder, salt and pepper, then add the eggs and milk. The host says it is thin enough to nearly make Yorkshire puddings. Set aside.
Cook the onions: Sauté the onions in a little oil with a pinch of salt and pepper.
Add the meat: Add the beef and cook it off, seasoning with a little more salt and pepper, and cooking off the water.
Add taco seasoning: Stir in a couple of tablespoons of taco seasoning and the garlic.
Add pepper and corn: Add the pepper and corn and cook just a minute, as it cooks more in the oven. Turn off the heat.
Heat the oven: Preheat to about 180°C (the host says 170°C at one point). Use a 9 × 13 inch dish, or bigger if you have more mixture.

Assemble: Put some of the mince mixture in the dish with some cheese, then a little batter, then the rest of the mince, then the rest of the batter (so it mixes into the crust for a firm-bodied pie), and finish with cheese on top.
Bake: Bake for about 30–35 minutes until golden, set and bubbling.
Rest and serve: Let it cool for about 5 minutes, then serve with a dollop of sour cream, salsa, guacamole or salad.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EKQkd6rSCzs
Uploaded 2025-09-09.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 180°C / 350°F. Grease a 9-inch x 13-inch (23 cm); Bake: Place in oven and bake 30–35 minutes, until golden and set in the center.

recipes.title: Taco Seasoning
ingredients: Cayenne pepper — ½–1 tsp (1–2 g), adjust to heat preference
steps: Combine: Put all the spices in a bowl (the host uses smoked paprika; sweet works too). Cayenne is optional if you don't like it spicy. Cornflour and sugar are optional extras; the sugar tempers any bitterness.
Mix: Stir it all together, breaking up the onion and garlic powder, which absorb moisture from the air.
Store: Spoon into an airtight container. The host adds a couple of silica gel packets to stop it clumping. It keeps for weeks.
How to use: Two tablespoons per 500 g of meat (beef, chicken, pork or anything). For a wet "taco gravy" to cook the meat in, use 2 tablespoons with 150 ml of water.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=nIH0b1Tgmmk
Uploaded 2025-09-09.

recipes.title: Chicken & Pepper Stir Fry
ingredients: Chicken breast or thigh, thinly sliced — 250 g (9 oz)
Bell peppers (red, yellow or green), sliced — 2 medium (≈ 250 g)
Water or chicken stock — 60 ml (4 tbsp)
Cornstarch — 1 tsp (3 g) dissolved in 2 tsp (10 ml) water as a slurry (optional)
steps: Prep: Mince the garlic. Slice the onion and pull the segments apart to give it a head start. Slice the peppers and the chicken.

Velvet the chicken: Mix the chicken with baking soda (¼ tsp, which tenderises), light soy sauce, white pepper, a little cornflour, an optional splash of Shaoxing wine, a little water (to get moisture into the chicken) and a touch of oil. Marinate for about 15 minutes.

Make the sauce: Combine the oyster sauce, light soy sauce, sesame oil, chicken stock (or water) and a little cornflour. Add white pepper to the sauce or over the finished stir fry. A separate slurry is only needed if you want it thicker. Don't worry about lumps; they dissolve as it cooks.
Flash-fry the veg: In a hot pan with a little oil, quickly fry the peppers and onions, then return them to the bowl and cover with a lid so they steam, soft outside and crunchy inside.
Cook the chicken: In the pan with a little oil, stir-fry the chicken until about 80% cooked, then add the garlic.
Combine: Return the veg, add the stock or water and then the sauce, and stir through until it thickens and just coats everything.
Serve: Serve over rice. (The description notes there is fan/hood noise in the quiet parts of the video.)
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=rzX4sIxvBTs
Uploaded 2025-09-08.

recipes.title: Wartime Eggless Sponge Cake (Dense Depression Cake)
ingredients: For a 7–8 inch (18–20 cm) round or square tin.
Baking soda / bicarbonate of soda — 1 tsp (5 g)
Vinegar (malt, cider, or white) — 1 tbsp (15 ml)
Vegetable oil (or melted margarine/dripping) — 60 ml (4 tbsp)
Mixed spice (or cinnamon) — ½ tsp (optional; the host used about a teaspoon of English mixed spice)
steps: Heat the oven: Preheat to 170°C (340°F). Grease and line the tin (see the tip in step 7).
Mix the dry: In a bowl combine the plain flour, salt, sugar, baking soda (not baking powder) and the mixed spice (or cinnamon). Any sugar you have works.

Mix the wet: In another bowl combine the water, vegetable oil, vanilla and about a tablespoon of vinegar. The vinegar makes the carbon dioxide that lifts the cake and cooks off without tasting of vinegar.
Combine: Pour the wet mix into the dry and stir just enough to get rid of the flour lumps without overmixing. It makes a very loose batter.
Bake: Pour into the tin (the host used a 7-inch springform) and bake for about 25–30 minutes (the description says 30–35 minutes), until a skewer comes out clean.
Cool: Leave in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out and cool fully on a rack. It keeps well wrapped in parchment in a tin and is better the next day.

Springform lining tip: To avoid leaks and sticking, cut a piece of baking paper bigger than the tin, turn the springform base upside down with the paper over it, then lock the tin over it so the paper sits flat inside. When the cake is baked it slides off on its paper.
Serve: Slice and serve with tea. The host suggests ground ginger instead of mixed spice for a ginger cake, optionally drizzled with golden syrup.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=eu9n5v538Rs
Uploaded 2025-09-07.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Grease and line a 7–8 inch (18–20 cm) round or square tin. Preheat oven to 170°C (340°F); Bake for 30–35 minutes until firm and a skewer comes out clean; Leave in tin 10 minutes, then turn out to cool fully. Keeps well wrapped, and tastes better the next day.

recipes.title: Carrot & Lentil Soup
ingredients: Red split lentils, rinsed — 200 g (7 oz)
Stock — 1 litre (the description says vegetable; the host says "chicken stock" in the video)
Dried parsley — ½ tsp (1 g) (or 1 tsp dried mixed herbs instead)
Salt — 1 tsp (6 g), or to taste
Lemon juice — 1 tbsp (15 ml) (optional, for brightness)
A swirl of yogurt or cream, butter, toast
steps: Prep: Dice the onion and carrots (as big or small as you like, depending on how much you blend). Mince the garlic and rinse the lentils.
Start the onion: Heat olive oil over a moderate flame (it doesn't need to be high) and sauté the onion for about a minute.
Add carrot, garlic and seasoning: Add the carrots, then the garlic, with salt and pepper, the dried parsley and the dried thyme to bloom in the oil.
Add cumin: Stir in about a teaspoon of ground cumin and coat the carrots.
Add lentils: Stir in the rinsed lentils and coat them in the flavour.
Add liquid: Add the stock and some water as well, since the lentils absorb a lot, and bring to the boil.
Simmer: Simmer uncovered for about 25–30 minutes so it thickens, stirring often so the lentils don't catch on the bottom. Scum from the lentils can be skimmed off or left.
Blend or mash: For a rustic soup, squeeze it down with a potato masher while still on the heat; or use a hand blender for smoother.
Finish: Turn off the heat, check seasoning and stir in a little lemon juice for freshness.
Serve: Ladle into bowls, optionally with yogurt or cream, a little butter and toast. 500 g carrots costs next to nothing, and the lentils add protein.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DMFUCy4RU7U
Uploaded 2025-09-06.

recipes.title: Pulled Beef Cheese Melt with Horseradish & Caramelised Onions
ingredients: Pulled beef (leftover, with a little gravy to keep it moist) — 200 g (7 oz; about 1 cup packed)
Bread (thick slices, sourdough, crusty or white) — 2–4 slices
Cheddar, grated or sliced — 100 g (1 cup)
Olive oil — 1 tbsp (15 ml) (the host used butter and oil)
steps: Slice the onions: Slice them thinly.

Steam-start the onions: In a pan with a lid, add the onions with a little butter and/or oil, a little sugar (helps caramelise) and a little salt (draws out moisture), plus a splash of boiling water from the kettle. Put the lid on and cook so they boil and steam.

Caramelise: When the water has boiled off, take the lid off, turn the heat down and keep turning the onions until caramelised, about 15 minutes in total. Stop when they're as dark as you want. Turn off the heat.

Make the butter mix: Slice thick pieces of crusty bread. Cream a tablespoon of mayo with a tablespoon of butter and spread it on one side of each slice right up to the edges (this side goes down in the pan).
Warm the beef: Rewarm the pulled beef with its little bit of gravy. You can caramelise it a bit for extra flavour.
Build the sandwich: On the unbuttered side, spread a decent layer of horseradish sauce, then add cheddar, pulled beef, caramelised onions and mozzarella, and top with the other slice.

Cook from cold: Put the sandwich into a completely cold non-stick pan, put on a very low flame and cover with a lid, pressing down if necessary. The heat builds slowly, everything melts and the bottom toasts. You don't need loads of butter or a high flame.
Flip: Carefully turn the sandwich (the hardest part) to toast the top, lid back on, until golden. Turn off the heat and let it sit a moment.
Serve: Serve hot; it's a knife-and-fork job.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A_4Cw_ev7I4
Uploaded 2025-09-05.

recipes.title: How To Make Roasted Chicken Stock for Richer Soups and Gravies
ingredients: Roasted chicken carcass (from a whole chicken, roasted 35 minutes or more) — 1 (the host used about 3 kg of carcasses in total)
Any veg stalks of choice (the host used parsley stalks)
Cold water — enough to cover everything
Olive oil — a drizzle on the carcass (optional, as the host does)
steps: Roast the carcass: Heat the oven to about 200°C. Drizzle the carcass with a little olive oil (don't season it) and roast for about 20 minutes, then turn it over.

Add veg to roast: When turning, add some peeled, cubed onion, carrot and celery around the chicken to caramelise for the last stretch. Skins are left off the onion at this stage to avoid burnt flavours. This is optional. Keep roasting until golden (the host gave it about another 30 minutes).
Know the ratios: Per kilo of bones, use about 500 g mirepoix: 50% onion (250 g), and 25% each celery and carrot (125 g each). Add peppercorns, bay leaves and thyme.
Chop the rest: Roughly chop the remaining onion, celery, carrot and parsley stalks, as it will all be strained out (onion skin can stay on or be left off).

Combine in the pot: Put the carcass with all its juices, the roasted veg, the chopped mirepoix, peppercorns, bay leaf and thyme in a big pan. Cover with water by a couple of inches, keeping the chicken off the bottom.

Simmer: Bring to the boil, then simmer gently. Skimming the foam is up to you (most professional kitchens don't, as it's strained). For a light mild stock simmer about 2 hours; for a more intense one up to 8 hours; the host used about 4 hours.
Strain: Turn off the heat, drain the contents to leave the liquid, then pass it through a sieve (twice, or with cheesecloth if needed).
Chill and de-fat: Cool, then refrigerate. The fat sets on top, so lift it off. This chicken fat can be used for cooking like oil. Strain again finely if you wish and store.
Light stock option: For a light chicken stock, boil the bones without roasting them.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OdtVy0Bh5u4
Uploaded 2025-09-04.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Yorkshire Fish Cake Bites
ingredients: White fish fillets or scraps (cod, haddock, whiting, pollock, any white fish), cut into small chunks — 250 g (9 oz)
Potatoes, peeled and sliced into 4 mm rounds (about 1½ inch diameter) — 400 g (14 oz)
Ground rice ("rice cones"; blitz plain dry uncooked rice) — 60 g (6 tbsp)
Water — 200 ml (as listed in the description; the potatoes are par-boiled in salted water)
Baking soda (bicarbonate of soda) — 1 tsp (5 g)
Malt vinegar (or white vinegar) — 2 tsp (10 ml)
Oil for deep frying (vegetable, beef dripping, or lard) — enough to cover the fish cakes in the pan
steps: Par-boil the potatoes: Boil the potato slices in salted water for about 4 minutes, until just pliable, then drain and let them cool and air-dry.
Make rice cones: Blitz plain dry rice (any type) in a blender or chopper into ground rice. It absorbs moisture from the fish.

Make the batter base: Mix the flour with 1 tsp baking soda (not baking powder) and add water until it's the consistency of single cream. It shouldn't be too thick; if too thin add more flour. Set aside.
Prep the fish: Slice the fish bits thinly.

Assemble the bites: Dust a potato slice with rice cones, put a little fish on it, dust the fish with more rice cones, and top with a second slice of potato, so the rice cones are trapped inside. Roll the little sandwich in rice cones so the batter sticks.
Heat the oil: Heat enough oil to deep fry to about 175–180°C.
Activate the batter: Just before frying, stir the vinegar into the batter; the vinegar and baking soda make carbon dioxide bubbles for a light, crispy batter. Don't make it ahead.

Batter and fry: Dip each bite in batter using your fingers (so you don't strip the batter off), lower it into the oil and fry, turning, for about 3–4 minutes until golden and cooked through from both sides. Keep warm in a low oven while frying the rest.
Scraps: Drizzle batter scraps into the oil too, and use them to soak up the salt and vinegar.
Serve: Pile on a plate with salt and more vinegar and eat with your hands.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MBYQQKfWLyY
Uploaded 2025-09-03.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Heat oil to 175°C / 350°F.

recipes.title: Cauliflower Cheese Bread Pudding
ingredients: Butter, unsalted — 2 tbsp (28 g) (1 tbsp melted for roasting the cauliflower; the rest to cook the onions)
Fresh thyme (or parsley), chopped — 1 tsp (1 g) (the host used a pinch of dried thyme)
Mozzarella — a little (added in the video, no quantity given)
steps: Roast the cauliflower: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Toss the florets with melted butter, salt and pepper on a tray and roast for about 20 minutes.
Prep the bread: Rip or cube the day-old bread.
Cook the onions: Sauté the onions in butter and oil for 3–4 minutes with a little salt, add the garlic and a good pinch of dried thyme and cook until a little colour.

Make the cheese sauce: Turn the heat down and add the milk and cream, warm through, then take off the heat and stir in a teaspoon of Dijon, black pepper, the cheddar, mozzarella and Parmesan until melted. Let it cool a little.
Make the custard: Beat the eggs and stir them into the cooled cheesy mixture (if it's too hot the eggs would scramble).
Mix: Pour over the bread and stir really well so there is little dry bread, though dry bits crisp up.
Add the cauliflower: Fold in the roasted cauliflower with its juices.
Assemble: Tip into a 9 × 13 dish set on a tray. Add some cheese through it, and top with the rest of the mix, more cheese, Parmesan and mozzarella.
Bake: Bake for about 35 minutes (the description says at 180°C / 350°F for 35–40 minutes uncovered) until golden brown, bubbling and set.
Serve: Rest a few minutes and serve with a spoon, as a side or main. Baked beans go well on the side.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z29LFosnI_A
Uploaded 2025-09-02.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 200°C / 400°F; Bake uncovered at 180°C / 350°F for 35–40 minutes, until golden brown and set.

recipes.title: Crunchy Cornflake Peanut Butter Squares – NO BAKE Classic!
ingredients: Makes 16 squares in a 20 × 20 cm / 8 × 8 inch tray.
Golden syrup (or corn syrup/honey/maple syrup) — 120 g (90 ml / 6 tbsp)
Light brown sugar — 75 g (⅓ cup, packed)
Chocolate, melted and drizzled or spread — 100 g (optional topping; the host melts it with a little milk, a pinch of salt and a tiny bit of butter for sheen)
steps: Melt the base: In a pan, melt the butter, then add the sugar, syrup and peanut butter with a pinch of salt (as much as you like, depending on how salty the peanuts are) and a little vanilla. Warm until fully incorporated, but don't boil it hard.
Add cornflakes: Turn off the heat and stir in the cornflakes until fully coated.

Press into the tin: Press into a lined tin (the host used a 9 × 7 for thicker bars), squashing it down with a spoon. For firmer bars, crush some of the cornflakes so they bind with the whole ones. The host kept them loose and crunchy.
Make the chocolate topping: Melt chocolate in a pan with a little milk, a tiny bit of salt and a tiny bit of butter, then drizzle or spread it over the top. It sinks in between the flakes.
Chill: Let it cool, then chill in the fridge for 1 hour or until set.
Cut and store: Cut into squares or bars. They keep in an airtight container for up to 5 days.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ZLuwUvP_ST8
Uploaded 2025-09-01.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Chill in the fridge for 1 hour or until set.

recipes.title: Dumplings in Heinz Tomato Soup 1960s–70s Thrifty UK Classic
ingredients: Self-raising flour — 200 g (1½ cups UK / 1⅔ cups US)
Shredded suet (or cold grated butter) — 100 g (½ cup)
Cold water — about 100 ml (7 tbsp), enough to form a dough
Heinz Cream of Tomato Soup — 2 tins (800 g; 2 × 280 ml cans UK / 2 × 295 ml cans US)
Water — 300 ml (swill out the cans with it)
Dried mixed herbs or black pepper — a pinch (optional)
Crusty bread, grated cheese on top (optional)
steps: Mix the dry: Stir the self-raising flour with the baking powder (extra) and salt, or the dumplings won't taste of anything.

Add suet: Crumble in the suet (vegetable or beef; butter also works but rises a bit less) like pastry. The host prefers to rub it in rather than just adding water. Herbs can be added for herby dumplings, but not here.
Add water: Add water a little at a time, mixing, until it's a dough that isn't sticky.
Shape: Break it into eight pieces and bring each together lightly, without squashing, so it stays light and airy. Cracks are fine.

Prepare the soup: In a pan, combine the tomato soup with about 300 ml water (swilling out the cans), black pepper and a pinch of herbs (Italian, English mixed, herbes de Provence, anything). Warm through without boiling. Any soup works, such as a chunky vegetable soup.
Add dumplings: Turn down to a simmer, add the dumplings and put on a lid.
Cook: Cook for about 20–25 minutes until the dumplings puff up.
Serve: Serve with crusty bread for dunking and optionally grated cheese on top.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PuvJC2E55f8
Uploaded 2025-08-31.

recipes.title: CHICKEN and CABBAGE Stir-Fry - Tender and Juicy
ingredients: Cabbage, shredded — 300 g (10.6 oz; 2 US cups)
Chicken breast, diced or sliced — 285 g (10 oz)
Green onions — 2 stalks, cut into 2-inch (5 cm) pieces
Dark soy sauce — ½ tsp (2.5 ml)
steps: Prep the veg: Mince the garlic, julienne the ginger, and cut the green onions, using the white end in the cooking and the leaf ends stirred through at the end. Cut the cabbage and pull the leaves apart to make stir-frying easier.

Velvet the chicken: Slice the chicken and mix with the soy sauce, dark soy (for colour), water, sugar, white pepper, baking soda (to velvet) and cornflour, with a little sesame oil. Mix by hand and marinate for no more than about 15 minutes.

Make the sauce and slurry: Mix the rice wine, soy sauce and dark soy for the sauce, and stir the cornflour into the water for a slurry, which forms the base of the sauce and helps it stick to the chicken and cabbage.

Stir-fry the cabbage: In a hot pan with oil, stir-fry the cabbage very quickly with a little salt and sugar and a splash of rice wine to bring out the sweetness. It only softens, then goes back into a bowl where it steams and stays crunchy.
Fry the aromatics and chicken: Add a little oil, then the ginger and green onion whites on a moderate flame, then the chicken, frying until it has some colour and the colour is even. Add the garlic.
Add sauce: Add the sauce and a splash of rice wine, letting the chicken take a little crust. Pour in the cornstarch-water mixture and stir until it thickens.
Combine: Return the cabbage, stir through, turn off the heat and stir in the green onion tops.
Serve: Serve straight away. The chicken is soft and juicy and the cabbage is still crunchy and sweet with ginger.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=cm0LVUEB63Q
Uploaded 2025-08-30.

recipes.title: CREAMY Mushroom MARSALA SAUCE It Will Make You FORGET the Main Course!
ingredients: Cremini or white mushrooms, sliced — 2 cups (200 g)
Marsala wine (dry or sweet) — ½ cup (120 ml)
Heavy cream (double cream) — ½ cup (120 ml)
Chicken or vegetable broth — ¼ cup (60 ml)
Fresh thyme leaves — 1 tsp (1 g) (or ¼ tsp dried)
Salt — to taste, approx. ½ tsp (3 g)
Black pepper, freshly ground — to taste, approx. ¼ tsp
steps: Prep: Mince the garlic (chunks are fine, or squash it to a paste with a knife). Wipe and slice the mushrooms (any type), cutting off the side so they sit flat.

Brown the mushrooms: Heat butter (you can keep a little to stir in at the end for gloss) and olive oil, add the mushrooms with a little salt and pepper (which draws out moisture) and cook for about 6–7 minutes until they have some colour. Don't rush.
Add thyme: Add about ¼ tsp dried thyme (or fresh) to rehydrate in the mushroom liquid.
Add garlic: After about 5–6 minutes, add the garlic and cook for a minute.
Add Marsala: Pour in the Marsala and reduce by about half.
Add stock and cream: Turn the flame down and add the stock and about half a cup (120 ml) of cream. Warm it up steadily and thicken a little, as thick as you like. No flour needed.
Finish: Stir through the optional parsley and serve over steak (also good on chicken, mashed potato or pasta).
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Tet6_uvrLpU
Uploaded 2025-08-29.

recipes.title: Chicken Pot Pie Bread Pudding
ingredients: For a 9 × 13 inch (23 × 33 cm) baking dish.
Cooked chicken, diced or shredded (leftover) — 2 cups (300 g)
Day-old bread, cubed or torn — 6 cups (about 300 g)
Milk or cream — 1 cup (240 ml) (for the sauce), plus a splash of milk in the egg custard
Fresh thyme (or ½ tsp dried) — 1 tsp (1 g)
Shredded cheddar or mozzarella — 1 cup (115 g) (the host used mozzarella)
steps: Prep: Mince the garlic, dice the carrot, onion and celery, and have the peas ready. Beat the eggs with a splash of milk for the custard. Break up the bread in a bowl.

Cook the veg: In butter and oil, start the carrots with a little salt for about a minute, then add the celery, then the onion, and then the garlic with black pepper and dried thyme (seasoning now so it blooms). Don't worry if there is some colour.

Make the sauce: Stir in a couple of generous tablespoons of flour and cook it out, then add the chicken stock gradually so it thickens, but keep it fairly fluid so the bread can soak it up. Add the milk (or cream).
Add chicken, peas and cheese: Stir in the chicken and then the peas, plus some mozzarella for cheesy creaminess. No need to boil it, as everything is cooked.
Heat the oven: About 180°C.
Soak the bread: Tip the filling over the bread, stir, and leave about 10 minutes, stirring gently.

Add custard: Stir about half the egg and milk custard through for richness, put it in the 9 × 13 dish (don't squash it, so the custard finds its way through the crevices), then pour the rest over the top so it sets like a pot pie crust. Top with mozzarella.
Bake covered: Make a loose foil tent so it steams, and bake for 25 minutes.
Bake uncovered: Remove the foil and bake another 20 minutes until golden and set.
Serve: It's very moist but doesn't run with sauce like a pot pie; use more liquid if you want it saucier, though the bread gets soggy.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7wsYxeHfPvk
Uploaded 2025-08-28.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Bake – Cover with foil and bake at 180°C / 350°F for 25 minutes. Remove foil and bake another 20 minutes until golden and set.

recipes.title: EASY Mascarpone Cheese - The Real Way - LOW FAT - No Lemon!
ingredients: Heavy cream (ideally minimum 35% fat; the host used UHT cream at 33.5%) — 1 litre (about 4 US cups)
Tartaric acid — ½ tsp (about 2.4 g), dissolved in 2 tbsp hot water
Cheesecloth and a sieve — for draining
steps: Heat the cream: Pour the cream into a pan and heat it to about 85–90°C (185–194°F), which is steaming but not boiling, stirring now and then so it doesn't catch on the pan.
Dissolve the acid: Meanwhile dissolve the tartaric acid in about 2 tablespoons of hot water and set aside. (Commercial mascarpone uses tartaric acid, not lemon.)

Add the acid and cook: At about 85°C stir in the dissolved tartaric acid and cook gently at the same temperature for about 5 minutes. It noticeably thickens, and is ready when it coats the back of a spoon.
Cool: Turn off the heat and let it come down to room temperature (a couple of hours), then put it in the fridge for about 4 hours to thicken. A thicker set means more cheese stays in the cloth.

Drain: Line a sieve set over a bowl with cheesecloth, scoop the mixture in, wrap it up and put a weight on top (the more weight, the firmer the cheese; keep it light for a firm but spreadable result). Return it to the fridge for about 6–8 hours (the description says 8–12 hours).

Store: Transfer to an airtight container. It keeps in the fridge for about 5–7 days (the description says up to 5 days). The host's yield was about 900 g from a litre of UHT cream (the captions also give a weighed figure that reads as 88 g, which appears to be an auto-caption error).
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Z5gH5QoZ6uE
Uploaded 2025-08-27.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Heat the cream 85–90 °C (185–194 °F), stirring constantly to prevent scorching; Refrigerate – Cover and refrigerate for 8–12 hours to drain.

recipes.title: Chicken and Broccoli Stir Fry
ingredients: Ginger, sliced or julienned — a few slices (no quantity given)
Chicken breast, thinly sliced on an angle — 330 g (12 oz)
White pepper powder — ⅛ tsp (0.5 g)
Water — ⅓ cup (80 ml) (for the pan sauce)
steps: Prep: Mince the garlic and julienne the ginger. Cut broccoli into florets and slice the stalks too.

Marinate the chicken: Slice the chicken on an angle and mix with soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar, baking soda (to velvet and soften), white pepper, cooking wine, water and cornflour. Leave for 15 minutes. Tofu can replace the chicken, but don't velvet it.
Mix the sauce: Combine the dark soy, oyster sauce and a little sugar.

Blanch the broccoli: Fry the ginger in a little oil over moderate heat, add the broccoli with a little salt and sugar, a splash of water and a splash of cooking wine. Don't let it brown. Take it out into a bowl and cover with a lid so it steams and stays crunchy.
Cook the chicken: Add a little oil and cook the chicken until about 80% cooked, with some colour, turning it over. Add the garlic.
Add sauce: Add the sauce and water. The cornflour on the chicken thickens it into a sauce. A dab more Shaoxing wine and a couple of drops of sesame oil are optional.
Combine: Return the broccoli, turn off the heat and stir through.
Serve: Serve with a shake of white pepper (optional) over rice or noodles.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h4qMW_nfTqw
Uploaded 2025-08-26.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Marinate the chicken Let sit for 15 minutes.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Cheesy Pepperoni Pizza Rolls - Golden on the outside Gooey on the Inside!
ingredients: Low-carb tortillas (about 20 cm / 8 in each) — 8 (any store-bought tortillas, or gluten-free)
Shredded mozzarella — 120 g (4.2 oz) (cheeses can be mixed)
Pepperoni slices — 16 slices (about 50 g), with some diced to go inside (salami, ham or bacon also work)
steps: Prep the filling: Finely chop the pepperoni (or salami, ham or bacon, or a mix) and dice the onion (optional). Mushrooms or sliced tomatoes can also go in.
Make garlic butter: Stir the garlic powder into the melted butter so it rehydrates.
Heat the oven: Preheat to 200°C (400°F) and get a suitable tray.
Fill the tortillas: Spread a little pizza sauce on each tortilla, leaving a border, then add mozzarella, the chopped pepperoni and a little onion.
Roll loosely: Roll each wrap loosely (not tight) and place seam side down on the tray.
Top: Brush with the garlic butter, lay three slices of pepperoni (or salami) on each roll, add more cheese, and sprinkle dried oregano. These can be prepped ahead and kept in the fridge.
Bake: Bake for about 10–12 minutes (the host says up to about 20 depending on the oven) until the cheese is melted, the ends are crisp and golden, and the rolls are heated through.
Serve: Serve with a salad, optionally with a little parsley.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ui81dKYdoUk
Uploaded 2025-08-25.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Preheat oven to 200 °C / 400 °F; Bake for 10–12 minutes, until the cheese is melted, edges are golden, and rolls are heated through.

recipes.title: Chicken Fillet Ala King
ingredients: Chicken breast, sliced into thin fillets — 520 g (about 1 lb 2 oz)
Cooking oil — enough for shallow frying
Onion, finely chopped — ½ medium (50 g)
Green bell pepper, diced — 2 tbsp (20 g)
Red bell pepper, diced — 2 tbsp (20 g) (optional, for colour)
Button mushrooms, sliced — ½ cup (50 g)
Chicken stock — 1 cup (240 ml) (low-sodium if possible)
Chicken bouillon cube — ½ cube (5 g) (skip if the stock is well seasoned)
Salt — start with ¼ tsp (1.5 g) (little needed, as the batter has fish sauce)
Black pepper — start with ¼ tsp (1 g)
Marsala wine, dry sherry or white wine — 1 tbsp (optional, for extra depth)
steps: Make the batter: Mix the beaten egg, flour, cornflour, garlic powder, black pepper and fish sauce into a thick, really sticky batter. If it's too stodgy, add a splash of water or milk.
Marinate: Coat the thinly sliced chicken in the batter and leave it for about 40 minutes.
Prep the veg: Cube the carrot, onion and peppers small (roughly the same size) and slice the mushrooms. Frozen mixed veg can be used instead.
Fry the chicken: Shallow-fry in a shimmering pan, turning, until it has colour and is cooked. It is a salty-flavoured batter rather than a crispy one. Drain on paper.
Start the sauce: Melt the butter and cook the carrots first, being hardest, then the peppers and onion (garlic is optional) for 2–3 minutes, with pepper.
Add mushrooms and flour: Add the mushrooms for about a minute for a little colour, then stir in the flour for a brief cook to take out the rawness, keeping it moving.
Add stock: Add the chicken stock (and bouillon if using), stirring in steadily, then turn the flame right down.
Add cream: Stir in the cream gently so it thickens into a full-bodied creamy sauce, and finish with a tablespoon of Marsala for richness.
Serve: Spoon sauce onto mashed potato, add the chicken, and spoon more sauce over the top. Thin with more cream, milk or water if you want it looser.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YKkpse7ZFds
Uploaded 2025-08-24.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: CHICKEN and ONIONS Stir fry
ingredients: Chicken breast, thinly sliced on an angle — 2 breasts (585 g / 21 oz)
Dark soy sauce — ¾ tsp (3.7 ml)
Green onion — 6 stalks, cut into 1-inch pieces (whites cooked with the aromatics, tops added at the end)
Dark soy sauce — 3¾ tsp (18 ml) (go steady, to avoid overpowering)
Unsalted chicken broth — ¾ cup (180 ml)
White (or black) pepper — ⅓ tsp (0.7 g)
steps: Prep: Cut the onions into big slices and pull the segments apart. Mince the garlic, slice or julienne the ginger and cut the green onions, keeping the leaf tops for later.
Marinate: Slice the chicken on an angle for long slices. Mix with the soy sauce, oyster sauce, dark soy, water, baking soda, sugar, white pepper and cornstarch, then add the sesame oil. Set aside.
Mix the sauce and slurry: Combine the rice wine, oyster sauce, sugar and dark soy for the sauce. Mix the cornstarch into the chicken broth for the slurry.

Stir-fry the onions: In a pan over medium heat with a little oil, quickly stir-fry the onions with a bit of salt and sugar, breaking up the segments, without getting much colour. Turn off the heat, put them in a bowl and cover with a lid so they steam, staying cooked but crunchy.
Cook aromatics and chicken: Add a little oil, then the ginger, garlic and green onion whites. Spread out the chicken and cook until about 80% done with a little colour, turning so none is raw.
Add sauce: Add the sauce mix and coat the chicken, then stir in the broth and cornstarch slurry to thicken.
Combine: Return the onions, add the green onion tops, stir through and finish with a shake of white pepper.
Serve: Serve over rice.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=H1AHbJRLiUs
Uploaded 2025-08-23.

recipes.title: CALIFORNIA Casserole 1970s NACHO Bake
ingredients: For a greased 9 × 13 inch (23 × 33 cm) baking dish.
Ground beef, cooked and crumbled — 500 g (1 lb)
Canned diced tomatoes (whole tomatoes cut in the tin with scissors, in the video) — 400 g (14 oz)
Canned kidney beans, drained — 400 g (14 oz) (any bean, or baked beans)
Tortilla chips (plain or lightly salted) — 150 g
Sour cream — 120 g (½ cup), sliced olives, jalapeños or spring onions
steps: Brown the beef: Cook the mince in a little oil, breaking it up, with salt and pepper and get a little colour on it. Salt only goes in at the start, as the tomatoes bring more.
Add onion and garlic: Add the onion for a minute or so until the rawness goes, then the garlic.
Bloom the spices: Add the chilli and cumin to bloom, plus the chopped jalapeños.
Add tomatoes and soup: Add the tomatoes and the condensed tomato soup (the 1970s way), then the kidney beans.
Simmer: Cook for a good 5 minutes to thicken and bring it together, leaving plenty of sauce.
Layer: In the 9 × 13 dish, layer tortilla chips (no need to crush them), then the meat mixture, then cheddar, and repeat for two layers, finishing with cheese on top.
Bake covered: Cover loosely with foil and bake at 180°C for about 20–25 minutes.
Bake uncovered: Remove the foil and bake another 10–15 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and golden.
Serve: Rest about 5–6 minutes, then scoop it out and dollop with sour cream and garnishes. It is also good cold with a salad. The host calls it a British chilli with nachos.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5bx7b_FbTM0
Uploaded 2025-08-22.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Cover with foil and bake at 180°C / 350°F for 20 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for an additional 10 minutes, until the cheese is bubbly and golden.

recipes.title: No Bake Chocolate Caramel Tarts – No Oven Required In Under an HOUR
ingredients: Makes about 6 tarts (the host used six tins or a silicone mould).
Digestive biscuits (or graham crackers), crushed — 200 g
Soft light brown sugar — 25 g (2 tbsp) (optional; more may be needed with graham crackers)
Salt — a pinch (as in the video)
Soft light brown sugar — 150 g (10 tbsp)
Golden syrup — 30 ml (2 tbsp) (optional; it still works without)
Sweetened condensed milk (not evaporated) — 200 g (14 tbsp)
steps: Crush the biscuits: Smash the biscuits (digestives, chocolate biscuits or graham crackers) to crumbs.
Make the base mix: Mix the crumbs with the melted butter and a pinch of salt until fully incorporated.
Line the tins: Press some of the mix into the bottom of each tin or silicone mould, then up the sides. Use any tin or size you like.
Chill the base: Refrigerate for about half an hour (the host says maybe as little as 15 minutes) so it sets enough to hold the filling.
Make the caramel: Gently melt the butter, sugar and golden syrup, add the sweetened condensed milk and simmer for about 5–7 minutes, stirring so it doesn't catch, until thickened. Turn off the heat.
Fill: Spoon the caramel into the bases, about three-quarters of the way up, and level.
Chill: Refrigerate to cool down completely.

Make the ganache (from the description): Heat the cream until steaming and pour it over the chopped chocolate. Leave for 1 minute, then stir smooth and stir in the butter for shine. Spoon or pipe it over the caramel layer and smooth the tops.
Set and serve: Chill for 30–40 minutes until set (description), then pop the tarts out. Add a little sea salt if you like.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EvOpPrkoOXw
Uploaded 2025-08-21.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Chill for 30–40 minutes until set.
Amounts weren't given for some ingredients; those are listed without a quantity.

recipes.title: Potato-Crust Creamy Tuna Sweetcorn Bake – No Egg - No Pastry!
ingredients: For a 9 × 9 inch / 23 cm square dish, or similar (the host used an 8-inch springform tin).
Mashed potatoes — 400 g (2½ cups; about 3 medium) (leftover mash is fine)
Raw potato, grated — 200 g (2 cups packed)
Milk — 1 tbsp (15 ml) (the host added none as his mash was wet enough)
Tuna in spring water or brine, drained — 2 × 160 g tins
Dijon mustard — ½ tsp (optional; the host used about a teaspoon)
Grated cheddar or mozzarella — 50 g (½ cup)
steps: Wring the raw potato: Grate the raw potato into a towel, then twist and squeeze out all the potato juice.
Make the crust mix: Mix the grated potato with the mashed potato, melted butter, salt and pepper by hand until fully incorporated (milk only if your mash is dry). Heat the oven to about 200°C.
Form the crust: Press into the tin, smoothing it up the sides to even thickness. This is the "pastry". Put the tin on a tray in case butter runs out.
Pre-bake: Bake the base for about 15 minutes (the host said 15–20) until it has firmed up and has a little colour.
Start the sauce: Melt butter and cook the onion with a pinch of salt and black pepper to cook out the rawness, without colouring.
Make the roux: Stir in the flour and cook it out, then add all the milk and stir until it thickens, adding the Dijon mustard (English mustard works too).
Add cheese: Turn off the heat and stir in the cheddar until it melts into a cheesy sauce.
Add sweetcorn and tuna: Stir in the sweetcorn, then fold in the tuna gently so you keep chunks.
Fill: Fill the baked crust right to the top, then add mozzarella and a little cheddar for colour (and breadcrumbs if you like).
Bake: Return to the oven at 200°C for about 20–25 minutes until golden and bubbling.
Serve: Serve hot after 10 minutes, or let it go completely cold and eat with salad. Chips are optional.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PZe-slvHVI8
Uploaded 2025-08-20.
Time and temperature tips from the video description: Base, Bake at 200°C / 180°C fan / 400°F for 15 minutes; Bake, Return to oven at 200°C / 180°C fan / 400°F for 20–25 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

recipes.title: Beef Shin & Potato Pie - Comfort Food Classic!
ingredients: Beef shin, boneless, diced — 1 kg (2.2 lb)
Plain flour — 2 tbsp (30 g) (optional dusting for the beef, per the video)
Fresh thyme — 1 tsp (or ½ tsp dried)
Ready-made shortcrust pastry — 400 g (about 1 standard pack)

Note: in the video the host instead makes a quick pastry (flour, salt, fats, water, apple cider vinegar, egg) with no quantities stated in the captions; a link to his pastry recipe is in the video description.
steps: Prep: Dice the onion, mince the garlic, dice the carrot and peel and dice the potatoes. Cube the shin into good chunks, as they shrink in the pressure cooker.
Season and sear: Season the beef with salt and pepper and sear in a hot pan until browned, then transfer it to the Instant Pot liner.
Cook the veg: Add a little more oil to the pan, cook the carrots for a minute, then the onions, with a little salt and pepper and the thyme.
Add flavour: Stir in the tomato paste and Worcestershire sauce, and loosen with a splash of the beef stock.
Potatoes: Drain the potatoes and stir them in for a couple of minutes.
Load the pot: Add everything to the Instant Pot with the rest of the beef stock (scrape up anything stuck) and the bay leaves.

Pressure cook: Pressure cook on High for 30 minutes (up to 40 for pull-apart beef), then natural release for 15 minutes before releasing the rest manually. Alternatives given: stove top about 3½ hours, or slow cooker 4–5 hours on high / 7–8 hours on low.
Prepare the pastry: Use ready-rolled shortcrust (or quick homemade), keeping some for the lid and some for the sides and base. Heat the oven to 200°C (180°C fan / 400°F / Gas 6).

Assemble: Roll the pastry to line a deep tin (about 8½ in loose-bottomed in the video), patch any breaks, fill with the filling, add the pastry lid, seal, cut a vent and brush with egg wash. Put it on a tray in case it leaks.
Bake: Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden brown, then rest 10 minutes before serving.
Serve: Serve with gravy, vegetables, chips, peas or mash.
recipes.notes:

recipes.title: BLOOMER - Traditional Classic British Bloomer at Home!
ingredients: Strong white bread flour — 500 g / 4 cups (UK) / 4 1⁄6 cups (US)
Instant yeast — 8 g / 2 ¾ tsp (about 60% of quick-rise amount)
Warm water (about 26–28 °C) — 700 ml / 1.23 UK pints / 2.96 US cups
Neutral or Olive oil — 30 ml / 2 tbsp / 27 g
steps: Mix the dough: Combine 500 g strong white bread flour and 500 g all-purpose/plain flour — or use all bread flour for more chew, or all plain flour for a softer crumb. Add the salt (20 g). Instant yeast (8 g) and the oil (30 ml / 2 tbsp) go in too; bakers often keep salt and yeast apart, though the host doesn't always bother. Add the warm water (700 ml, about 26–28°C).

Knead and first rise: Knead in a stand mixer about 8 minutes (the host also mentions 10). The dough can be quite tacky, especially in damp weather; flour your hands if you need to. Cover and leave about 1½ hours, until it has doubled.

Shape: Flour your hands, roll the dough up tightly, pinch the seam, and roll the ends down a little so you get the characteristic bloomer rise and tail. Sit it seam-side down on a lined baking tray as a long oval loaf.
Second rise: Cover with a bag or cloth. The description says about 45 minutes; the host also talks about covering it for about another hour. Meanwhile heat the oven to 220°C (200°C fan / 425°F).

Steam, slash and bake: Put a tray of water on a lower shelf so the loaf bakes above a bit of steam. Lightly dust the loaf with flour and slash it diagonally with a baker's lame, razor or a sharp knife. Bake 25–30 minutes until deep golden brown and it sounds hollow when tapped underneath. Serve with butter.

recipes.title: Quick & Easy Pickled Red Cabbage - NOT for me!
ingredients: 1 small red cabbage (about 600g / 1.3 lbs), thinly sliced
240 ml white vinegar (1 cup UK & US / 240g)
3 tbsp sugar (38g / 45 ml / 3 UK tbsp / 2 US tbsp)
Optional: 1 clove garlic, sliced or 1 tsp caraway seeds (3g) for flavour twist
Keeps in the fridge for up to 3 weeks.
steps: Salt the cabbage: Thinly slice a small red cabbage (about 600 g), toss it with the salt (1½ tsp / 9 g in the description — the host uses plain sea salt, not iodized) and leave it 30 minutes so it starts to release moisture.

Make the brine: While the cabbage stands, put the white vinegar, water, sugar, mustard seeds, black peppercorns, a bay leaf, and optional garlic or caraway seeds in a pan. Bring it to the boil to dissolve the sugar, then turn it off and let the brine cool right down — the host doesn't like pouring it on hot.

Rinse and pack: Rinse the cabbage clean and drain it in a colander about 10 minutes. Pack it tightly into sterilized jars (the host just scalds his with boiling water; this is a fridge pickle, not a long keep).

Cover and wait: Pour the cooled brine over so the cabbage is fully covered. It's ready to eat after 4 hours, but leave it 24 hours for a better pickle. It keeps in the fridge up to about 3 weeks. The mustard and peppercorns give a gentle warmth; the host is not a huge pickled-cabbage fan, but the method is straightforward.

recipes.title: EASY Pan Seared & Oven Finished WHITE FISH with CREAMY Tarragon Sauce
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper — ¼ tsp (1 g)
Fresh lemon juice — 1 tsp (5 ml), to drizzle before serving
Dry white wine — ½ cup (120 ml)
Fresh tarragon, finely chopped — 2 tbsp (6 g), plus extra for garnish
Fresh lemon juice — ½ tsp (3 ml)
Sea salt — a pinch, to taste
White pepper — a pinch, to taste (optional)
steps: Heat the oven: Put it on 200°C (400°F) and put a baking tray in to get hot — the fish will finish on that hot tray so the skin stays crisp.

Prep the fish: Pat the sea bass fillets dry (about 150–180 g each; the host's piece was about 300 g and the description is written for two smaller fillets). Oil them with olive oil, sea salt and black pepper.

Sear: Heat a pan with only a little extra oil if you need it — there is already oil on the fish. Sear skin-side down about 2–3 minutes until the skin is golden, pushing the oil towards the sides of the fish. Flip for about 30 seconds.

Finish in the oven: In those 30 seconds, take the hot tray out. Transfer the fish to the tray skin-side up (as the description says) and bake about 6 minutes, or 6–8 minutes in the captions (the description says 4–6 minutes for thin fillets or 6–8 for thicker ones) until the flesh is opaque and flakes, still with a soft centre.

Tarragon cream sauce: In the same pan, pour off extra fat if there is too much, then add about a tablespoon of butter to the remaining oil — don't brown the butter. Cook the finely chopped shallot for a little onion flavour. Add about 120 ml dry white wine and reduce it by half, then add about the same amount of cream. Stir in about a good teaspoon of Dijon mustard, a little salt and pepper (white pepper is optional in the description), the chopped fresh tarragon (the host wants a couple of tablespoons of chopped leaves; the description lists 2 tbsp / 6 g), and lemon juice if you are using it. Cook only until the sauce is slightly thickened — about 5 minutes. You are not looking for a thick sauce.
Serve: The description has a drizzle of lemon juice and optional lemon slices to garnish, with extra tarragon if you like.

recipes.title: One SECRET To PEKING Sauce - Stop Using Hoisin!
ingredients: ¼ cup (60 ml | 60 g | 4 tbsp UK/US) rice wine vinegar
2 tbsp (30 g | 30 ml) golden syrup, honey, brown sugar, or white sugar
½ tsp (2.5 ml | 2 g) sesame oil
2 tbsp (30 g) Tian Mian Jiang (sweet fermented wheat paste)
1 tbsp (15 ml | 15 g) dark soy sauce
Optional pinch of 5 spice ot grated ginger
steps: The key ingredient: Real Peking sauce needs Tian Mian Jiang (sweet fermented wheat paste), which is wheat-based. Without it, the host says you are just making a version of hoisin sauce.

Mix in a pan: Put in about ¼ cup rice wine vinegar, the sweetener (the host uses brown sugar; the description also allows golden syrup, honey or white sugar — 2 tbsp), Shaoxing wine (2 tbsp in the description), about ½ teaspoon sesame oil (it goes a long way and can overpower), two good tablespoons of Tian Mian Jiang, about a tablespoon of soy sauce and dark soy sauce, plus the oyster sauce, ketchup (80–100 ml) and water (100–125 ml) from the description. An optional pinch of five-spice or grated ginger is listed too.

Thicken: Stir in a heaped tablespoon of cornflour (cornstarch) straight into the pan — the host does not make a slurry. Mix, then heat steadily until it thickens, stirring so the sugars don't stick. If it goes too thick, splash in a little water.
Store: Use it as a dip or a coating for Peking duck, beef or chicken. The host says it lasts about 3 weeks in the fridge.

ingredients: Grated Parmesan cheese — ½ cup | 50 g
Olive oil or melted butter — 2 tbsp | 30 ml
Dijon mustard or and mayo — 2 tbsp | 30 ml (for coating)
Grated Parmesan (optional for finish) — 2 tbsp | 15 g
Chicken stock or broth — ¼ cup | 60 ml
Optional: pinch of nutmeg or squeeze of lemon juice for brightness
steps: Dress the broccoli and heat the oven: Toss the florets with a little olive oil, salt and pepper. Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F).

Crumb the chicken: Mix the panko, grated Parmesan, garlic powder, dried parsley, salt and pepper, and a little melted butter or olive oil. Stir together 1 tablespoon mayonnaise and 1 tablespoon Dijon mustard (the description also allows 2 tablespoons of either). Brush that over the chicken breasts, then press on the crumb.

Bake in two stages: Start the chicken on its own for 10 minutes. Take the tray out, arrange the broccoli around it, sprinkle a little extra Parmesan on the broccoli if you like, and return it to the oven about 20–25 minutes, until the chicken is golden and cooked through — 74°C / 165°F in the middle. The description gives a total bake of 25–35 minutes. Serve with mash, roast potatoes or carrots if you want.

Optional Parmesan cream sauce: While the tray is in the oven, melt a little butter over a steady, not high, flame and cook the minced garlic about 30 seconds just to take the rawness out. Add pepper — the host skips extra salt because a chicken stock cube and the Parmesan are already salty — then the chicken stock and as much cream as you want. Bring it back up gently, add a pinch of nutmeg if you like, then stir in the grated Parmesan so it thickens slightly, a little parsley, and a squeeze of lemon juice at the end.
recipes.notes:
From Backyard Chef on YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J_-9JXQOUPU

recipes.title: CREAMY Pesto CHICKEN with ROASTED Tomatoes and Bucatini
ingredients: 4 boneless, skinless chicken breasts (680–750 g | 24–26 oz)
¼ tsp ground black pepper (0.5 g | 1.25 ml)
½ cup heavy cream or cooking cream (120 ml)
⅓ cup basil pesto (80 g | 80 ml | approx. 5 tbsp + 1 tsp) How to make -
steps: Heat the oven: Put it on 200°C (390°F). Season the chicken breasts with a tiny bit of salt and pepper and a little olive oil, and get them into the oven first for about 10 minutes. The tomatoes roast more quickly.

Add the tomatoes: After about 10 minutes, add the halved cherry tomatoes with a little olive oil, a tiny bit of salt, pepper if you like, and the dried oregano from the description. The description says to roast uncovered 22–25 minutes in total, or until the chicken reaches 75°C (165°F) and the tomatoes are blistered. Near the end the host loosely gathers the chicken and covers the tray with foil while the sauce is made; take the tomatoes out if they are already done.
Cook the pasta: Boil the bucatini in salted water 8–10 minutes, until it is nearly done.

Pesto cream sauce: Over a gentle flame, not too high, warm the cream and stir in the basil pesto — the host uses about five tablespoons (the description lists ⅓ cup / about 5 tbsp + 1 tsp). Homemade or a jar is fine. Loosen with a little pasta water, then stir in grated Parmesan if you are using it, gently, and don't let the sauce get too thick.
Finish: Toss the bucatini in the sauce and serve with the roasted chicken and tomatoes, and fresh basil if you like. A tiny bit of extra pesto can go over the top.

recipes.title: Crispy Pork Schnitzel with Peppercorn Sauce
ingredients: ½ tsp freshly ground black pepper
2 tbsp green peppercorns in brine, drained and lightly crushed
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Prep the pork: Cut 4 boneless pork loin chops in half if you like and pound them out — if you leave them thick, the crumbs can burn before the pork cooks. Season the meat itself with salt and pepper, not just the flour.

Bread and rest: Coat in flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs, and squash on grated Parmesan if you want. Sit the breaded cutlets on a rack about 10 minutes so the pork juices are absorbed into the crumbs.
Fry: Heat the vegetable oil and fry until golden and crisp, with the heat going through the pork without burning the crumbs.

Peppercorn sauce: In butter, cook the finely chopped onion and the drained, lightly crushed green peppercorns. Add the brandy and cook 1–2 minutes to cook off the alcohol (shorter if you want a stronger brandy flavour), then add the chicken stock and let it reduce a little before you gently stir in the cream. Give it about 5 minutes; thicken it further if you want. Season to taste. Serve the schnitzel with the sauce, and mash, noodles or a salad.
