recipes.title: Moist OATMEAL GINGER Cake
ingredients: Rolled oats — 1 cup | 90 g | 16 tbsp | 240 ml hot water (to soak oats)
Chopped walnuts or pecans — ½ cup | 60 g
Crystallized ginger pieces — ¼ cup | 40 g, finely chopped
Brown sugar sprinkle — 2 tbsp | 30 g before baking
Cream cheese glaze or whipped cream, for serving
steps: Soak the oats: Pour the hot water over the rolled oats (1 cup / 90 g oats and 1 cup / 240 ml water in the description) and leave about 5 minutes (the host's batch had about 6).

Cream the butter and sugar: Heat the oven to about 180°C (350°F). Cream the softened butter with the brown sugar, then add a little vanilla and the eggs (one at a time if you prefer). The host tips in a little of the flour first to stop the eggs curdling.

Dry ingredients: Mix the remaining flour with the salt, baking soda (not baking powder), ground ginger and cinnamon, then stir it into the butter mixture. Dump in all of the soaked oat mixture and mix until combined. The host uses an 11 × 9 inch tray; a loaf tin is also mentioned in the description.

Top and bake: Optional walnuts, pecans, chopped crystallised ginger or a brown-sugar sprinkle are listed. On this cook the host just soaks a pinch of extra oats in a little water for about a minute and scatters them on top, without compressing the batter. Bake about 35–40 minutes, or 45–50 in a loaf tin, until a toothpick comes out clean — the host's shallower tray went in for about 30 minutes because it was small. Leave it in the tin about 10 minutes, then turn out to finish cooling.

Serve: Good with a cup of tea, whipped cream, ice cream, a cream-cheese glaze, or custard. The host makes a quick instant custard at the end; follow the packet or the video rather than inventing amounts.

recipes.title: If Nonna Made Meatloaf with Potatoes… It’d Be This!
ingredients: Potatoes (peeled and diced) — 900 g | 6 cups mashed
Italian bacon or pancetta (chopped) — 150 g | 6 slices
Italian sausage (casing removed) — 225 g | ½ lb
Cheddar or Italian blend cheese (shredded) — 100 g
Dried Italian mixed herbs — 2 tsp | 2 g
Fresh parsley (chopped, for garnish) — 8 g | 2 tbsp
Chopped tomatoes (canned or fresh) — 400 g | 14 oz
Dried Italian mixed herbs — 1 tsp | 1 g
Sugar — ½ tsp | 2 g (to balance acidity)
steps: Mash the potatoes: If you don't already have mash, peel, dice and cook about 900 g of potatoes and mash them. The host doesn't season the mash yet, so he knows what he's adding later. Butter the inside of a 900 g / 2 lb loaf tin so the sides will brown and crisp. Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F).

Cook the meats: Cook the chopped pancetta, Italian bacon or streaky bacon how you like it, then take it out. Cook the Italian sausage (casings removed) in the same pan until it has a little colour and crust, then cook the chopped onion and minced garlic a couple of minutes to take the rawness out, keeping that fat in the mix.

Mix the loaf: Combine the mash with the bacon, sausage, onion and garlic, shredded cheddar or an Italian-blend cheese, the beaten egg (that's the only raw ingredient — it binds), Italian herbs, salt and pepper to taste, and the butter from the list if you haven't already used it.
Bake: Pack it into the greased tin and bake 30–35 minutes until golden and firm. Rest 10 minutes before you turn it out and slice. Garnish with chopped parsley.

Quick tomato sauce: While it bakes or rests, cook the minced garlic in a little olive oil, add the chopped tomatoes, a good heaped tablespoon of tomato paste if you are using it, Italian herbs, optional sugar, and salt and pepper. Cook very gently about 10 minutes. Blend it smooth if you want. Serve with the loaf — or swap the tomato sauce for gravy if you prefer a more British sausage-and-bacon version.

recipes.title: EASY Churros – CLASSIC Recipe with CHOCOLATE Sauce
ingredients: Chocolate (dark or milk): 50g | 2 oz | 1.75 oz (UK cup) | ¼ US cup (chopped)
Water: 220 ml | slightly under 1 UK/US cup
Extra sugar and ground cinnamon (for dusting- Optional)
Heat oil in a deep pot to 180°C / 350°F.
Fry until golden brown (2–3 minutes per side)
steps: Start the dough: In a pan put the water, sugar and salt and heat, stirring, until the sugar and salt dissolve. Add the butter and bring it up to the boil.
Add the flour: Take it off or turn the flame low and beat in all the flour with a wooden spoon until it is fully incorporated. There is enough residual heat to finish the job.

Beat in the eggs: When the dough has cooled down — it doesn't have to be completely cold — beat in about half the beaten eggs, then the rest. A hand mixer helps. You want a thick but pipeable dough; if it is too stiff, beat in a little splash of water.
Rest: Cover and leave it somewhere cool about 30 minutes (the host says overnight or 4 hours gives more flavour).

Chocolate sauce: Mix cornflour with water — the host uses a couple of tablespoons; the description lists 1 tsp cornflour and 2 tsp water — to make a slurry. Heat the milk and sugar with a little salt, add the chopped chocolate (from the description) and the slurry, and heat, stirring, until you have a thick, glossy, slightly creamy dip, a little sweet and a little salty.

Fry: Heat enough oil to fry the churros to about 180°C / 350°F. Pipe the dough with a star nozzle (you can pipe onto parchment and lower it in). Fry until golden, 2–3 minutes per side according to the description. Drain, and coat in extra sugar and cinnamon if you want (optional, from the description). Serve with the chocolate sauce.

recipes.title: ALFREDO meets CARBONARA  becomes  LASAGNA -  Ultimate PARMESAN BACON Lasagna
ingredients: 50g / ½ cup Parmesan, grated (½ UK/US cup)

Whisk in the whole milk and heavy cream, bring it up to a simmer and let it thicken. Stir in the grated Parmesan, a little pepper, only a tiny bit of salt (the bacon is salty), and a pinch of nutmeg if you like.
Ricotta mix: Beat the ricotta with the egg and the chopped parsley from the description.

Layer: Heat the oven to about 190°C (375°F). The host uses about an 8×8 dish. Layer cooked lasagne noodles (or ready-to-use sheets — the host mentions some that cook in about 40 minutes), the ricotta mixture, the white sauce, the bacon, and the mozzarella and Parmesan. Repeat, finishing with sauce and cheese.
Bake: Cover with foil (oil it if you don't want it to stick) and bake 25 minutes, then uncover and bake another 10–15 minutes until golden and bubbly. Rest 10 minutes before cutting.

recipes.title: Juicy Chicken Meatballs in Rich Tomato Sauce – Better Than Beef?
ingredients: Milk — 60 ml (4 tbsp / ¼ UK cup / ¼ US cup)
Parmesan cheese, grated — 30g (2 tbsp / ¼ UK cup / ¼ US cup)
Onion, finely chopped — 100g (about 1 small / ⅔ UK cup / ½ US cup)
Crushed tomatoes — 400g (1 UK can / 1½ US cups)
Water — 100 ml (about 7 tbsp / ⅓ UK cup / ⅓ US cup)
Fresh basil or parsley (optional) — to garnish
steps: Mix the meatballs: Rehydrate the breadcrumbs in the milk first so the balls stay succulent, then mix with the ground chicken, egg, minced garlic, finely grated onion, grated Parmesan, chopped parsley, salt and pepper. Let the mix sit about 5–6 minutes, then roll into balls and set them on a tray. Bigger balls will take longer to cook.

Fry: Heat the olive oil and fry the meatballs to crisp and colour the outsides — give them a minute, then turn; they will finish in the sauce. They can be cooled and frozen at this stage, or shaped in the morning and cooked later.

Sauce: In a little more olive oil, cook the chopped onion and minced garlic about 3 minutes to take the rawness out. Stir in a couple of tablespoons of tomato paste and cook that out, then the crushed tomatoes, Italian seasoning, oregano, sugar, salt, pepper and the water (100 ml). Bring to a simmer.

Simmer and pasta: Add the meatballs, put a lid on and simmer about 10 minutes. In that time, boil the spaghetti in salted water until it is nearly done, then drain. When the meatballs have had a good 10 minutes, serve them and the sauce with the pasta, and garnish with basil or parsley if you like.

recipes.title: OLD School CHICKEN Mushroom & Sweetcorn COBBLER
ingredients: 250 g (7 oz) mushrooms, sliced minimum, I used about 400 g
150 ml (⅔ UK cup / ⅝ US cup) milk
150 g (1 UK cup / 1 US cup) sweetcorn (frozen or canned, drained)
200 g (1 ⅓ UK cups / 1 ⅔ US cups) self-raising flour
100 g (½ UK cup / ½ US cup) grated mature cheddar + extra on top (optional)
100 ml (⅓ UK cup + 1 tbsp / ⅓ US cup + 1 tbsp) milk (plus extra for brushing)
steps: Heat the oven and start the filling: Put the oven on 200°C. In the pan (the host uses about an 8 × 10 inch tin later) heat a couple of tablespoons of butter and about a tablespoon of oil. Cook the onion (and the garlic from the ingredient list) a couple of minutes to take the rawness out.

Cook the mushrooms: Add the sliced mushrooms. The description lists 250 g minimum; the host used about 400–450 g and says you only need about 300 g. Give them at least 7 minutes, with a little salt and black pepper. They will finish in the oven.

Thicken: Stir in a good couple of heaped tablespoons of flour and cook it off. Season, then add about a teaspoon of Dijon mustard. Loosen with some of the chicken stock (and the milk from the description) so the flour doesn't go lumpy, and give it a minute to come together. Add the shredded cooked chicken and the sweetcorn (parsley or thyme if you are using them).

Make the cobbler dough: In a bowl mix self-raising flour, a little salt, thyme if you are using it, and cold diced butter, then add milk to make a dough. The description also adds grated mature cheddar in the topping, with extra for the top.

Top and bake: Pat or roll the dough gently — don't roll it thin; cracks don't matter. Cut rounds (the host says they're a bit like American biscuits) and sit them on the filling. Brush with a little milk for a golden, crispy top and add a little extra cheese if you like. Bake 25 minutes (the description says 25–30 minutes at 200°C / 180°C fan / 400°F) until the top is golden and the filling is bubbling.
Serve: Lift the cobbles so you can get at the creamy chicken, mushroom and sweetcorn underneath, and serve with vegetables if you like.

recipes.title: Beef Shawarma - Easy, fatty, lean, and everything in between!
ingredients: 1.5–2 kg beef off-cuts, cubed or chunky (include some fat for flavour)
1 large onion, grated or finely chopped
Optional: pinch of cinnamon or chilli flakes if you want more depth or heat
Pressure Cook (Instant Pot) on High for 70–80 minutes, depending on the size and toughness of the meat.
steps: Marinate the beef: Use 1.5–2 kg beef off-cuts, cubed or in chunks, with some fat left on for flavour. Grate a large onion (you want the juice as well) and mix it through the meat with the minced garlic, about a teaspoon of salt, black pepper, about a tablespoon of olive oil, three good tablespoons of baharat, and some yogurt (the description also lists 2 tbsp lemon juice, and vinegar as an alternative tenderiser — lemon juice is clearly used later in a garlic mayo, so don't invent a marinade amount if you don't see it go in). Optional chilli flakes or a pinch of cinnamon are listed too. Mix thoroughly, with gloves if you like, then bag or cover it and leave it to marinate (the captions cut off before a time is given — watch the video rather than inventing one).

Pressure-cook: The host uses an Instant Pot with a trivet and about 1½ cups of water so the meat steams under pressure. Roll and pack the meat in butcher's net, or roll and tie it with string. Pressure-cook on high 70–80 minutes depending on the size and toughness (the host does 70 minutes / an hour and 10), then natural release 10 minutes before you vent.

Crisp in the oven: Heat the oven to 220°C / 425°F. Put the meat on a spit if you have one, or roast it in a tray, so the edges go crispy while the inside stays soft and almost like pulled beef. The description says 15–20 minutes; the host talks about about 10 minutes at the top of the oven — watch it rather than inventing a finish time. You can cut the string off first if you wish. It also reheats and browns well from frozen.
Serve: The host puts it with a quick garlic mayo (garlic, mayo, a little salt, and just a squeeze of lemon) and a simple salad such as shredded iceberg.
